candidates.title: Embodying the victim: Virtual embodiment equalizes gender responses to simulated domestic violence
candidates.abstract: Virtual embodiment (i.e. the first-person experience of inhabiting a virtual body) has been shown to modulate emotional and cognitive responses across diverse social contexts. In the domain of domestic violence, virtual reality (VR) offers a promising tool for fostering awareness of and sensitivity to aggressive behavior. Yet any VR-based intervention relying on shared experiential ground across genders must first establish cross-gender equivalence, regardless of whether VR is ultimately the optimal delivery platform. To address this requirement, we embodied 40 participants (20 male, 20 female) in a female avatar and exposed them to a VR domestic violence scenario featuring escalating verbal and physical aggression. We measured physiological responses (electrodermal activity, EDA), behavioral performance (Onset Time), and self-reported experiences (presence, embodiment, empathy), supplemented by post-experience verbal reports. Cross-gender equivalence was evaluated using a Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) procedure. Across physiological, behavioral, and subjective measures, male and female participants responded equivalently: EDA modulation was comparable across scenario phases, distress-threshold reaction times were statistically equivalent, and ratings of presence and embodiment did not differ meaningfully between groups. Of 33 binary verbal indicators, 30 (91%) fell within the equivalence margin. The three non-equivalent indicators were interpretive in nature: males more frequently reported guilt and submission, and tended to identify the onset of violence only upon physical aggression, whereas females recognized it during earlier verbal escalation. Within-gender EDA coupling further distinguished the groups – in males, physiological arousal co-varied with feelings of submission; in females, it co-varied with discomfort and perceived violation. These findings demonstrate that virtual embodiment substantially aligns male and female responses to simulated domestic violence, supporting its potential as a standardized tool for prevention and rehabilitation programs targeting gender-based violence.

candidates.title: Value dimensions shaping digital healthcare adoption: a conceptual review with implications for BRICS countries
candidates.abstract: Digital healthcare has revolutionized the way we see modern healthcare delivery bringing a massive shift from hospitals to home. However, recent literature points towards a scattered understanding of the concept. Thereby, this study analyses the literature around digital healthcare adoption to broaden the scope and their consumption value drivers. It explores the core consumption values through which digital healthcare gets augmented for their impact on preventive and promotive healthcare utilising bibliometric and content analysis methodologies with the theoretical base of the Theory of Consumption Values. The contribution of the study includes: classifying Digital healthcare research into paradigms, offering a conceptual framework, and exploring how consumption values may shape the user attitude, intention, and sustainable utilization of the futuristic wellness landscape. The framework brings together five value dimensions—functional, social, emotional, conditional, and epistemic—and organizes the reviewed literature into eight thematic categories. For BRICS health systems, the discussion considers affordability, infrastructure, clinical workflow integration, digital health literacy, and cultural adaptation. These implications are conceptual propositions rather than findings from a comparative cross-national study. The proposed relationships require empirical validation, particularly regarding sustained use and their applicability across healthcare settings. The findings hold implications for researchers, healthcare businesses, providers, and policymakers proposing possibilities for research exploration.

candidates.title: Anthropomorphism and risk perception: The role of trust and domain knowledge in decision-support AI
candidates.abstract: Anthropomorphic design is increasingly used to make conversational AI systems more approachable and socially engaging, yet its effects on users’ risk judgments remain unclear. Drawing on theories of anthropomorphism and cognitive–affective trust, we develop a moderated mediation model explaining how perceived anthropomorphism relates to risk perception in AI decision support. We conducted a large-scale between-subjects online experiment (N = 1,256) using a simulated financial advisor chatbot with a 2 2 2 anthropomorphic design manipulation varying visual cues (human vs. machine avatar), identity cues (human name vs. bot identifier), and communication style (human-like vs. machine-like communication). Results show that perceived anthropomorphism was positively associated with both cognitive trust and affective trust, but these trust dimensions had different relationships with perceived risk. Cognitive trust consistently predicted lower risk perception, whereas affective trust showed a weaker positive association with risk perception that was not robust across model specifications. Self-reported domain knowledge moderated these relationships: higher domain knowledge attenuated the association between perceived anthropomorphism and both trust dimensions, while participants with lower domain knowledge showed a stronger negative indirect association between anthropomorphism and risk perception through cognitive trust. By treating the perceived risk of following AI advice as a focal outcome, this study extends anthropomorphism research beyond trust formation and distinguishes how cognitive and affective trust relate to users’ risk judgments. The findings highlight the importance of calibrating, rather than simply maximizing, anthropomorphic cues in high-stakes AI decision-support systems.

candidates.title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration
candidates.abstract: AI-enabled remote patient monitoring is evolving beyond passive data collection toward agentic AI systems that interpret patient states, coordinate care, and initiate action across domestic and clinical settings. This structured scoping review finds that mature agentic care has not yet emerged: Most systems remain human led, while stronger decision-action coupling and embodied AI remain largely confined to prototypes and pilots. Healthcare robotics makes the transition from monitoring to action especially visible by translating AI-generated recommendations and decisions into speech, movement, prompting, physical assistance, escalation, and care coordination, making embodiment, clinical integration, human oversight, and governance fundamental design requirements. Further progress requires safe and interoperable care architectures in which intelligent components operate through clinically validated and accountable workflows. We propose agentic robotics as a future direction for supervised systems embedded in the care ecosystem, connecting AI agents and robots with clinicians, caregivers, and patients through auditable workflows that can be interrupted and remain subject to human oversight and explicit AI governance.

candidates.title: Gaze semantics: A scoping review of how gaze conveys and constrains meaning in social contexts
candidates.abstract: Humans rely on gaze to encode information and signal to others. Gaze may indicate where someone is attending, but its contribution extends beyond spatial orientation. Evidence is scattered across different research traditions. This scoping review synthesizes 361 publications on gaze as a meaningful social cue. Gaze semantics describes the systematic contribution of gaze to conveying and constraining social meaning. A cross-domain synthesis identified four recurrent operations: gaze orients by making objects, people or locations socially relevant; addresses by positioning people as recipients or interaction partners; qualifies by modifying how other cues are interpreted; and coordinates by organizing participation and unfolding action. These functional contributions can co-occur within a single gaze event. Gaze interpretation is inferential, shaped by five categories of contextual factors: signal properties; interactional availability; multimodal and sequential embedding; cultural, social and activity frame; and gazer and observer states and interactional history. We propose a Gazer-Observer Model of Gaze Understanding that integrates these findings to describe the dynamic relation between gaze production and interpretation. The same gaze pattern may support different interpretations across situations yet allow a relatively specific interpretation within a particular encounter. Gaze can therefore systematically affect social interpretation while remaining semantically underdetermined to varying degrees.

candidates.title: Evaluating human-like chatbot interaction in customer service: integrating anthropomorphism and conversational capability
candidates.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI)-based technology has driven the development of rule-based chatbots into AI-based chatbots. This development is used by various companies to use AI chatbots as the frontline of customer service. Meeting user expectations for AI chatbots requires an evaluation model to measure chatbot quality. Based on the literature, chatbot evaluation models still focus solely on technical quality, even as AI chatbots are evolving towards human-like services. This research will explore the integration of the technical dimensions of information system success with a new dimension, namely Human-Like Chatbot Interaction (HLCI) as a higher-order construct of anthropomorphism and conversational capability. This quantitative study uses an explanatory research approach. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of users of the Veronika chatbot, owned by Telkomsel, an Indonesian telecommunications company. A total of 213 respondents had data ready for analysis using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method in SmartPLS 4, namely the measurement model and structural model tests. The analysis results show that service quality is not significantly related to user satisfaction but has a direct effect on trust. Meanwhile, information quality, system quality, and human-like chatbot interaction are positively related to trust and user satisfaction. Trust and user satisfaction are positively related to intention to continue using. The results of this study can contribute both theoretically and practically to modern AI chatbot quality evaluation models.

candidates.title: The Economic Sustainability of Intangible Cultural Heritage in the Platform Age With Global Evidence and Implications for Xinjiang
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Digital platforms lower market access costs for intangible cultural heritage but can concentrate visibility, weaken community control, and disconnect revenue from cultural reproduction. This global survey integrates platform and cultural economics with research on authenticity, intellectual property, and heritage governance. Its Platform Frictions, Cultural Rents, and Intergenerational Reproduction framework distinguishes living practices from their commercial products, recordings, and experiences. Economic sustainability requires four minimum conditions that cannot substitute for one another. These comprise adequate net market access, viable cultural reproduction, a sufficient practitioner value share, and meaningful community control. The framework distinguishes these conditions from the mechanisms through which platforms affect them. Rankings, provenance labels, copyright, and certification can improve discovery and bargaining while concentrating demand, excluding legitimate variants, or burdening small producers. Community authorization requires representation, reviewable delegation, and effective appeal. Distributional assessment separates individual earnings, collective transfers, unpaid contributions, and investment in transmission. Applications to Xinjiang differentiate crafts, performances, foodways, and community events by economic object and institutional responsibility. Longitudinal indicators of apprentice retention, repertoire in use, and contextual participation distinguish authorized adaptation from commercial hollowing. Platform growth sustains living heritage when returns support practitioners, learning, and community authority.

candidates.title: Data-driven fandom culture: exploring parasocial interactions between digital fan labor and traffic stars using interaction ritual chains theory
candidates.abstract: Traffic stars and digital fan labor become a widespread phenomenon in China. Digital fan labor refers to the use of tools and data-driven social media strategies to interact with their favorite stars, organize events, measure popularity, and influence the popularity; such stars are referred to as traffic stars. While existing research has largely focused on the characteristics and motivations of digital fan labor in participating in fan activities, few studies have examined the factors influencing their interactive rituals with other fans and parasocial interactions with their celebrities. Parasocial interactions between traffic stars and digital fan labor refer to fans establishing emotional connections with celebrities through participation in fan activities, while celebrities, in turn, strengthen fan engagement through actions such as commenting and liking posts. At this point, Interaction Ritual Chains Theory provides a theoretical framework for the assessment of the importance of collective effervescence and the shared emotional intensity experienced during group rituals in virtual spaces. Therefore, this study uses factors drawn from interaction ritual chains theory to explore the parasocial interaction between so-called ‘traffic stars’ and the digital fan labor they attract within data-driven fandom communities. The sampling strategy was using snowball sampling of a purposive group, and 329 Chinese fans aged between 18 and 42 years old were selected. SPSS version 26.0 was used to obtain descriptive statistics, t-test, mediation effects and moderation effects, and AMOS version 24.0 was used to investigate the result of correlation analysis. The resulting indicated that virtual experience, sense of community, mutual focus of attention, and shared mood all are all associated to the interactive ritual of digital fan labor. This study also found that interactive ritual outcomes play a mediating role between interactive ritual elements and parasocial interactions, especially having different mediating effects with subgroups. However, personal norms did not have a moderating role regarding ritual ingredients affecting interactive ritual outcomes and parasocial interaction. Consequently, this study identified a noteworthy phenomenon: the parasocial interaction between traffic stars and digital fan labor involving a higher level of interactive rituals arises from a hybrid pattern of online actions that develops in a particular environment.

candidates.title: From Emotional Impulse to Recurring Revenue: Consumer Psychology, Unit Economics, and VC Investment Evaluation of AI Companion Hardware for Gen Z
candidates.abstract: With the rapid convergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) and embodied intelligence, AI companion hardware targeted at Generation Z (e.g., desktop AI pets and smart emotional robots) has emerged as a premier track for venture capital (VC) investment. However, these conceptual devices frequently face severe Unit Economics crises characterized by high customer acquisition costs (CAC), elevated initial product returns, and steep user churn rates. This paper examines the psychological drivers behind Gen Z's willingness to pay (WTP) high emotional premiums for feature-incomplete AI hardware, and investigates how hardware enterprises can leverage proactive retention mechanisms to optimize LTV/CAC ratios and valuation multiples . This paper conducts a literature review that synthesizes theoretical frameworks from behavioral finance, consumer psychology, human-computer interaction (HCI), and venture capital valuation models. The study reveals that Gen Z's demand for loneliness compensation and social status validation provides firms with strong initial pricing power and gross margins. However, sustaining long-term commercial viability requires overcoming the "novelty decay trap" through proactive AgentOS interactions and dynamic memory graphs. Transforming hardware from a one-off transaction into an Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) subscription model substantially improves capital efficiency, expanding valuation multiples from 1.0x–2.0x P/S to 8.0x–12.0x P/S.

candidates.title: Voice-Native LLMs Hear Frustration but Do Not Listen to It
candidates.abstract: Users convey frustration in what they say and in how they say it, and voice-native models, which hear speech instead of an ASR transcript, can register both. Existing evaluations read unchanged performance as robustness without checking perception. Following Brunswik's lens model, we measure on identical audio whether frustration is expressed, perceived, and utilized. We cross frustrated wording with frustrated voice in a within-item 2x2 design over 353 tasks and release the 1,412 clips as VoxAffect. Across 8 models, outputs look robust, with no detectable vocal effect on accuracy for 7. With neutral wording, all 8 label the frustrated voice frustrated in at most 3.1% of clips, although 7 of them detect acted anger in 73-100% of clips and human listeners classify the voice correctly in 65.3% of judgments. Yet linear probes decode the frustrated voice from the audio encoders of the 2 open-weight models, with paired accuracy 0.67 and 0.69, and in proprietary models too the voice raises perceived frustration once the words agree. The models thus hear the frustrated voice but do not listen to it, whereas their invariance to frustrated wording, perceived in 40-75% of clips, is genuine robustness. Our work is openly accessible at https://github.com/Astarojth/hear-not-listen.

candidates.title: BRIDGING AUTOMATION AND ROBOTICS IN INDUSTRIALIZED BUILDING SYSTEM (IBS): CHALLENGES, IMPACTS, AND STRATEGIES OF ADOPTIONS
candidates.abstract: The Industrialised Building System (IBS) was introduced in Malaysia in the early 1960s to address the growing demand for affordable housing, reduce reliance on foreign labour, and enhance the overall quality and productivity of the construction sector. Recently, the construction industry has begun integrating automation and robotics, aligning with the global shift towards the Fourth Industrial Revolution (IR 4.0). The Construction 4.0 Strategic Plan (2021–2025) further emphasises digitalisation, robotics, and automation to improve industry efficiency and sustainability. However, the construction industry has been slow to adopt these advancements, limiting the full benefits of automation in IBS. Persistent challenges, including resistance to change, high initial investment costs, a shortage of skilled personnel, and technical complexities, hinder widespread adoption. This research examines the integration of automation and robotics in IBS to enhance construction productivity. A questionnaire survey was used for the data collection exercise. The data collected were analysed using descriptive statistical methods utilising the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) software. The study is guided by three (3) objectives: (1) To identify barriers to the integration of automation and robotics in IBS, (2) To analyse the impact of automation and robotics on construction productivity compared to conventional IBS, and (3)To propose strategies to improve the adoption of these technologies.Findings reveal that the integration of automation and robotics in (IBS) facessignificant barriers, primarily due to the high costs of investment. candidates.title: MESSPa: A Multi-modal Embodiment Stimulation Shoulder Pad for Preserving the Sense of Agency in a Detachable Robotic Arm
candidates.abstract: Wearable robots such as supernumerary robotic limbs (SRLs) can augment human capability, but their effectiveness depends strongly on the operator's sense of embodiment, comprising the sense of agency (SoA) and the sense of ownership (SoO). When an SRL is detached from the body so that the operator can act in two places at once, both the sense of agency and task performance tend to degrade. This paper presents the Multi-modal Embodiment Stimulation Shoulder Pad (MESSPa), a wearable interface that combines one-to-one motion transfer with spatially distributed pneumatic (balloon) haptic feedback on the shoulder, with the goal of preserving the sense of agency across attached and detached states. We describe the system design, the control mapping, and a controlled experiment using a $2\times2$ mixed design that crosses the control interface between groups (MESSPa, $N=13$, vs. keyboard control, $N=12$ from our previous study) and attachment (on-shoulder/detached) within participants, under single- and dual-task loads. Compared with keyboard control in the detached condition, MESSPa significantly reduced task completion time and significantly improved the sense of agency in the detached state, while narrowing the performance gap between the attached and detached conditions. The sense of ownership did not change significantly. These results indicate that combining motion transfer with positional haptic feedback is an effective way to recover agency when a robotic limb is operated remotely.

candidates.title: Create, Innovate, Play and Explore: Opportunities for Formal and Informal Teaching and Learning in Makerspaces in Ireland
candidates.abstract: The Maker Movement has gained in popularity over the last decade, allowing people of all ages and with varying skills and abilities to come together in order to create and explore in areas such as art, science, and engineering. To facilitate this movement, for profit companies, non-profits, and educational institutions run makerspaces. This qualitative study set out to examine the benefits of makerspace adoption in higher education in Ireland, with particular attention to their pedagogical value. The authors sought to identify opportunities for teaching and learning and the development of rich, diverse, and inclusive educational environments, as well as the potential to develop a maker network linking tertiary makerspaces with the wider community. Nine administrators from diverse types of makerspaces participated in interviews where they described the impacts and observed effects of makerspaces on participant learning experiences. Findings indicate that makerspaces support self-directed and peer learning, foster inclusive learning communities characterised by skill-sharing and mentorship, and provide safe environments for experimentation and productive failure. In doing so, makerspaces support learning dispositions such as agency, resilience, and self-efficacy, which are increasingly recognised as critical to student learning, persistence, and adaptability in contemporary higher education. Participants also perceived positive impacts on mental health, an area that remains under-researched in tertiary makerspaces. Finally, interviewees advocated for the development of a maker network in Ireland, suggesting that such a network could facilitate the sharing of skills and resources and strengthen access to larger-scale funding.

candidates.title: R-Metaverse: multimodal social cues for real-world-centered telepresence–MR collaboration with telepresence robots
candidates.abstract: Remote collaboration in live physical workspaces requires direct access to the evolving scene and shared task information anchored to it. Telepresence provides embodied access but lacks a shared spatial interaction layer, whereas fully virtual collaboration requires reconstructing the workspace. R-Metaverse (Ritsumei Real-World Robotic Metaverse) is a telepresence–MR system design centered on the physical workspace. A remote participant operates a telepresence robot and views its camera image augmented with virtual objects through a head-mounted display (HMD), while an on-site participant views the same spatially registered virtual objects through a smartphone. The robot–mobile configuration creates viewpoint and embodiment asymmetries that can reduce social presence. Robot–robot collaboration makes partner distance and approach difficult to perceive because of robot-camera field-of-view limitations. To restore missing cues, we implement facial-expression display, motion-synchronized avatar overlay, spatially localized audio, and distance-linked vibrotactile feedback. The first three target robot–mobile collaboration; the fourth targets robot–robot collaboration. Ablation experiments show that facial-expression display improves affect understanding and closeness, while distance-linked vibrotactile feedback supports co-presence and spatial awareness under field-of-view constraints. Avatar, audio, and vibration-pattern effects are interpreted as exploratory after Holm correction. These results suggest that gap-specific multimodal cues can partially compensate for reduced social presence in real-world-centered telepresence–MR collaboration.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence Anthropomorphism and Emotional Affiliation Needs among Young Adults
candidates.abstract: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into interpersonal communication has transformed the dynamics of emotional relationships between humans and digital technologies. This study examines the relationship between AI anthropomorphism and emotional affiliation needs among young adults, focusing on perceived social presence, emotional attachment, and AI-mediated companionship. Employing a qualitative library research approach, the study thematically synthesizes 35 scholarly publications published between 2018 and 2026. The findings suggest that humanlike communication, personalized responses, and perceived emotional responsiveness may strengthen social presence and facilitate emotional attachment. Such interactions may provide perceived emotional support, particularly for individuals experiencing loneliness or unmet affiliation needs. However, intensive emotional engagement may also contribute to dependence, unrealistic relational expectations, and psychological vulnerability following the disruption of AI companionship. This study develops a conceptual synthesis integrating anthropomorphism, social presence, emotional attachment, and affiliation needs to explain the dynamics of human–AI emotional relationships. Further empirical investigation is needed to validate this framework among young adults.

candidates.title: LabMaker: Conectando educação, inovação e impacto social por meio da cultura Maker
candidates.abstract: Maker culture has been established as a strategy to promote active learning, innovation, and social impact, contributing to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), especially SDGs 4, 10, and 12. In this context, this paper presents a set of actions developed by the extension project Labmaker, a multidisciplinary laboratory that integrates education, accessibility, healthcare, and sustainability through Maker culture, additive manufacturing, and Web technologies and platforms. The actions presented include training activities in robotics, programming, and 3D modeling, the development of assistive technologies and solutions for the healthcare sector, the promotion of circular economy initiatives focused on 3D printing, and the use of digital media and Web platforms to expand the project’s reach and interaction with the community. The results of these actions demonstrate the project’s potential to democratize access to technologies, strengthen the relationship between the university and society, promote hands-on learning, and contribute to the development of innovative solutions aligned with the SDGs.

candidates.title: Baby-schema-related cues shape moral expectations about decision-makers: evidence from names, faces, and AI avatars
candidates.abstract: People routinely form expectations about how others will behave in morally difficult situations, and such expectations guide consequential decisions, including whom to trust, hire, or delegate responsibility to. The present research examined whether baby-schema-related cues systematically bias these moral predictions. Across three experiments with Chinese university students (total N = 858), we tested three manifestations of baby-schema-related cues that share the function of evoking infant-like associations: repeated two-syllable names (Experiment 1), babyfaced appearance (Experiment 2), and visually cute artificial intelligence (AI) avatar designs (Experiment 3). Participants consistently perceived decision-makers displaying baby-schema-related cues as less likely to make utilitarian choices involving direct harm to others. The results show that superficially irrelevant social cues can bias moral expectations about others, although the underlying psychological mechanism remains to be clarified. These findings are relevant to moral psychology, person perception, and the design and evaluation of AI systems.

candidates.title: AI vs. AI: An AI-Enabled Conversational Intervention to Inoculate Against AI-Generated Fake News
candidates.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is a double-edged sword that can be used to amplify the proliferation of highly sophisticated fake news as well as to fight it. In this work, we explore a new route: using one AI to inoculate humans against fake news generated by another AI. Motivated by psychological inoculation theory, we created ‘Alex’, a conversational AI agent that engages users in an adaptive conversational dialogue designed to build cognitive resilience against AI-generated, AI-related fake news. We tested its efficacy in a Solomon four-group experiment with 542 participants. The results of a 2 × 2 ANOVA show a significant main effect of the intervention on participants’ discrimination of true and false headlines, with no significant evidence of pretest sensitization. We show that AI can be designed as a scalable, interactive conversational intervention for delivering psychological inoculation against AI-generated, AI-related fake news.

candidates.title: Virtual idol consumption among Generation Z: exploring fandom motivations, engagement behavior, and marketing implications
candidates.abstract: Virtual idols have rapidly gained worldwide popularity among young people and have become a significant marketing tool for promoting brands and expanding market reach. Grounded in Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this study conducted in-depth interviews to explore motivations, engagement behavior, and consumption patterns underlying Generation Z’s virtual idol fandom. The findings reveal that virtual idol fandom is shaped by both intrinsic and attribute-driven motivations. Within the fandom, engagement with and consumption of virtual idols are driven by overlapping motivational pathways combining emotional involvement, relational control, technology fascination, and community participation. Where community participation is involved, virtual idol fandom extends beyond individual engagement into a socio-technical ecosystem shaped by user agency, platform affordances, and regulatory oversight. At the same time, virtual idol fans seek emotional involvement while pursuing a ‘secure distance’ that preserves psychological boundaries and relational control. This study develops an SDT-informed interpretive framework that reconfigures diverse motivations within contemporary virtual idol fandom. By mapping distinct fan-as-consumer profiles, this study offers practical implications for the scalability of digital persona-led industries and insights for brands seeking to leverage the visibility and influence of virtual idols for targeted promotion among young consumers, enhanced brand value creation, and sustainable expansion in global markets.

candidates.title: A Survey on AI-Based Household Robots Focusing on Voice Assistance, Smart Kitchen Support, Home Monitoring and Autonomous Navigation
candidates.abstract: The proposed system places a Raspberry Pi at the centre, connected to a microphone, speaker, display, camera, ultrasonic sensors, a motor driver and a wheeled base. A conversational AI layer interprets natural-language requests, while obstacle detection, emergency stop and motor time-outs are kept in local safety logic outside the AI loop. Design considerations, a proposed function-to-module mapping, safety logic and an evaluation plan are presented.

candidates.title: Bespoke Visual Assistance: What and How do Blind and Low-Vision People Create with Agentic Programming?
candidates.abstract: AI-powered assistive technologies have long supported blind and low vision (BLV) people in everyday tasks, but they are general-purpose and often fall short of meeting complex, individualized, in-situ accessibility needs. Though agentic programming tools, like GitHub Copilot, have the potential to bridge this gap by lowering the technical barriers to building personal AT using natural language, the practical applicability of this creation paradigm has been unknown. We address this knowledge gap through a two-phase longitudinal co-design study with five tech-savvy BLV users using ProgramAT, an agentic programming tool that supports the creation, iteration, and testing of camera-based AT. Overall, co-designers created over 37 tools, with some addressing needs unmet by any existing commercial AT—such as identifying Uber rides or interpreting hand gestures. Qualitative feedback from our co-designers and analysis of development logs surface BLV strategies for tool creation, along with key challenges including model capability limits, specification conflicts, and barriers to successful creation. We discuss recommendations to provide appropriate conversational scaffolding, community tool sharing capabilities, and support for specialized models and personal datasets for future agentic programming environments to empower BLV users to create bespoke visual assistance for themselves.

candidates.title: Fan identity, power shifts, and ownership change: a conceptual analysis of foreign investment in European football
candidates.abstract: Foreign investment has become a defining feature of contemporary European football, reshaping not only club governance but also the cultural identities and social relationships embedded within fan communities. Drawing on a theory-driven conceptual analysis informed by a thematic review of the literature on foreign club ownership (2008-2025), this article examines how foreign ownership alters fan meaning-making, symbolic interaction, and club–community bonds through interactionist, critical, and figurational sociological perspectives. Interactionist theory is used to analyze how supporters construct identity through shared rituals, symbols, and communal practices, and how these processes are disrupted when ownership shifts toward actors with limited local presence or conflicting cultural logics. Critical theory highlights how global capital and geopolitical interests reconfigure power relations, normalizing ideological influence and diminishing the capacity of supporters to shape the cultural direction of their clubs. Figurational theory situates these developments within long-term processes of commodification, commercialization, and de-amateurization, emphasizing evolving interdependencies between clubs, supporters, markets, states, and investors. The analysis demonstrates that foreign ownership often displaces established identity markers, erodes symbolic interactions, and produces forms of fan alienation, especially under absentee or politically motivated owners. In response, supporters negotiate belonging through protest, collective action, accommodation, or the construction of hybrid identities that reconcile local traditions with increasingly commodified football cultures. The article argues commodification restructures interdependencies, redistributes symbolic and institutional power, and reshapes the ways supporters construct and negotiate identity. By integrating interactionist, critical, and figurational perspectives, the study demonstrates how emotional attachment, resistance, and adaptation become embedded within an increasingly globalized football economy.

candidates.title: A sociolinguistic analysis of automatic speech recognition bias in Newcastle English
The social self: integration of multimodal communication signals in dyadic interactions
candidates.abstract: Humans are in continuous exchange with other persons, thereby integrating the individual self and the social self. This requires the production of different verbal and nonverbal signals at the subpersonal level (individual self) and, at the same time, their coordination with various perceived signals at the interpersonal level (social self). Many of our communicative signals are conveyed substantially nonverbally-that is automatically, intuitively and effortlessly, requiring dynamic coordination over time ('chronemics'). Whereas successful communication is usually perceived as pleasant and satisfying, communication can also be experienced as disrupted if chronemics do not unfold properly. With respect to the particularly informative example of autism spectrum disorder, we propose the concept of 'double invisibility'. Non-autistic persons intuitively produce and expect a rich, multimodal stream of communication signals without being aware of it (first invisibility). By contrast, autistic persons produce and expect nonverbal cues either to a significantly lesser extent or not at all without being aware of it (second invisibility). This mismatch leads to misunderstandings and disturbed communication. The coordination within the dyad that is continuously constructed through real-time communication is crucial to understand the full complexity of multimodal interactions and their disturbances. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue 'From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self'.

candidates.title: Adaptive Motion Scaling With Phase‐and‐Gaze Awareness for Laparoscopic Robotic Teleoperation
candidates.abstract: Teleoperated surgical robots commonly employ a small fixed motion scaling factor to improve precision and suppress hand tremor. However, in laparoscopic teleoperation, this configuration limits the effective workspace on the slave side and necessitates frequent clutching during large‐range motions, thereby diverting the operator's attention and increasing cognitive workload. To address this, this article proposes a phase‐ and gaze‐aware adaptive motion scaling framework for laparoscopic robotic teleoperation, integrating real‐time surgical phase recognition, fusion of robot kinematics and eye‐tracking features, and personalized parameter tuning based on Bayesian optimization. The inferred phase probabilities and dominance weights are used to suppress unnecessary scaling fluctuations during fine manipulation while preserving responsiveness during coarse manipulation. Eye‐tracking features are used as attention‐related cues and fused with robot kinematics to determine motion scaling online. To validate the proposed framework, personalized optimization experiments and pilot within‐subject comparison studies were conducted with eight nonclinical participants. The results show that, compared with fixed and other adaptive scaling methods, the proposed method can reduce clutching frequency, shorten task completion time, and improve subjective ratings. These results indicate that the proposed framework can provide self‐adaptive and stable motion mapping for laparoscopic robotic teleoperation, offering a transferable strategy for broader robotic teleoperation scenarios.

candidates.title: Engagement digital y participación del fandom de Critical Role en YouTube
candidates.abstract: In an era in which transmedia narratives continue to expand, understanding audience engagement and digital interactions is essential for both content creators and researchers. Purpose: This study analyzes the forms of engagement and participation of the Critical Role fandom, one of the most influential Actual Play productions within the contemporary transmedia ecosystem. The aim is to examine audience interaction through YouTube comments by analyzing types of engagement, recurring discussion topics, and the sentiment behind these interactions. Methodology: The research is based on a quantitative content analysis of a non-probabilistic sample of 1,864 comments drawn from six episodes across the show’s three main campaigns. Results: The results reveal that, although opinion-based comments are the most frequent, informative contributions generate the highest levels of engagement and shape the most debated topics. Conclusions: These findings contribute to a broader understanding of digital fandom behavior and the active role of online communities in the construction and reception of transmedia content.

candidates.title: Remote Expert Evaluation of Tabletop Avatar Gaze Control in Asymmetric Multi-Scale MR-VR Collaboration
candidates.abstract: This paper proposes an integrated setup for a multi-scale asymmetric collaboration scenario in the context of a "remote-expert" use case, focusing on the expert side. In this system, the remote expert (with an exocentric view in Mixed Reality (MR)), uses a Tangible User Interface (TUI) to precisely position and rotate their avatar within a scaled, tabletop World-in-Miniature (WIM). Inside the WIM, the expert’s avatar and the operator share the same scale and egocentric view, while the expert retains a global tabletop overview of the plant to support collaboration. Interviews with industry experts during the participatory design phase revealed the need for an egocentric view inside the plant on the remote-expert side to enable full collaboration. We designed and study three interaction-visualization combinations to integrate and control the expert avatar’s gaze: VR (fully immersive with direct head control), Head (floating screen with direct head control), and Touch (on-avatar screen with touchpad control). We evaluated these methods with 29 participants across two fault-detection tasks: Same Machine, where both collaborators inspect the same machine, and Twin Machine, where they inspect identical machines in separate locations. The VR condition, which combines immersion, direct head control, and a full-scale view, yielded the strongest overall performance and user experience, while the tabletop avatar setup was well received for collaboration. Our findings inform the design of gaze-control techniques for asymmetric MR–VR collaboration and reveal challenges and opportunities for future work.

candidates.title: Anthropomorphism and emotional reactions to human–AI collaboration.
candidates.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly enters human professional domains, understanding emotional reactions to its involvement becomes critical.We introduce a novel experimental paradigm that distinguishes between AI involvement in "Thinker" and "Doer" roles to examine how the role AI occupies shapes affective and evaluative responses to human-AI collaboration.Across four countries (N = 1,345), including the United States, the United Kingdom, India, and Colombia, participants evaluated scenarios in which professional jobs were completed under four conditions: human only, full AI automation, human as Thinker with AI as Doer, or AI as Thinker with human as Doer.Our results showed that AI involvement decreased positive affect and appreciation while increasing negative affect.We also found particularly negative emotional reactions to AI executing emotionally charged professions (e.g., artist).Individual differences in AI anthropomorphism consistently moderated these effects.These findings demonstrate that emotional reactions to AI depend on the role it plays and the domain in which it operates.This research highlights the importance of task characteristics and individual differences in understanding human-AI collaboration in professional settings.

candidates.title: Exploring Socially Acceptable 3D Feedback Design for Inclusive Small-Group Conversation
candidates.abstract: Prior research has shown that providing feedback on group dynamics can improve the quality of small-group conversations. However, publicly delivered feedback that targets specific individuals may reduce social acceptability due to negative experiences such as social pressure, embarrassment, and resistance. This work investigates how public feedback can be designed to remain socially acceptable while maintaining its effectiveness in XR-based small-group conversations. Informed by social science and HCI literature, we identified three design strategies (incorporate humor, reduce social attention, and use indirectness) and proposed a set of metaphor- and agent-based 3D feedback probes. We then conducted a two-phase study: (1) an online survey with 50 participants to examine how such feedback designs are perceived under public and private delivery, and (2) follow-up interviews with 14 participants who completed the survey to better understand their interpretations and elicit additional insights. Results show that metaphor- and agent-based feedback can reduce social discomfort while maintaining effectiveness. Interview findings further highlighted the role of three strategies in making feedback easier to accept, while requiring careful balance. We also discussed design implications for creating socially acceptable 3D feedback to support inclusive small-group conversations in XR.

candidates.title: Lilo: A Multi-Agent Conversational Sandbox for Children's Digital Communication
candidates.abstract: Children's peer conflicts increasingly play out in group chats, where tone and timing are stripped away, and a hurtful message is easier to send than to say aloud. We present Lilo, a multi-agent conversational system that lets children practice such conversations, so they are better prepared when they encounter them in real digital communication. In Lilo, the child joins two AI-driven peers mid-argument, coached by a mentor character, also named Lilo, through a Stop-Think-Act traffic light. Through an exploratory study with 28 children (aged 9-11), we examine how children engage with Lilo's simulated peer conflict and the mentor's traffic-light interventions. The study included an intervention with Lilo, surveys before and after the intervention, and exit interviews. Participants reported significantly higher self-efficacy for coping with unpleasant messages after their interaction with Lilo. They felt safe experimenting, knowing nothing they wrote would be held against them.

candidates.title: Editorial: Rethinking technology adoption in the age of agentic artificial intelligence
Enabling Robot Learning Through Capable Hardware: Preliminary Studies In Multimodal Tactile Sensing, Bimanual Mobile Manipulation, And Semantic Demonstration Synthesis
candidates.abstract: Physical AI is continuing to advance rapidly, but its current capabilities are limited by the underlying hardware and perception stack. Robot learning, in particular, is often bottlenecked by current sensing capabilities, which limit the amount of information available to the learning algorithm and the range of tasks that can be attempted. Most robotics operations are contact-rich, meaning it requires robotic systems to have robust tactile sensing and whole-body perception to understand the state of the world during grasping and object manipulation. In this thesis, I present how there is a need to develop more capable hardware and perception capabilities to enable robot learning in robotic dexterous manipulation and mobile manipulation. To show this, I discuss how DenseTact sensors can be improved to provide more reliable tactile sensing in robotic end effectors, how we can utilize the TidyBot++ mobile manipulator platform to enable bimanual mobile manipulation research and education, and how we can use a single RGB video of a human performing a manipulation task to generate a large set of robot demonstrations for downstream policy learning. DenseTact is an optical tactile sensor that provides high-resolution tactile sensing for robotic manipulation. It’s current capabilities include shape and force sensing. Currently, it has reliability limitations in terms of its manufacturing process, calibration pipeline, and overall hardware design. Additionally, it lacks the ability to sense vibration and temperature, which are important for many manipulation tasks. As a result, I am presenting the current progress to move DenseTact to be more antrhropomorphic, reliable in manufacturing and calibration, and to have multimodal sensing capabilities. The strategy for this is to introduce a new version of the DenseTact Mini sensor, an automated calibration pipeline that builds on TensorTouch, and prototyping hardware and software for localized vibration and distributed temperature sensing modalities co-localized with the existing shape and force channels. MR. CRABS is a holonomic bimanual mobile manipulator that is built on the open-source TidyBot++ base. It includes two Realsense D435 depth cameras, one of which has an active pan-and-tilt mechanism for near-ground perception. It also includes a top LIDAR for long-range perception. It also utilizes two Trossen Robotics Widow-X arms. MR. CRABS is designed both as a research platform for bimanual mobile manipulation and as the next-generation educational platform for Stanford’s ME 326, replacing the LoCoBots used previously. The more capable hardware proved to be essential to allow students to complete the course’s final project, allowing them to better navigate the scene and perform more complex manipulation tasks that cannot be done with the LoCoBots. I present that more teams were able to complete more of the final project, and the projects were more complex than in previous years. Finally, I present Semantics as a Present (SAP), a demonstration-augmentation pipeline that turns a single RGB video of a human performing a manipulation task into an N ×M set of robot demonstrations spanning a family of pre-scanned cousin objects, with no depth sensor, no teleoperation, and no per-object annotation. The method recovers per-frame SE(3) object pose from RGB alone via distilled-DINO and depth-ranking losses, grafts the recovered motion onto each cousin via regionweighted semantic 3D Gaussian splat alignment, and replays the grafted trajectories in IsaacLab to mint demonstrations for any downstream policy (diffusion policy, ACT, π0). SAP shares its vision front end with the first two contributions, illustrating the thesis’s central claim: that perception-grounded, capable hardware is what enables modern robot learning to translate from benchmarks to real, contact-rich, bimanual, semantically rich tasks. It is compared with human demonstrations collected with an Realsense camera and teleoperation, then trained on a VLA benchmark and evaluated on a real robot to show that it can achieve comparable performance to the human demonstrations. We evaluate SAP on seven different tasks.

candidates.title: Love to Fandom: Ethical Condition for Cosplayers Subjectivity
candidates.abstract: Abstract Cosplay is a fan production that allows its participants to express their subjective values through dressing up as characters from media products. Such phenomenon exemplifies the intricate dynamics of consumer relations since cosplay explores multiple aspects of consumer culture theory. Thus, drawing from fan studies and Foucauldian frameworks, the aim of the research is analyzing how cosplayer subjectivity is constituted. In this sense, the study performs an Ethnographic Foucauldian Genealogy, based on a corpora constituted of autoethnography, netnography, online ethnographic interviews and virtual ethnomethodology data. The results evidenced two subject-forms: Nailers, representing the position taken by cosplayers who take on the role of exemplary representing the cosplay phenomenon; and Guardians, highlighting how some cosplayers feel responsible for maintaining a community of practitioners that allows those interested in cosplay to feel comfortable. Both subjectivities share an ethic named as Love to fandom. Such ethic guide cosplayers to produce truths about the ways in which they interact or show solidarity between peers based on their own condition as fans, legitimizing autonomous and complementary subjectivities, and enhancing and ensuring experiences with cosplay practice. Thus, the study expands the possibilities of living love through consumption – here, inherent to fans. It is a love established and maintained by the consumers themselves both through the intense relationship with the products consumed and through interactions with their peers.

candidates.title: SurgPace: Complexity-aware progressive distillation for surgical multimodal large language models
Big Data and Predictive Analytics Capability and Triple Bottom Line Sustainability Performance: A Resource‐Based Perspective From BRICS Nations
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT This study aims to investigate the relationship between big data and predictive analytics (BDPA) capability and triple bottom line (TBL) sustainability performance in BRICS manufacturing firms. Grounded in the resource‐based view (RBV), we conceptualise BDPA capability as a third‐order hierarchical construct comprising tangible resources (data infrastructure and technology), intangible resources (organisational culture, organisational learning and data‐driven culture) and human‐related skills (technical skills and management skills). Survey data have been used from 304 IT and analytics professionals representing different organisations across BRICS economies and partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS‐SEM) with 5000 bootstrap samples; we test six hypotheses examining both the resource‐capability link and the capability‐performance link. Results reveal that all three resource categories significantly contribute to BDPA capability, with human‐related skills exerting the strongest influence. BDPA capability, in turn, significantly predicts environmental performance, social performance and economic performance, explaining 40%, 50% and 55% of variance, respectively. The study contributes to the literature by providing an empirically validated, multi‐level resource‐capability‐performance framework for analytics‐driven sustainability in emerging economies.

candidates.title: Dexterous Robotic Hands in the Foundation-Model Era: A Full-Stack Survey of Hardware, Data, Cross-Embodiment Transfer, Learning, and Evaluation
candidates.abstract: Dexterous robotic hands are increasingly coupled to large-scale human data and foundation models, yet progress in hardware, representation learning and evaluation is often assessed separately. This survey reviews work from January 2024 to early November 2026, with earlier studies included to establish technical lineages. We organize the literature into five interdependent layers: hardware; data collection and curation; cross-embodiment transfer; learning and foundation models; and evaluation and applications. Human hand-object understanding and tactile sensing provide two cross-cutting perspectives. A system-level architecture, comparative tables and five case analyses connect design choices across these layers. We distinguish within-study experimental comparisons from heterogeneous corpus statistics, vendor specifications and company-reported results. Three conclusions emerge. First, the value of human data depends on kinematic, visual and contact alignment, not recording volume alone. Second, shared action representations and foundation policies do not remove embodiment-specific constraints on force, latency and contact. Third, task completion is insufficient to establish physical correctness or deployment readiness. Evidence remains limited for zero-shot transfer of contact-rich skills between morphologically different hands, long-duration reliability, and cross-sensor tactile generalization. We identify eleven open problems and propose reporting interfaces and controlled comparisons that can make full-stack progress more measurable. The review is a structured narrative synthesis rather than a pooled performance ranking or an exhaustive systematic review.

candidates.title: Fans for life? Popular culture-inspired tattoos and the challenges of inscribed expressions of fandom
candidates.abstract: This article examines active practices of fandom and identity communication through the collection of fandom-based tattoos. Through an analysis of fan theory, the article argues that fans who express their devotion to media culture through tattooing engage in a distinctive act of active fandom that represents a bodily extension of Rojek’s concept of the fan reliquary, a religiously inspired repository of collected items and artefacts by which fans signify their fandom to inspiration figures (such as Taylor Swift). The article considers the critical issues relating to fans that have used their bodies as tattooed reliquaries, but for whom the designs have become problematic in the wake of negative social actions and cultural reactions towards the objects of the fandom, such as J.K. Rowling. Tattoos, therefore, signify a potent expression of fan identification, but their permanence makes them a risk in an unpredictable landscape of popular and media culture.

candidates.title: Personality expression and perception in large language models and humans
candidates.abstract: Abstract Growing numbers of people frequently turn to Large Language Models (LLMs) for concerns from various areas of life. Because its content has become ubiquitous, examining user perceptions of LLM-produced text and its distinguishability from human writing is crucial. This study investigated how seven LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-3.5, Llama 3, Gemma, Gemini, Phi-3, Orca-2) describe themselves when compared to humans. LLM-generated outputs and human responses were collected using psychological questionnaires (Big Five, self-esteem, narcissism) and tailored prompts to elicit short self-descriptive texts. Six LLM and ten human judges then evaluated personality traits and text origin based on these self-descriptions (140 total, half LLM-generated). Results show that current LLM outputs can convey personality-consistent cues in questionnaires and texts. The perception of such significantly differed from that of humans. Both LLM and human judges accurately inferred personality from short self-descriptions and correctly differentiated between LLM-generated and human text. Linguistic analysis and participant feedback revealed textual cues distinguishing LLM-produced from human language and offered insights into how LLM versus human judgment and decisionmaking differ.

candidates.title: The Effect of AI Virtual Influencers on Purchase Intention: The Mediating Role of Parasocial Interaction: A Field Study on the Fashion Industry in Egypt
candidates.abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the effect of AI virtual influencers (VIs); in terms of perceived authenticity and perceived anthropomorphism on Purchase intention, viewing the mediating role of Parasocial interaction, by application on the women fashion industry in Egypt. Questionnaire was used to collect data, and a non-probability purposive sampling technique was adopted. A total of 128 responses were collected and analyzed. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was performed in R using the SEMinR package (version 2.5.0). The findings supported all the proposed direct and indirect hypotheses, concluding that perceived authenticity and anthropomorphism play a vital role in directly influencing purchase intention, and that parasocial interaction also plays an indirect role in mediating this relationship.

candidates.title: Federated Learning for Official Statistics: A Systematic Review of Privacy‐Preserving Architectures and the Path Toward GSBPM Integration
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT National Statistical Offices (NSOs) face an escalating “privacy‐utility” impasse, where the demand for high‐granularity data must compete with the near zero risk tolerance of legal frameworks like the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Traditional centralized collection creates “honeypots” for breaches, exposing a nation's entire digital census or tax records. This paper provides a systematic review of Federated Learning (FL) as a decentralized framework that eliminates raw microdata consolidation. Drawing on 77 peer‐reviewed. Studies and technical reports published between 2020 and 2026, the study evaluates Horizontal and Vertical FL architectures alongside Privacy‐Enhancing Technologies (PETs). The analysis reveals that while PETs introduce a “utility gap,” Under controlled experimental settings and standardized non‐IID configurations, the evaluated architectures frequently achieve utility bounds exceeding 90% of their centralized equivalents, though this outcome varies based on the assigned privacy budget () and data distribution. Crucially, the study demonstrates that the mathematical noise required for Differential Privacy (DP) can threaten strict accuracy thresholds; for example, an aggressive privacy budget can cause census distributions to shift more than 77% from the true mean, rendering indicators like Gross Domestic Product (GDP) or unemployment rates statistically meaningless. Beyond these accuracy trade‐offs, the paper addresses the Non‐Independent and Identically Distributed (Non‐IID) nature of government datasets and identifies research gaps in standardized audit trails. The paper proposes a novel roadmap for integrating FL into the Generic Statistical Business Process Model (GSBPM), offering NSOs and international statistical bodies a technically grounded and legally coherent pathway toward next generation data infrastructure.

candidates.title: Crafting Persuasive Environmental Messages for Virtual Influencers: The Role of Anthropomorphic Conversational Style, Persuasion Appeal, and Behavioral Context
candidates.abstract: The use of virtual influencers (VIs) has emerged as an alternative to human influencers for marketing initiatives. Prior studies have focused primarily on the visual characteristics of VIs and their use in advertising settings, with limited attention given to their capacity to drive pro-environmental behaviors (PEBs). We have developed an integrated persuasive framework, grounded in the Elaboration Likelihood Model and Congruity Theory, that links VI characteristics, message appeals, and behavioral context to persuasion outcomes. Study 1 examined VI message strategies and found that competence (vs. warmth) anthropomorphic conversational style and influencing (vs. de-influencing) appeal enhanced message persuasiveness. Study 2 explored the effectiveness of VIs in promoting plastic waste reduction behaviors across different behavioral contexts and found that messages pertaining to difficult (vs. easy) and private (vs. public) behaviors significantly enhanced message persuasiveness, but that messages promoting easy and private behaviors generated stronger behavioral intentions. The insights from these studies can provide valuable guidance to businesses, marketers, and environmental advocates on effective VI message strategies for addressing challenges related to climate change.

candidates.title: Teach, Abstract, Apply: A Framework for Dialogue-Driven Task Learning with Collaborative Robots
candidates.abstract: Collaborative robots (cobots) are designed to be safer and more interactive than traditional industrial robots, share the same workspace as humans, and assist them in a range of shop-floor tasks such as palletization, joint assembly, and part inspection. Many of these tasks involve repetitive workflows that may evolve with changes in production environments and task specifications. These requirements motivate the need for intuitive interfaces that allow workers to modify workflows on the shop floor and generalise these routines for future use. This work introduces the Teach-Abstract-Apply (TAA) framework, which enables human operators to (a) teach new workflows to cobots in natural language, (b) abstract the taught workflows into skills for later use, and (c) apply these skills in different settings. As a case study, we apply the TAA framework to a collaborative structure-building task and evaluate it with both open-weight (Qwen3-Coder) and closed (GPT5.2-Codex) models in self-play and cross-model configurations. Our results show that skill abstraction improves task success rates and reduces interaction cost. Beyond automated evaluation, a preliminary human-in-the-loop study suggests that the pipeline also works with human instructions.

candidates.title: Sensorium: An Open-Source Multimodal Data Collection and Curation Library for Embodied Surgical AI
candidates.abstract: Embodied surgical AI requires reliable multimodal data, yet surgical data collection remains costly, difficult to repeat, and strongly dependent on the hardware setup. We present Sensorium, an open-source Python library for recording, processing, annotating, and curating multimodal surgical data from configurable robot and sensor streams using the Robot Operating System (ROS) and ROS2 middleware. The library combines operator-facing data acquisition, configurable processing, semantic annotation, and episodic dataset generation. We evaluate Sensorium across 1516 recordings of phantom, ex vivo, and in vivo porcine experiments involving multiple surgical tasks and sensing configurations, and report preliminary usability feedback.

candidates.title: Gaze-Assisted Supervisory Control for Lunar Robotic Arm Teleoperation Under Concurrent Monitoring
candidates.abstract: Rover-mounted robotic arms can extend human reach during lunar sample handling, but continuous joystick teleoperation requires repeated visual-motor alignment while operators may also need to monitor system states. This paper presents a gaze-assisted supervisory control framework in which gaze nominates a rock or placement target, explicit confirmation authorizes the action, and the robot performs bounded autonomous grasp-and-place execution. The framework was evaluated against manual joystick teleoperation in a mission-analog virtual reality study with 16 participants. The study used a 2 x 2 x 3 within-subject design varying control mode, placement difficulty, and concurrent monitoring load. Mean recorded task completion time decreased from 47.65 to 18.43 s per rock, with 72.5% of this difference arising during grasping. Under the tested auditory monitoring conditions, gaze-assisted supervisory control showed less average proportional slowing, with no detected control-mode difference in monitoring-response accuracy or speed. The rate of gaze shifts between core areas of interest decreased from 49.98 to 27.73 shifts/min, while the raw NASA Task Load Index score decreased from 32.54 to 18.26. However, the benefit was task dependent. In precision placement, manual control yielded lower mean placement error and a higher placement success rate. These findings support a mixed-initiative allocation in which gaze enables rapid task-level intention specification and autonomous execution, while precision-critical stages retain manual refinement.

candidates.title: Making Meets Informal Innovation: Formalisation, Access and Openness in Indian Makerspaces
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Makerspaces and fabrication labs (fablabs) are inclusive and open infrastructures. They democratise access to tools and technologies and facilitate bottom‐up innovation. Research on these spaces thus highlights the importance of openness, community orientation and the ability to foster informal experimentation that these spaces enable. In this paper, I examine how these features have been operationalised in contexts characterised by a high degree of economic and institutional informality by focusing specifically on Indian makerspaces and fablabs. I ask how these spaces relate to need‐driven local innovation practices and how they are sustained. The paper uses qualitative data collected through semi‐structured interviews and analyses the organisation of access, learning and innovation in these spaces. The analysis indicates that makerspaces and fablabs in India do not work as open infrastructures in their entirety. Instead, they serve as mediators between informal innovation practices and institutionalised pathways shaped by an entrepreneurial discourse. The analysis further indicates that they create new limits of participation, expertise and knowledge exchange. The paper contributes to the body of literature on open infrastructures and informal innovations by reconceptualising the notion of openness as a result of governance rather than as a characteristic of such spaces.

candidates.title: Emotional and behavioral asymmetries in user responses to virtual versus human influencers
candidates.abstract: As AI virtual influencers (AIVIs) proliferate, understanding human-AI emotional engagement is vital for advancing affective computing. To examine whether AIVIs evoke comparable affective responses to human influencers (HIs), we analyzed 156,918 Instagram comments that received 12+ million likes, integratinglarge language model (LLM)-derived knowledge graphs, emotion analysis, and machine learning. HI-directed discourse shows more differentiated emotional expression and a pattern consistent with more cohesive semantic networks than AIVI-directed discourse. AIVI-directed comments are less likely to express positive affect (24.8% vs. 41.5%) and also less likely to express negative affect (5.8% vs. 9.3%), indicating reduced affective expression of either valence rather than heightened negativity. This group-level tendency is not uniform: affective engagement varies substantially across AIVIs, and that variation is more closely associated with positive than with negative expression. Our Multi-Signal Embedding Network (MSEN), incorporating behavioral metrics and OpenAI semantic embeddings, classified influencer types from behavioral, affective and semantic features (F1 = 0.89), outperforming baselines including a state-of-the-art zero-shot LLM. These findings identify a boundary condition for the Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) paradigm: human-like appearance can elicit social responses without producing affective and semantic response patterns as rich as those elicited by HIs.

candidates.title: From digital shadows to assured intervention: a systematic review of embodiment, authority, and assurance in manufacturing quality digital twins
candidates.abstract: Abstract Rapid advances in AI and robotics are extending manufacturing digital twins beyond passive monitoring to closed-loop control and physical intervention. Yet in manufacturing QA, the term “digital twin” is used for both systems that only observe and systems that act on the physical process. This distinction matters because once a digital twin acts, model validity is no longer enough; the intervention must also be authorized, bounded, traceable, and verified. Existing maturity frameworks capture connectivity and automation but give less attention to the assurance requirements that arise when digital-twin outputs are translated into physical action. We address this gap by introducing an Embodiment-Authority-Assurance (EAA) framework that distinguishes how quality information leads to physical action, who has authority over that action, and how the intervention is assured. We apply the framework to a systematic review of 235 manufacturing QA studies, selected from 868 publications identified through Scopus and Web of Science between 2017 and 2026, classifying them across five maturity levels from digital shadows to governed adaptive QA twins. We found that the frontier of manufacturing QA digital twins is shifting from monitoring and advisory support toward human-approved and bounded autonomous intervention, with higher-maturity applications becoming increasingly visible in recent years. Yet these advances remain fragmented across the literature, with no reviewed study bringing them together into a fully assured intervention chain. By revealing this shift, our study reframes manufacturing QA digital-twin maturity around a new frontier: not simply whether digital twins can act, but whether increasingly autonomous interventions can be governed and assured.

candidates.title: Understanding Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption: Practices, Challenges, and Evolution in Open-Source Software
candidates.abstract: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards establish algorithms for quantum-safe systems, but empirical evidence about how software projects implement and maintain PQC support remains limited. We investigate this implementation and maintenance work by mining 114,361 commits and 5,713 issues across 179 open-source repositories. We use human annotation and validated LLM classification to identify PQC algorithms in commits, classify their adoption status and deployment mode, and identify technical challenges in issue discussions. The commit classification for PQC algorithms reveals that 90% of commits concern maintenance of existing support. From the issue discussions, we construct an 11-category taxonomy of recurring technical challenges. Build, packaging, and dependency failures, along with functional defects, account for approximately half of categorized issues. To examine how PQC support evolves, we use time-series analysis and first implementations of individual algorithms within repositories around NIST standardization milestones. After the 2024 finalization, standardized algorithm names appeared in more than 80% of the PQC development changes analyzed, although earlier names such as Kyber continued to appear. Development activity increased over the observation period. Our milestone analysis, however, did not find a significant increase in first implementations. Migration plans should therefore account for sustained maintenance, prioritize build reliability and integration testing, and track both standardized and predecessor algorithm names. We make the dataset, taxonomy, annotations, and analysis pipeline publicly available.

candidates.title: Neither queer, nor just a transaction: realignment speech and the pursuit of heteronormative intelligibility in otome cosplay commissions
candidates.abstract: The commercial rise of Chinese otome games has birthed a novel gig economy: ‘cosplay commissions’, where female fans hire female cosplayers to enact fictional romances. Drawing on 32 in-depth interviews, this study explores the tension in this novel fan practice: while the practice enables participants to experiment with a feminized, consumer-driven model of intimacy, where women actively orchestrate their ideal romance, it simultaneously triggers anxieties about violating scripts of heteronormativity. To manage these tensions, participants collaboratively enact a ‘sanitized romance’ through relational work that meticulously curates idealized heteronormative romance scripts (caring, pampering, and exclusivity), compensating for the perceived failures of real-world masculinity. More importantly, to secure moral legitimacy within China’s patriarchal constraints, participants produce what we term realignment speech, drawing symbolic boundaries to distance themselves from any association with sex work, queerness, or moral deviance. Through this boundary work, they reframe their actions not as ‘buying love’ or ‘loving a woman’, but as ‘immersing in pure love fantasy’. We argue that this ambivalent mode of intimacy – transgressive in practice yet normatively policed in self-understanding – demonstrates how realignment speech renders female desire intelligible and thus survivable within a rigid moral economy through both micro-resistance to dominant norms and creative reappropriation of their toolkit.

candidates.title: Beyond Being Accurate: Implications for Using Natural Language Descriptions for Accessible 3D Modeling with~Blind and Low Vision Makers
candidates.abstract: People who are blind or have low vision (BLV) are largely excluded from 3D modeling tools that rely on visual representations of geometry. Natural language descriptions offer a potential path to accessibility, but it is unclear whether language alone can support the deep spatial understanding that editing, not just browsing, requires. Advances in generative AI offer the promise of automatic model description, yet descriptions suited to BLV modelers are structurally distinct from alt-text and from existing 3D model captioning datasets, and the domain-specific requirements for generating them are not well understood. We address this through two coordinated studies: an autoethnographic pilot in which the blind first author worked with 12 sighted participants to develop a taxonomy of descriptive strategies, and a Wizard-of-Oz main study that applied those strategies as idealized scripts with 10 BLV participants. We identify a systematic use-to-editing gap: descriptions that support accurate but incomplete mental models are insufficient for specifying modifications, because editing requires knowing the state of features the user did not know to ask about. We show that this gap produces four failure types (accuracy, completeness, expression, and navigation) that accuracy-focused evaluation frameworks cannot detect. We propose a two-phase evaluation framework that diagnoses the failure type a description system exhibits and guides developers toward targeted design interventions, thereby providing a methodological standard for assessing whether description-based systems genuinely support BLV modelers as creators.

candidates.title: Editorial: Computational multimodal sensing and perception for robotic systems
candidates.abstract: Each sensor captures its own slice of the physical world. For robots working in complex and dynamic 2 environments, robust perception requires integrating complementary information from multiple sensory 3 modalities. Vision may provide global context, while tactile, auditory, event-based, and other emerging 4 sensing technologies can reveal more interaction details that are difficult to obtain by vision alone. Together, 5 these modalities can support more robust and adaptive robotic behaviors. Rather than relying on artificial calibration targets or discrete semantic labels, the method aligns continuous 44 semantic probability distributions between LiDAR and camera data.
