candidates.title: RoboARCade: Benchmarking Agentic Robot Control
candidates.abstract: Improvements in multi-modal capabilities have enabled agents to act directly as robot policies, a setting we refer to as agentic robot control (ARC). We introduce RoboARCade, a benchmark of long-horizon manipulation tasks across three embodiments designed to test in-context adaptation, memory, and reasoning for precise control. The tasks build on existing open-source benchmarks, which we make harder by widening the range of initial conditions. RoboARCade is easy to use and extend: all tasks run on a single simulation backend, MuJoCo, each task is a self-contained data pack, and agents connect through interchangeable interfaces, so new tasks, agents, and interfaces can be added independently. The benchmark separates leading agents: GPT-6 Astra achieves 49.8% compared with 43.6% for Claude Fable 5.1, leaving substantial room for improvement. Comparing two interfaces, we find that a richer visual interface adds only 1.5 to 6.8 points at 1.7 to 2.3 times the cost. Failures stem mostly from choosing a poor manipulation strategy or executing a good one imprecisely, rarely from misunderstanding the scene, and agents incorrectly claim success on 24% to 39% of attempted subtasks. Agents can also improve without human input: one successful demonstration in context raises Astra's score from 53.5% to 73.0% on a five-task subset, and a prompt the agent writes and revises itself reaches 72.0%. Code, videos and full traces are available at roboarcade.org.

candidates.title: A Taxonomy of Mental Health and Technology Needs for Alzheimer’s and Dementia Caregivers
candidates.abstract: Family members caring for individuals with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (AD/ADRD) provide the foundation of long-term care worldwide. In 2023, more than 11 million U.S. family and friends contributed 18 billion hours of unpaid care, often at the cost of their own physical and mental health. These informal caregivers-also referred as the "invisible second patients"-experience elevated rates of mental health problems. Yet research commonly reduces their complex psychosocial experiences to a single construct of caregiver burden, obscuring which specific needs are unmet or effectively supported. At the same time, digital and AI-enabled technologies are rapidly expanding, from smartphone apps and videoconferencing to sensor platforms and AI chatbots. However, the absence of shared frameworks across medicine, psychology, and technology research limits cumulative progress. This study introduces a Caregiver Mental Health and Technology Taxonomy that systematically links AD/ADRD caregiver needs with corresponding classes of technology-based interventions. Drawing from an interdisciplinary literature review and two qualitative studies with caregivers, the taxonomy identifies mismatches between caregiver priorities and existing technological support, highlights under-served domains such as relational strain and compassion fatigue, and proposes design directions for adaptive, responsive systems. The framework offers a shared vocabulary to guide clinicians, researchers, and technology designers in developing more person-centered and clinically grounded innovation in dementia care. Supplementary Information: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s12126-026-09686-4.

candidates.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization for Agentic Robotics
candidates.abstract: Frontier models such as GPT-6 Astra now directly control robots and can generalize better than vision-language-action models (VLAs). We argue that this ability could arise from two distinct, composable skills: semantic reasoning, to understand what a task asks for in a scene, and motion control, to move the robot to do it. We show that small open VLMs are already capable of the first and mainly lack the second. We introduce Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP), a recipe that teaches this missing motion skill, entirely in simulation on simple primitive tasks and from the model's own successes, with no frontier teacher or distillation and no real-world robot data. ZAP reaches 96.7% success on real-world tasks, matching GPT-6 Astra in our harness while running 3x faster and 17x cheaper, and 74.0% on a bimanual adaptation of RoboLab-120, on par with GPT-6 Astra's 72.2%. ZAP also generalizes to new objects, goals, and strategies, and in simulation to a robot embodiment on which it never trained.

candidates.title: AI in Food and Agriculture: Ethics from Farm to Table
candidates.abstract: This book offers the first comprehensive philosophical account of what is ethically at stake as artificial intelligence (AI) becomes embedded in agricultural systems, from precision irrigation platforms on the Kansas High Plains to robotic harvesters in the apple orchards of Washington State. In the face of changing weather patterns, droughts, and fewer available resources, modern agricultural practices are evolving, embracing AI systems to help increase crop efficiency, production, and yields. However, technological innovation on the farm often comes with environmental and social costs. This book analyzes AI and Information Systems through the lens of contemporary challenges in agricultural processes ranging from farm to table. Drawing on field visits across the Pacific Northwest and sustained engagement with agricultural ethics, the philosophy of technology, and environmental justice, this book develops three original frameworks for evaluating agricultural AI: the Four Pillars of Agricultural Ethics, which assesses AI across its impacts on society, individuals, the environment, and animals; the SEED framework, which translates sustainability into design-stage commitments for responsible AI; and a trivalent environmental justice framework that holds distribution, recognition, and intergenerational responsibility together as inseparable governance concerns. Together, these tools make the case for bringing ethics into the design of agricultural AI before costs become embedded in the landscape. This book will be of great interest to students and scholars of agricultural and food ethics, agricultural technology and innovation, AI and the philosophy of technology.

candidates.title: Business Ethics: A Contemporary Introduction
candidates.abstract: Packed with examples, this book offers a clear and engaging overview of ethical issues in business. It begins with a discussion of foundational issues, including the objectivity of ethics, the content of ethical theories, and the debate between capitalism and socialism, making it suitable for the beginning student. It then examines ethical issues in business in three broad areas. The first is the market, where it examines what can be sold (the limits of markets) and how it can be sold (ethics in marketing). The second is work. Topics in this area are health and safety, meaningful work, pay, hiring and firing, privacy, artificial intelligence, and whistleblowing. The third area is business and society. Here readers explore corporate social responsibility, business and politics, environmental ethics, and international business. Issues are introduced through real-world examples that underscore their importance and make them come alive. Arguments for opposing positions are given fair hearings and students are encouraged to develop their own views. Major changes to the Second Edition include a new chapter on businesses’ environmental obligations, extended discussion of the ethics of artificial intelligence, and expanded treatment of marketing ethics and shareholder primacy. To aid in teaching, learning, and accessibility, each chapter now provides a summary and list of learning objectives. Examples are updated throughout, and a new a list of cases alongside a glossary of key terms are featured at the end of this book. Key updates to the Second Edition Includes a new chapter on business, the environment, and climate change. Adds features to make the text easier to navigate, including a more detailed table of contents, a glossary of key terms, and a list of cases and examples used in the book. Each chapter now begins with a summary and list of learning objectives, helping students to read more actively. Includes more focused study questions at the end of each chapter, encouraging more engagement with the text. Contains a heavily revised, more nuanced third chapter on ethical theories. Provides additional coverage of AI ethics throughout the book, focusing specifically on issues of bias, transparency, privacy, and safety.

candidates.title: การศึกษาเปรียบเทียบความเหงาและปัจจัยที่เกี่ยวข้องก่อนและหลังการเลี้ยงแมว ของผู้พักอาศัยในเขตกรุงเทพมหานครและปริมณฑล
candidates.abstract: This study aimed to: (1) examine owners’ loneliness levels before and after adopting a cat; and (2) analyze factors associated with changes in loneliness levels among cat owners. A prospective observational pre-post design was employed. The participants comprised 37 volunteers aged 18 years or older who resided in Bangkok and its metropolitan areas and had recently started keeping cats exclusively indoors. The research instruments consisted of an online questionnaire covering participants’ demographic characteristics and cat-related information, and the Thai version of the UCLA Loneliness Scale Version 3, which demonstrated a Cronbach’s alpha reliability coefficient of 0.91–0.93. Data were collected at two time points: before cat ownership and after 14 days of cat ownership. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, paired t-tests, independent t-tests, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), and Pearson’s correlation coefficient, with statistical significance set at .05. The findings revealed that the mean loneliness score decreased significantly from 40.14 ± 11.37 before cat ownership to 35.97 ± 10.81 after 14 days (t = 3.367, p = .002, Cohen’s d = 0.55). Regarding factors associated with changes in loneliness, quantitative variables and the biological characteristics of cats were not significantly associated with loneliness reduction. In contrast, cat-carrying behavior was the only factor significantly associated with a decrease in loneliness (t = 2.154, p = .038). Participants who carried their cats experienced a mean reduction of 5.12 points in loneliness scores, compared with a reduction of only 1.20 points among those who did not engage in this behavior. These findings suggest that 14 days of cat ownership were associated with a significant reduction in loneliness, while close physical interaction, particularly carrying a cat, may represent an important factor associated with this change. However, the absence of a control group and the relatively short follow-up period limit the interpretation of causal relationships. Further studies should employ larger samples, include control groups, and extend the follow-up period to establish more robust evidence regarding the long-term relationship between cat ownership and loneliness.

candidates.title: Livestreaming Platform Research: The Netnography of YouTube Communities
candidates.abstract: The aim of the article is to provide a framework for adapting qualitative ethnographic research within the field of YouTube communities. Drawing from literature on netnography and online communities, this article discusses established research guidelines and how they need to be adapted to the context of YouTube communities. The fans’ communities on YouTube fulfill the definition of online communities. YouTube communities require a specific approach when applying netnographic methodologies. Some issues, like privacy, are debatable; therefore, researchers need to answer a series of ethical questions before attempting to conduct research within this field. This work contributes to the literature on qualitative research by introducing guidelines for netnography applied to streaming platforms on the example of YouTube. The article provides guidelines for future research within the streaming platform environment. Ethical dilemmas are discussed to facilitate methodological decision-making in future research.

candidates.title: Personalization of Basic and Moral Values Guiding LLM-Controlled Assistant Robots
candidates.abstract: Personal assistant robots powered by large language models (LLMs) are likely to enter everyday life within the next decade, but the values that should guide their behaviour remain largely unspecified. Current alignment practice steers a single model toward an aggregate of human values, ignoring that individual users may prefer a robot whose value profile differs from their own. We administer parallel self- and robot-targeted versions of three established psycho-metric instruments - the simplified Schwartz Values Survey (SVS), the Portrait Values Questionnaire (PVQ-21), and the Moral Foundations Questionnaire (MFQ) - to potential future users (N=22), capturing both their personal values and the values they would want an assistant robot to embody. We compare the three instruments as personalization tools using the UEQ-S and benchmark fifteen contemporary LLMs against the resulting profiles. Participants wanted their robot to score markedly lower than themselves on personal-focus values and higher on social-focus values; moral profiles were nearly identical. LLMs prompted to act as robots shifted only weakly toward the desired profile, indicating that default model behaviour and prompt engineering are no substitute for explicit value personalization.

candidates.title: Queer Social Television: an empowering consumption assemblage explored through RuPaul’s Drag Race
candidates.abstract: Purpose Social Television (STV) describes the digital engagement of consumers with TV shows. Marketing studies have used this term to investigate how transmedia strategies broaden reach, engagement and co-productive consumption experiences. However, its managerial potential within contexts of gender and sexual dissidence remains overlooked. To explore this gap, this study aims to understand how queer fandom practices (re)configure the STV phenomenon toward the digital engagement of dissident identities. Design/methodology/approach The authors conducted a year-long netnography on Twitter/X with Brazilian fans of RuPaul’s Drag Race. Findings The findings suggest how discourses and practices are enacted through four interconnected categories of queering work that happen through broadcast, social media, fandom and activism. Social implications Four managerial strategies capable of promoting inclusion and social change are proposed, linking the study to Sustainable Development Goal 10 (Reduced Inequalities). Originality/value This study conceptualizes Queer Social Television and theorize it as an empowering consumption assemblage, explaining its nuances through a Global South perspective. In doing so, it contributes to both STV and Consumer Culture Theory (CCT) scholarships.

candidates.title: From Bias to Positionality: A critical grammar for Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Bias has become a default lens for understanding what machine learning systems do and how we should relate to them. Bias is at root a deviation from a standard; in decision making systems we can supply a standard from outside: a law, a protected attribute, a benchmark, a statistical property. However, even there, biased is often used as a shorthand, without stating what the position taken is - a silent ``relative to''. In a general use of language models, nothing supplies the standard: there is no decision to audit and no counterfactual output, so the shorthand fails. We argue that positionality -- the located, articulated, owned and contestable position from which anything is said -- is the better grammar for the question these models now force: who is speaking, from where? Against the vendors' answer of nowhere and the seductive possibility of everywhere, we argue that when a model is taken as-if speaking, it speaks from somewhere, and this means positionality can describe models, and the way they are believed beyond their warrant, even though they are not accountable speakers. A model's positionality is laminar -- laid down across corpus, tuning, system prompt, application and the live conversation. We separate three sets of factors: the positionality of a model's creators, the behaviour they intend for it, and the behaviour it enacts, and situate current work within this matrix. This lets us highlight what each stratum inherits from the one below, with ruptures and collapses where that inheritance is disavowed. We then return to where models speak from, and discuss the implications for how models are made, read and held accountable.

candidates.title: Designing IoT Applications with Serverless Concepts and Open Source Tools
candidates.abstract: This work explains step-by-step development and implementation of serverless functions at sensor, edge, and cloud levels for IoT-enabled applications, addressing data privacy, cost inefficiency, and scalability challenges. It discusses the systematic deployment of serverless functions across sensor nodes, edge clusters, and cloud infrastructure using open-source tools such as ESP-IDF, WasmEdge, and OpenFaaS. It covers key topics including edge-fog-cloud computing, IoT communication protocols (MQTT, LoRa, Zigbee, etc.), benchmarking methods, and performance comparisons. It highlights the integration of serverless concepts to build efficient computing platforms, drawing on insights from collaborative research with leading universities. Discusses the application of serverless functions on edge-enabled clusters, such as Raspberry Pi clusters mounted at our research labs. Details exploration of IoT communication protocols and offers benchmarking methodologies for evaluating serverless IoT systems. Expresses the utilization of open-source tools and frameworks to activate serverless functions in IoT-enabled applications. Explains future directions for scalable and efficient IoT application development. This book is for professionals, academicians, and students interested in IoT-enabled applications.

candidates.title: The Generative Economy of Agony: Latent Structures of Meaning and Resilience Mechanisms in the Lyrical Work of Taylor Swift
candidates.abstract: Abstract This article employs the methodology of Objective Hermeneutics to reconstruct the latent structures of meaning and resilience mechanisms within the lyrical oeuvre of American songwriter Taylor Swift. Moving beyond intentionalist and biographical reductionism, the analysis identifies a generative case logic structured around four sequential dimensions: the dialectic of emotional staging and drive structure, the somatization and material reification of psychological trauma, the establishment of a generative economy of agony, and the ultimate transition toward absolute indifference. Drawing on the sociology of emotion and theories of emotional capitalism, the study demonstrates how the lyrical subject converts vulnerability, powerlessness, and rage into highly liquid aesthetic and emotional capital, culminating in a structural resilience defined as a "sequin armor". Furthermore, the paper integrates the Aristotelian concept of catharsis to illustrate how this autofictional narrative serves as a therapeutic script, facilitating collective emotional regulation, purification, and empowerment within transnational fan communities. Ultimately, the work is analyzed as a late-capitalist protocol of emotional labor, where private suffering is systematically economized and transformed into a globally resonant resilience framework.

candidates.title: ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING: CHARACTERIZING CARTEL UAS INNOVATION PATHWAYS
candidates.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM), particularly low-cost 3D printing, is creating a new pathway for Mexican cartels to locally reproduce, modify, and customize unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) and their components. Cartels already demonstrate technical adaptability, commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) supply chains, and the use of 3D-printed components that could support broader AM adoption. The growing availability of digital UAS designs, technical documentation, inexpensive printers, and commercially available electronics could reduce cartels’ dependence on identifiable COTS platforms while enabling more decentralized and adaptable drone supply chains. Over the next five years, advances in AI could further lower the technical expertise and time required to design and manufacture customized UAS components, increasing the potential significance of AM as a component of the cartel UAS ecosystem.

candidates.title: Designing an Open-Source Multi-Vat Digital Light Processing Printer
candidates.abstract: Abstract Additive manufacturing has undergone rapid evolution in modalities that can mimic some of the aspect of native human tissue architectures with high resolution. Among these emerging approaches, digital light processing (DLP)-based printing enables the fabrication of intricate biomimetic architectures through the photopolymerization of polymer-based hydrogels. The recent emergence of multivat printing further enhances this capability, enabling the spatial arrangement of differently formulated or labeled photocrosslinkable resins. However, the widespread adoption of DLP printing remains constrained by the high cost, proprietary hardware, and limited customizability of commercially available systems. Here, we present an open-source multivat DLP printing platform developed through the integration and modification of two low-cost commercially available 3D printers. A dedicated Python-based graphical user interface was developed, providing user-defined control over critical printing parameters, including exposure time, layer height, printing sequence, and vat switching. Comprehensive hardware documentation and a complete bill of materials (BOM) are provided to ensure reproducibility and accessibility across research laboratories. In addition to multivat printing, the system enables spatial modulation of mechanical properties within a single photocrosslinkable formulation through programmable light exposure and supports enhanced z-axis resolution through user-defined layer thickness control. The platform was validated through the fabrication of geometrically complex, multivat, and mechanically heterogeneous constructs. Collectively, this work establishes an accessible and customizable DLP printing platform that enables advanced hydrogel fabrication and demonstrates automated multivat printing.

candidates.title: Water–material interactions in underwater laser additive manufacturing: process physics, microstructure evolution, and performance
candidates.abstract: Abstract A harsh marine environment causes severe surface damage to underwater infrastructure, jeopardizing its long-term reliability and necessitating in-situ underwater repair. Underwater laser additive manufacturing (ULAM) is a promising technique that enables direct deposition of metallic materials on water-exposed components. While there is a consensus that ULAM fundamentally deviates from land-based processing due to extreme boundary conditions such as strong optical attenuation, intensified heat dissipation, and environment-assisted chemical reactions, significant scientific controversies remain. Current studies present contradictory conclusions regarding the exact mechanisms of defect nucleation, the stability of the gas-liquid interface in local dry cavity, and the competing effects of thermal gradients on microstructural phase evolution versus residual stress. This review evaluates these disputed mechanisms. By dissecting the multi-physics coupling among the laser, melt pool, and underwater environment, we identify the fundamental causes of discrepancies in existing literature. This review establishes a comprehensive process-structure-property framework that systematically links transient thermophysical phenomena to microstructural characteristics and surface degradation behavior. By delineating established knowledge from unresolved contradictions, this work highlights the critical scientific gaps and provides a clear roadmap for achieving controllable quality and reliable engineering deployment of the ULAM technique.

candidates.title: A Low-Cost Co-Designed Robotic System for Selective Sweet Pepper Harvesting with Edge-Computed Perception and Decision-Making
candidates.abstract: Existing selective sweet pepper harvesting systems use industrial arms and high-performance computers, which limits adoption on small farms and replication by researchers. We developed a low-cost, open-source modular harvesting robot based on Raspberry Pi 5 and a 3D-printed manipulator. The system has three modules. First, an improved YOLOv13n detector combines GhostConv, ReLU6, and DIoU Loss. It reaches 96.9% mAP@0.5 for fruits and 95.1% for peduncles with 2.35 M parameters. Compared with the YOLOv13n baseline, parameters and GFLOPs drop by 4.1% and 3.2%, while overall mAP@0.5 falls by 1.8 percentage points. Second, an adaptive size measurement and multi-criteria decision strategy uses the correlation between median depth and tilt angle (R2 = 0.824), giving a mean absolute error of 5.0 mm and a 95.4% effective hit rate. Third, a ROS 2-based full-stack platform enables closed-loop perception–decision–execution. Laboratory tests give a selected-target harvesting success rate of 95.4% (103/108) and an overall success rate of 85.8% (103/120), with 1.9% fruit damage. Motion planning and execution consume 83% of cycle time. All hardware designs, ROS 2 packages, and model weights are released.

candidates.title: PoET²S: Folding a digital twin into validator selection for blockchain consensus in peer-to-peer energy trading
candidates.abstract: Blockchain platforms for peer-to-peer energy trading often add a digital twin that forecasts each meter's generation and demand. In most designs the twin only raises alarms, while validators are still chosen by stake or computation. The proposed scheme, PoET²S, incorporates the twin's evidence into validator selection: a node's weight is a stake-and-energy term multiplied by its Twin-Trust Score raised to γ = 2.5, so nodes that contradict the physical forecast quickly lose committee seats. A discrete-event simulator compares PoET²S (500 nodes, 15% Byzantine, 30 paired seeds) with seven classical baselines and three design points from recent work: a binary veto, an additive energy-and-trust score, and a linear (γ = 1) reputation weight. Detection is a near-tie: PoET²S catches 91.0% of attackers and the veto 91.7%. PoET²S raises more false alarms per catch by default (13.9 against 9.7) but matches the veto's catch rate at equal false-alarm cost. The malicious committee share is 10.8% under the veto, 3.8% under the linear weight, and 2.6% under PoET²S, and on 100 seeds the gain over the linear weight is 37% (Holm-adjusted p = 7.2 × 10⁻⁹). At 45% Byzantine nodes, the one-third fault bound fails in 64.4% of veto blocks and 2.4% of PoET²S blocks. Simulated commit latency (30.2 ms) is higher than for Proof of Stake and Delegated Proof of Stake, lower than for Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance, and flat up to 4,000 nodes; an optional fast path lowers it to 26.8 ms. Against Sybil attacks, top-K selection needs certified meter identities.

candidates.title: FROM DESTINATION ANTHROPOMORPHISM TO SELF-DESTINATION CONNECTION: AN INTEGRATIVE FRAMEWORK FOR TOURIST–PLACE RELATIONSHIPS IN NATURE-BASED TOURISM
candidates.abstract: Tourism research increasingly recognizes destinations as psychologically meaningful relational objects rather than merely bundles of attributes and services. Yet research on destination anthropomorphism, identity-based destination connection, place attachment, and psychological ownership has largely evolved in parallel, leaving unclear how a destination perceived as human-like may become incorporated into tourists’ self-concepts and subsequently develop into deeper relational bonds. This focused integrative review develops the Humanization–Identification–Relationship (HIR) Framework and organizes the evidence directly around four research questions. A controlled evidence-selection workflow assembled 36 full-text reports across four complementary search streams; five duplicate copies were removed, 31 unique reports were assessed for eligibility, one contextually peripheral report was excluded, and 30 studies were retained for thematic synthesis. Findings show that destination humanization is enabled by environmental, experiential, symbolic, communicative, and person-level conditions; that identity, attachment, nature relatedness, and psychological ownership are related but non-equivalent mechanisms; that direct evidence connecting destination anthropomorphism with Self-Destination Connection (SDC) remains limited; and that relational states are consistently associated with environmentally responsible behavior, conservation support, loyalty, advocacy, citizenship behavior, recommendation, and revisit intention. The HIR Framework therefore treats Humanization, Identification, and Relationship as analytically distinct but potentially connected domains. SDC is positioned as a theoretically plausible identity-internalization bridge rather than an established mediator. The review contributes by distinguishing empirically supported pathways from propositional transitions and by specifying a testable research agenda for explaining how socially humanized destinations may become self-relevant and relationally consequential in nature-based tourism.

candidates.title: Wellness Robots and the Path to Full Autonomy
candidates.abstract: This paper introduces the autonomous wellness robot as a distinct category of socially assistive system, defined by its capacity to continuously assess and respond across the seven ICAA dimensions of wellness (see Figure 2). We propose the Care Robot Autonomy Scale (CRAS): a six-level taxonomy (L0-L5) modeled on the automotive automation standard SAE J3016 and evaluated across four wellness-aligned dimensions. We present Ryan, developed initially at the University of Denver and commercialized by DreamFace Technologies, as a case study. NIH/NIA-funded longitudinal evidence (N = 18; 887 hours) shows statistically significant cognitive improvement (SLUMS +2.61, p = 0.015) and a clinically meaningful directional reduction in depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 -2.50, p = 0.073), with no novelty effect. We position Ryan today at CRAS Level 1-2, with emerging Level 3 capabilities in some dimensions, and outline a three-phase roadmap to L5 (full autonomy) by the early 2030s.

candidates.title: Fit4MedRob: design and preliminary validation of a modular robotic framework for hemispatial inattention rehabilitation
candidates.abstract: The Fit4MedRob initiative (“Fit for Medical Robotics”) is a large-scale project funded by the Italian Ministry of University and Research under the Italian Complementary National Plan, involving 25 partners across academia, clinical centers, and industry. Within this framework, Mission 2 – Activity 5 (Match-Making #53) focuses on the development of robotic solutions for the rehabilitation of post-stroke hemispatial inattention (HI), a condition characterized by impaired awareness of one side of space. This work presents the design and preliminary validation of a modular robotic framework based on the TIAGo platform, a collaborative mobile manipulator developed by PAL Robotics. The proposed architecture integrates six functional modules: Navigation, Patient Identification, Patient Interaction, Patient Monitoring, Exercise Delivery, and Evaluation. The system is designed to support structured rehabilitation sessions while enabling the acquisition of quantitative sensor-based measurements. Preliminary validation was conducted with healthy participants under controlled conditions and focused on selected technological components of the framework, including autonomous navigation, patient identification, speech-based interaction, markerless head-orientation estimation, and upper-limb motion tracking. Ground-truth kinematic measurements were obtained using a stereophotogrammetric system where applicable. Navigation enabled the robot to establish an interaction configuration compatible with subsequent identification, although systematic differences were observed between onboard and reference estimates of subject distance and alignment. Patient identification was successfully achieved within the intended interaction range, while the speech-based interaction module reached an overall intent-classification accuracy of 92.6%. Markerless head-orientation estimation showed high agreement with the reference system for yaw, whereas larger errors were observed for pitch. Upper-limb tracking captured the main spatial and temporal characteristics of robot-guided movements, although angular alignment showed greater variability.

candidates.title: Agibot: An Open-Source Modular Swerve-Drive Robot Platform for Agricultural Robotics Research and Education
candidates.abstract: Agricultural production faces persistent labor shortages and increasing demand for automation, yet progress in agricultural robotics remains constrained by the limited availability of affordable, flexible, and accessible research platforms. This paper presents Agibot, an open-source, modular, low-cost agricultural robotics platform designed for autonomy research and experimentation, with potential applications in hands-on robotics education. The platform integrates four-wheel independent swerve drive, swappable computing, distributed embedded control, multimodal sensing, and configurable manipulation within a unified sense-plan-act-verify framework supporting perception, control, navigation, manipulation, and autonomous task verification. The platform was evaluated through representative row-crop navigation and manipulation tasks under varying lighting and soil conditions. Experiments demonstrated reliable lane following, autonomous row-to-row navigation, target identification, seed dispensing, plant manipulation, and closed-loop verification of task success. Its modular architecture supports independent testing, modification, and validation of autonomy components for rapid prototyping and experimentation. These proof-of-concept tasks, controller-tuning studies, and integrated trials demonstrate the platform's research capabilities, while its accessible and reconfigurable design supports its use for hands-on robotics education. By combining affordability, modularity, open-source accessibility, configurable manipulation, and end-to-end sense-plan-act-verify autonomy, Agibot provides a practical platform for agricultural robotics research, technology development, and workforce training.

candidates.title: Construction of Adolescent Self-Identity in K-Pop Artist Roleplay: A Phenomenological Study of NCT Dream Premium Roleplayer Account Users on Telegram
candidates.abstract: Roleplayer activities provide adolescents with a space to explore and make sense of sexual identity through characters and relationships in digital spaces. In the NCT Dream Premium roleplayer community on Telegram, this process can be seen through the use of K-Pop idols as face claims and BxB (Boy x Boy) shipping practices. This study aims to understand the construction of adolescent sexual identity through experiences of engaging in roleplayer activities using NCT Dream face claims on Telegram Premium. Using a qualitative approach and Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA), data were collected through in-depth interviews with six informants and analyzed using open coding, axial coding, and selective coding. Stuart Hall identity construction theory served as the primary theoretical foundation, supported by Jenkins’ fandom concept and Boyd affordance concept. The findings show that sexual identity is constructed through creating spaces and characters, self-expression, relationships and safety, and reflection on sexual identity. It is shaped by experiences and interactions within the roleplayer community rather than by the face claim itself.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence and Media: Assessing the Risks and Rewards
candidates.abstract: Exploring how artifical intelligence (AI) technologies— from generative AI (GenAI) to robotics—are reshaping the media landscape, this groundbreaking text critically examines the nature of AI and its impact on journalism, media, and society. In this timely analysis, John V. Pavlik explores the opportunities and challenges of AI integration across the media landscape, from newsrooms to entertainment platforms, offering critical insights into how AI technologies are reshaping content creation, distribution, and public engagement. The book provides readers with a clear and comprehensive understanding of AI's transformative impact on media by offering accessible explanations of complex AI concepts and applications, evidence-based analysis of current AI implementations in journalism and entertainment, a critical examination of ethical challenges and regulatory frameworks, and practical insights into GenAI, robotics, and emerging media technologies. Featuring case studies and real-world examples from across journalism, film and television, social media, and beyond, the book offers invaluable insight into the practical application of AI technologies and an overall understanding of the risks and rewards surrounding AI-driven media. This book will be essential reading for students and scholars of media, journalism, and communication studies, as well as media professionals seeking to understand AI's impact on their field. It also offers crucial insights for policymakers involved in media regulation and AI governance.

candidates.title: Selective attention or inattention? Enabling efficient perception in embodied intelligence agents
candidates.abstract: Abstract As embodied intelligence increasingly operates in the physical world, perception efficiency, robustness, and adaptability become central bottlenecks separating artificial agents from biological organisms. Unlike conventional perception pipelines, biological perception is inherently selective and resource-aware: attention amplifies task-relevant information, while inattention suppresses distraction and redundancy. This survey investigates attention-driven adaptive perception as a promising mechanism for improving embodied systems. We consolidate interdisciplinary findings from neuroscience, cognitive science, robotics, and machine learning to clarify the distinct yet complementary roles of selective attention and inattention in optimizing perceptual processing. Building on these insights, we introduce the Unified Selective Attention and Inattention Model (U-SAIM) and extend it into a three-tier architectural framework that maps biological principles to embodied perception systems. Guided by this structure, we review existing implementations across robotics, multimodal fusion, lightweight perception, and attention modulation strategies, extracting design patterns and performance implications. Moreover, we discuss the challenges and opportunities for future development. Together, these perspectives chart a unified theoretical and practical roadmap toward attentional embodied perception—agents capable of perceiving, reasoning, and acting with the adaptive intelligence, efficiency, and flexibility that define human perception.

candidates.title: A STATEWIDE EVALUATION OF LOW-VALUE IBC USAGE AND ITS IMPLICATIONS FOR CTE PROGRAMMING
candidates.abstract: Industry-Based Certifications (IBCs) have emerged as a significant element of the Career and Technical Education (CTE) accountability models for Texas high schools, especially within the College, Career, and Military Readiness (CCMR) framework. Nevertheless, concerns have grown about the labor-market worth, equity considerations, and accountability use of low-value certifications. In this study, the patterns of IBC use across the state were evaluated and their associations with CTE programming, accountability policy, and student readiness indicators were examined. The study was based on the Improvement Science framework; it had a quantitative descriptive and longitudinal research design that was conducted with analysis conducted in JASP and Python. The dataset was a combination of statewide IBC master records, district accountability datasets, CCMR indicators, regional certification counts, and program-level workforce pathway data from 2022-2025. The results showed that the value of approved certifications is unevenly distributed across the statewide IBC list. Among the 474 current certifications on the 2025–2030 accountability list, Tier 1 credentials, those most strongly aligned with high-wage, high demand occupations constituted only 4.9% (n = 23), while Tier 2 credentials dominated at 73.6% (n = 349) and Tier 3 accounted for 21.5% (n = 102). A chi-square goodness-of-fit test confirmed that this distribution departs significantly from uniformity, χ² (2, N = 474) = 2 366.09, p < .001, indicating constrained access to the most valuable credentials. Analysis of multi-cycle list data showed that certification sunsetting is a recurring feature of the system: comparable cohorts of roughly 60 certifications were phased out at successive cycle transitions, while the approved list expanded substantially across cycles, from 207 certifications (2019-2022) to 294 (2022-2024) to 474 (2025-2030). Persistent demographic inequalities were also evident. Non-economically disadvantaged students significantly outperformed economically disadvantaged students within the same districts (mean gap = .164, t(921) = 36.40, p < .001, Cohen’s dₖ = 1.20, a very large effect, and special education students performed lowest of all (dₖ = 1.52 relative to economically disadvantaged peers). Regional variation was also significant, F(19, 999) = 3.64, p < .001, η² = .065. A composite equity-adjusted index and a Pareto decomposition across the 20 regions showed that regional standing reorders substantially once the evenness of readiness is weighed alongside its level, and that each region’s readiness shortfall concentrates in roughly three student groups. A pathway-substitution analysis further showed that the college-ready route dominates for every student group in every region and that access to the certification pathway is lowest for the same groups that trail on college readiness. Although the study originated as an examination of credential value, equity in access to readiness pathways emerged as its most significant system-level concern: the subgroup disparities were the largest and most statistically robust effects observed and were stable across cohorts. Taken together, the findings indicate that Texas CTE accountability systems may benefit from weighing credential value and equitable access alongside certification counts rather than treating all certifications as equivalent. Consistent with the study’s diagnostic, non-causal design, these results are interpreted as system-level patterns rather than demonstrated causal effects. Policy implications to consider include refining IBC tiering, monitoring subgroup access to high-value pathways, and supporting districts through 3 accountability transitions.

candidates.title: The collective turn in DIY: doing it together as cultural resistance in an age of polycrisis
candidates.abstract: Launched in April 2023, DIY, Alternative Cultures & Society has quickly established itself as a pivotal platform for scholarship on do-it-yourself (DIY) from around the world.Contributions to the journal have come from authors in Europe, Africa, Asia, Oceania and North and South America.In addition to featuring the work of established authors, we have published articles by many emerging scholars, thereby furthering the journal's mission of advancing DIY studies as a dynamic and continually evolving field of research.Across the four volumes of DIY published to date, there have been three special issues, focusing respectively on the Global South, austerity and precarity, and fanzines, and a fourth, on DIY in arts education, is scheduled for December 2027.Such varied themes underscore the role of the journal in both responding to and facilitating the rapid diversification of DIY studies.A further key aspect of the journal's mission has been to broaden the understanding of DIY and alternative cultures in a way that continues to embrace established perspectives on DIY, such as resistance, activism and protest, while also introducing newer ones, including creative citizenship, equity and social justice, economic and environmental sustainability, space and place, and wellbeing and mental health.The practice of DIY has been a deeply embedded aspect of human societies for centuries.Initially born of necessity, in a world that predated capitalism and its concomitant forms of mass production, DIY has in more recent times become an alternative to capitalist production and to the mass dissemination of commercially produced goods and services.Although such contemporary DIY sensibilities are frequently tied to the emergence of punk in the late 1970s, McKay (2024) argues, in an article written specifically for this journal, that such a straightforward association oversimplifies the reach of DIY in both the pre-and post-punk eras.Likewise, although punk proved highly influential in shaping a particular discourse of DIY and its political economy during the late 1970s and early 1980s, current renderings of DIY do not necessarily share punk's polemical reading of DIY as a wholesale rejection of mainstream ideologies (Bennett, 2018;Bennett and Guerra, 2019;Guerra, 2018).Rather, in an era characterised by intersecting political, economic, environmental and pandemic crises, key dimensions of what Henig and Knight (2023) term the 'polycrisis', DIY has evolved into a broad platform for a plethora of activities in which discourses of resistance merge with an emphasis on tolerance and equity, and with support for a range of causes that seek to promote social

candidates.title: Para-authenticity, ontological flexibility, and ontological detachment: how creatives construct and manage virtual endorsers
candidates.abstract: Research on virtual endorsers has largely focused on consumers, leaving the creative strategies behind their development underexplored. This study examines how creatives construct and manage the authenticity of virtual influencers and brand ambassadors while navigating an evolving ethical landscape. Based on in-depth interviews with eleven practitioners, our findings suggest they deliberately construct virtual personas plausibly situated in recognizable social and material worlds despite their artificiality. To manage the tension between brand control and perceived relatability, practitioners integrate imperfections and contextual cues to evoke para-authenticity – a strategic illusion of plausibility. We also explore the business case for virtual endorsers and how practitioners navigate ethical complexities through strategic disclosure, ontological flexibility (the capacity to vary an endorser’s form), and ontological detachment (the ethically ambivalent use of such flexibility to move beyond human embodiment and its associated demographic categories). Overall, this study reframes authenticity as a strategic construction in a synthetic advertising landscape.

candidates.title: Robots in the City: Persona-Based Perceptions of Urban Robots
candidates.abstract: Pedestrians increasingly encounter robots in urban public spaces without interacting with them, but how robots change the perceived safety of a street remains unclear. We examine how robot presence and type affect perceived safety across urban contexts. We generate 18 images of Seoul streets that vary in time of day, road class, and robot condition (no robot, a delivery robot, or a humanoid). Two multimodal large language models (MLLMs), Qwen3.8-27B and Gemma4-26B, each conditioned on 500 synthetic personas, choose the safer image in each pair, and 25 human respondents complete the same task. Both models prefer streets without robots and favor the delivery robot over the humanoid. Robots are chosen more often at night and less often by older personas, whereas road class has smaller effects. In the model rationales, the delivery robot appears as a physical obstacle, whereas the humanoid appears as either a threat or a source of protection. Like humans, both models chose robots more often at night, but chose the humanoid over the delivery robot far less often, and Gemma showed a night effect for the humanoid about three times that of humans. These results show that the effect of a robot on perceived safety depends on when it appears, and that persona-conditioned MLLMs capture only part of human judgments.

candidates.title: Mapalus Social Wisdom in the Digital Era: Ranoketang On Village, Southeast Minahasa
candidates.abstract: Village digitalization raises a fundamental question for communities whose solidarity depends on collective work and physical presence. Previous studies have treated Mapalus, the mutual-aid institution of the Minahasa people, as either a declining or a revitalized heritage, while studies of digital mutual aid have rarely examined how a local worldview governs technology use. This study analyzes how Mapalus operates as a structure that guides the digital practices of residents of Ranoketang Atas Village, Southeast Minahasa Regency, and how these practices reproduce or transform it. Using a qualitative case study framed by Giddens's structuration theory, data were collected between July and September 2026 through in-depth interviews with 14 purposively selected informants, including village officials, customary and church leaders, heads of funeral, farming, and savings-and-loan Mapalus groups, digital-native youth, and ordinary members. Reflexive thematic analysis was applied, verified through triangulation and member checking. The values of Si Tou Timou Tumou Tou, torang samua basudara, reciprocity, and equality function as rules of signification and legitimation that determine how WhatsApp, Facebook, bank transfers, and e-wallets may be used. Digitalization strengthens speed, outreach to migrant residents, financial transparency, and youth involvement, but loosens shared meals and physical presence; residents counter this through the norm that “a group message is not Mapalus” and through face-to-face rituals. The effect is uneven: transferable resources (money, information) gain most, whereas embodied resources (labor, presence) are most vulnerable. The study proposes a three-layer hybrid Mapalus model of core values, digital channels, and rituals of presence. Unlike earlier hybridization accounts, the model explains which dimensions strengthen or loosen and why. It extends structuration theory by showing that a local worldview filters how technology is enacted, that the duality of structure is conditional on the type of resource mediated, and that faceless digital trust is re-embedded through facework.

candidates.title: For You, Not for Everyone: Bystander-Aware Delivery of Critical Feedback in Robot Tutoring
candidates.abstract: Robots in shared settings may expose information intended for an individual user to nearby bystanders. Robot tutoring makes this concern particularly salient: critical feedback is directed at an individual learner, yet bystanders may overhear or see it. To address this, we compared context-invariant and context-adaptive robot behaviors in a between-subjects study with 40 participants. Following an initial phase without a bystander, a bystander entered the setting. Participants then received two scripted critical feedback messages concerning their pronunciation and handwriting, independent of their actual performance. With the context-invariant behavior, the robot tutor delivered both messages aloud. With the context-adaptive behavior, the robot tutor scanned for the bystander, turned its body and display away after detecting them, gave a spoken attention cue, and presented the same feedback messages silently on its display. Participants rated the robot tutor higher in perceived privacy awareness and perceived social competence in the context-adaptive condition than in the context-invariant condition, while evidence for reduced experienced embarrassment was inconclusive. These findings inform the design and evaluation of robots that respond to bystander presence by adapting how they communicate potentially sensitive information.

candidates.title: LLMs as MDP Designers: A Dependency-Aware Agentic Framework for Automated Robot Policy Generation
candidates.abstract: We investigate the automated generation of executable robot reinforcement learning (RL) policies from natural-language task descriptions. Rather than using large language models (LLMs) as execution-time decision makers, we use them as designers that construct RL pipelines before deployment, including Markov decision process (MDP) formulation and simulator implementation. We identify a phase-wise structure in this problem: MDP formulation is dependency-structured and sequential, whereas simulator implementation becomes modular once the formulation is fixed. Based on this structure, we propose ARPG, a dependency-aware agentic framework that performs sequential MDP modeling, localized verification and correction, and simulator-structured implementation while externalizing intermediate artifacts. ARPG targets a key failure mode of automated policy generation: executable code may still yield non-learnable policies when state, action, reward, and termination artifacts are not semantically aligned. Experiments in Isaac Sim show that ARPG improves modeling correctness, environment executability, and policy-generation success compared with monolithic LLM baselines and off-the-shelf agentic systems. Additional demonstrations on custom robotics, standard RL, and engineering-domain MDPs further suggest that the same modeling pipeline can be reused beyond the main benchmark suite.

candidates.title: Smart Robotic Inspection of Levees and Culverts: A Scoping Review of Robotic Platforms, Sensing Technologies, AI Methods, and Multi-Robot Coordination for Flood-Control Infrastructure
candidates.abstract: Abstract Earthen levees, dikes, flood-control embankments, culverts, and stormwater drainage conduits represent vital lifelines for mitigating catastrophic inun-dation in urban and rural watersheds. However, conventional manual walk-downs and tethered closed-circuit television (CCTV) surveys remain severely labor-intensive, hazardous, subjective, and difficult to scale across vegetated, flooded, submerged, and GPS-denied environments. Autonomous robotics, multimodal remote sensing, deep-learning-based computer vision, and multi-robot coordination offer transformative opportunities to enhance inspection frequency, spatial accuracy, and maintenance decision-making. Following the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), this study maps the multidisciplinary land-scape across six major scholarly databases: Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar (2010–2026). Out of 1,860 initially retrieved records, 1,314 unique studies were screened, 212 full texts were assessed, and 64 primary empirical studies were systemati-cally synthesized. We chart the evidence across seven interconnected the-matic streams: (1) unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) corridor surveying; (2) unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) and pipe crawlers; (3) amphibious and autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs/ROVs); (4) multimodal sensor fusion (RGB, thermal infrared, LiDAR, sonar, and GPR); (5) deep learning for defect detection and semantic segmentation; (6) degraded-environment SLAM and GPS-denied navigation; and (7) multi-robot coordination, com-munication relays, and digital-twin maintenance integration. Quantitative findings show that while aerial thermal/RGB levee inspection and in-pipe YOLO/U-Net defect detection achieve high localized accuracy (mAP ex-ceeding 75–86%, segmentation IoU > 0.71), end-to-end systems integration remains scarce. Only 10.9% (n = 7) of the literature validates heterogeneous multi-domain robot teams in operational flood-control environments, and fewer than 5% close the loop from automated anomaly detection to predic-tive maintenance prioritization. To bridge these gaps, we propose a resilient six-tier reference architecture for communication-aware, heterogeneous robot teams and establish a concrete ten-point research agenda for operational flood-control infrastructure management.

candidates.title: Exploring Proximity and Tactile Sensing for Robotic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Pre-touch sensing, or sensing information about an object before contact, is an attractive modality for robot hands as it can allow a robot to anticipate and respond to a contact before it happens. In this work, we introduce ToFTouch, a multimodal tactile sensor combining three multizone (4$\times$4 resolution) time-of-flight sensors with an optics-based pressure sensing array. We mount this sensor on a parallel jaw gripper and demonstrate its utility on three distinct tasks: (i) pre-grasp adjustment, (ii) item extraction from clutter, and (iii) item insertion into tight spaces. For pre-grasp adjustment, ToF feedback reduced cycle time by 7.4$\%$ by enabling anticipatory gripper closure during approach. For extraction, ToF sensing enabled successful retrieval across all tested depth offsets ($\pm$2 cm) deviating from the nominal pick point, including conditions where baseline approaches failed, with standard deviations below 0.4 cm. For insertion into dense clutter, we explore the proximity and tactile information provided from ToFTouch during an insertion trajectory. The results demonstrate the utility of multizone ToF sensing in a manipulation environment.

candidates.title: Religious Conflict and Coexistence in Korea
candidates.abstract: This Reprint brings together a set of essays that examine the question of religious conflict and coexistence in the Korean context. Using a range of disciplinary perspectives, the contributions offer fresh insights into both longstanding and emerging issues in the study of religion, including shamanic rituals and cosmologies, ecumenical engagement, interreligious dialogue, the dynamics of religion and politics, religious art, Confucian ritual and its interpretation, and the religious dimensions of space and time. Despite their thematic and methodological diversity, the essays share a common concern with how religion in Korea, both historical and contemporary, responds to changing and often challenging conditions. These responses take multiple forms: epistemological and behavioral adjustments, the development of new institutional and ritual configurations, the articulation of idealized values through aesthetic media, and the reconfiguration of spatial meanings. Taken together, the volume highlights the creativity and vitality of religious traditions in Korea as they engage an evolving social and cultural milieu.

candidates.title: Digital Technology and Artistic Interventions for Rural Revitalization in China
candidates.abstract: China’s rapid urbanization continues to exert structural pressures on agriculture, rural communities, and farmers. The practice of artistic intervention in rural communities – yishu xiangjian – has shifted since the mid-2000s from avant-garde experiments to a nationwide multistakeholder movement. Under the Digital China initiative, this movement now encompasses blockchain-traced ancient tea forests, algorithmically enhanced village football tournaments, and points-based governance platforms, among others. This chapter examines three empirically grounded pathways through which digital technologies mediate rural cultural practice: the digital preservation of intangible heritage, integrated urban–rural cultural tourism scenarios, and digitally enabled governance for civilized rural customs. Our analysis suggests that technological empowerment reconfigures community relationships and advances institutional adaptation toward esthetic governance, but simultaneously subjects rural agency to platform metrics, algorithmic visibility, and financialized assetization. China’s experience offers a Global South model of postagricultural civilization that integrates ecological concerns, vernacular creativity, and community governance with advanced digital infrastructure; however, its sustainability depends on negotiating the tension between flexible connectivity and digital sovereignty. Technology functions not only as an instrumental tool but also as a contested mediator connecting locality with globality, cultural inheritance with modernization, and rural subjects with expanded yet uneven horizons of participatory cultural practice.

candidates.title: Lost in the Repository: A Standardized Inventory of Open-Source Agricultural Digital Solutions
candidates.abstract: Open-source software and hardware have become important drivers of digital agriculture by providing transparent, adaptable, and cost-effective technologies for precision farming, geospatial analysis, farm management, and decision support. However, these technologies remain fragmented across software repositories, project websites, and institutional platforms, making their discovery, comparison, and reuse challenging. This study presents a curated inventory and standardized characterization of the open-source agricultural digital ecosystem. A total of 191 agricultural digital solutions were identified and characterized using a multidimensional metadata framework describing technology maturity, licensing, connectivity dependency, artificial intelligence capabilities, repository characteristics, and agricultural operational intervention level. The results reveal a diverse collection of agricultural digital technologies comprising complete applications, reusable software components, IoT and interoperability frameworks, geospatial services, and open-hardware technologies. GitHub hosts the majority of the inventoried solutions, while repository analyses reveal substantial variability in community activity, licensing practices, and scientific dissemination. Comparative analyses further demonstrate that high operational intervention level is not exclusively associated with advanced artificial intelligence or continuous cloud connectivity, highlighting the important roles of rule-based automation, scientific modelling, edge computing, and interoperable software components. Beyond the inventory itself, the principal contribution of this work is the proposed classification scheme, which provides a standardized and reproducible methodology for organizing, comparing, and maintaining open-source agricultural technologies. The resulting inventory offers a valuable resource for researchers, developers, policymakers, and funding agencies while supporting future decision-support systems, technology discovery, and more interoperable and sustainable digital agriculture.

candidates.title: ARM-01: an open-source reversible 2-DOF upper-limb rehabilitation robot with internal cable routing and intrinsic safety
candidates.abstract: The rising global incidence of stroke necessitates accessible and effective upper-limb rehabilitation solutions. However, the widespread adoption of commercial rehabilitation robots is often hindered by prohibitive costs, complex setups, exposed wiring hazards, and the financial burden of requiring dedicated left- or right-arm systems. This paper presents ARM-01, a cost-effective, open-source, 2-degree-of-freedom (DOF) rehabilitation robot engineered for passive range-of-motion and predefined trajectory tracking of the shoulder and elbow joints. Built using highly accessible off-the-shelf (OTS) components, 3D-printed parts, standard aluminum profiles, and SUS304 stainless steel, the hardware is specifically designed for straightforward replication. To maximize economic viability and clinical adaptability, the ARM-01 features a tool-free reversible mechanism, allowing a single unit to seamlessly alternate between left- and right-side upper-limb rehabilitation. Furthermore, the system incorporates a hollow-shaft internal cable-routing strategy that reduces exposed wiring and associated entanglement risks. Biomechanical alignment between the robot and the user's glenohumeral joint is facilitated through a combination of a mobile base and a motorized lifting column, enabling convenient adjustment of the robot's position relative to the user. The system's hierarchical control architecture integrates a ROS2-based backend with an intuitive Unity 3D human-machine interface (HMI), facilitating tailored trajectory execution, real-time spatial monitoring, and multi-layered safety protocols. Comprehensive kinematic modeling, workspace simulation, and static load analyses theoretically evaluate the system's actuator torque adequacy and safety boundaries. Successful operational testing in a controlled laboratory setting demonstrates the prototype's basic operational feasibility under non-clinical conditions, offering the research community an adaptable and reproducible platform for further development of upper-limb rehabilitation technologies.

candidates.title: Closer, Not Just More Credible: How Parasocial Interaction Explains Consumer Responses to Virtual and Human Influencers
candidates.abstract: concentrated on Europe, Asia Pacific and North America [12], and responses to VIs depend on the cultural setting [13].To address these questions, this study compares VIs and HIs on trustworthiness, expertise, attractiveness and authenticity among Lithuanian consumers.It tests two routes to purchase intention (PI): a credibility route, through which source characteristics make the message believable (message credibility, MC), and a relational route through PSI.The study extends source credibility research on VIs with a relational explanation and gives brands evidence for choosing between the two influencer types.The remainder of the paper is structured as follows.Section 2 reviews the literature and develops the hypotheses, Section 3 describes the method, Section 4 discusses the findings and their implications, and Section 5 concludes.

candidates.title: Designing Immersive Learning Experiences: Teaching Robotics Programming in Virtual 3D Environments
candidates.abstract: This article presents a teaching scenario using virtual environments, often referred to as part of the ‘metaverse’, to address educational challenges highlighted during the COVID-19 pandemic. The increasing shift to online learning environments emphasizes the need for flexible, anytime-anywhere access to education. Virtual 3D environments offer a level of immersion that surpasses traditional online formats, such as video conferencing, and enable innovative didactic concepts, including collaborative group activities. To illustrate these benefits, we showcase a case study involving the simulation of robot programming within a virtual 3D environment. Additionally, the integration of personal assistants, such as conversational or pedagogical agents, is explored as a means to alleviate teachers' workloads. Advances in artificial intelligence have made natural language interactions with these agents highly effective, further enhancing the potential of virtual 3D environments in educational contexts. Keywords: e-learning, e-teaching, immersion, virtual 3D rooms, gamification, cyber-physical systems

candidates.title: Present Drawing: Exploring Avatar-Mediated Drawing Events with Physical Traces
candidates.abstract: We introduce Present Drawing, an approach for staging an avatar-mediated drawing event that leaves physical traces in the real world. Present Drawing aims to reconfigure conventional drawing events by relaxing their physical constraints. We describe an organizer-oriented design space for such an event along four elements: Time, Site, Control Source, and Avatar Embodiment. To ground this concept, we developed a proof-of-concept prototype in which an observer wears a head-mounted display to view an avatar. The avatar’s motion is synchronized with a customized pen plotter whose mechanical parts are hidden from the observer. We also developed five application examples spanning live, playback, multi-site, mascot, and system-controlled configurations. We conducted an initial evaluation of one representative playback autograph configuration, showing the basic plausibility of the core Present Drawing experience as an avatar-mediated drawing event and highlighting factors associated with perceiving the avatar as the drawer.

candidates.title: Revisiting the Uncanny Valley in the AI Era: A Review of Visual Artifacts and Aesthetic Perceptions in AI-Generated Characters
candidates.abstract: The rapid evolution of generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly diffusion-based image synthesis models, has fundamentally transformed digital character design and visual storytelling. However, the frequent occurrence of "visual artifacts"—such as anatomical distortions, unnatural skin smoothness, rigid facial expressions, and latent space blending—presents significant aesthetic and psychological challenges. This paper provides a critical, multidisciplinary review that re-examines the classic "Uncanny Valley" hypothesis within the contemporary context of AI-generated media. Moving beyond the conventional engineering perspective that views these artifacts merely as technical deficiencies to be eliminated, this study investigates their potential reinterpretation through the lenses of post-digital media art, glitch aesthetics, and visual semiotics. We analyze how audience perception, cognitive friction, and emotional engagement are affected by these synthetic cues. Furthermore, we explore how human designers utilize advanced node-based control frameworks (e.g., ComfyUI, ControlNet) to negotiate, fix, or intentionally embrace these algorithmic anomalies. Finally, we establish a conceptual framework for human-AI co-creation and highlight future research trajectories for character narrative design in generative media.

candidates.title: FabDreamer: Exploring the Image-to-Physical Workflow Through AI-Assisted Layered Fabrication
candidates.abstract: Generative AI lets anyone create rich visual content in seconds, yet translating that content into a physically fabricable artifact still demands manual decomposition, occlusion repair, and structural verification that most tools leave entirely to the user. We present FabDreamer, an image-to-physical system that carries an image to fabrication-ready SVGs through three stages with deliberately staged AI initiative: (1) AI leads decomposition into depth-ordered layers, (2) assists on demand during creative editing with real-time 3D preview, and (3) advises on structural integrity before export. We instantiate this workflow for layered laser-cut art and evaluate it through three rounds including a formative analysis, an early prototype user evaluation (N=13), and a cross-domain practitioner study with specialists from 6 fabrication domains (N=6). Our findings show that physical awareness during design opens creative opportunities beyond error prevention, that practitioners appropriate the system’s generic geometric operations for their own domains, and that the fabrication agent covers geometry-readable constraints while domain knowledge remains with the maker.

candidates.title: K-Pop Hegemony and Ambivalent Digital Resistance: A Critical Discourse Analysis of the SEAblings–Knetz Conflict
candidates.abstract: Cultural hegemony and digital resistance intersect in the 2026 SEAblings–Knetz conflict, a transnational online dispute between Southeast Asian and South Korean netizens concerning racism, cultural superiority, and K-Pop fandom. Drawing on Gramsci’s theory of hegemony, Bourdieu’s concept of symbolic violence, and Fairclough’s Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA), this study examines how K-Pop operates as both global popular culture and a mechanism of symbolic domination in digital communication. Using a qualitative approach, the study analyzes comments, hashtags, viral posts, and memes circulated on X, TikTok, and Instagram between January and March 2026. The findings reveal that social media platforms function as contested discursive arenas where engagement-driven circulation amplifies racial stereotypes, conflict narratives, and nationalist sentiment. Racist discourse targeting Southeast Asian netizens reflects asymmetrical power relations associated with the global dominance of Korean popular culture. In response, SEAblings mobilized digital solidarity, counter-discourses, boycott campaigns, and platform-based activism. However, this resistance remains ambivalent, as some counter-discourses reproduce the stereotyping and symbolic violence they challenge. Theoretically, this study extends CDA-based research on cultural hegemony by demonstrating how domination and resistance coexist within digital discourse, challenging binary understandings of online activism. Practically, the findings highlight the importance of platform moderation, media literacy, and ethically reflexive fandom practices in addressing symbolic violence within transnational fan communities.
