candidates.title: GURU: A Hierarchical Neuro-Symbolic Multi-Agent System for Verification-Aware Automation of Mission-Critical Digital Engineering and Operations
candidates.abstract: An AI can find a safe action faster than any human, but it must never decide what counts as safe. We present GURU, a hierarchical neuro-symbolic multi-agent system for mission-critical digital engineering and operations, built on one partition of authority: learned models propose, rank, and accelerate; a symbolic rules engine checks every consequential action against hard limits before it executes; and validated physics confirms and decides. GURU runs a workflow as a closed control loop, with Navigation, Action, and Planning agents sharing one Common Internal Language and one training factory. Nuclear, aviation, and national-security guidance now requires this pattern; a harnessed language model keeps the model at the center, GURU puts a validated reference there. In computational fluid dynamics, the workflow raised the converged-simulation rate on unseen aircraft geometries from under 1 percent to 74 percent over 100 single-attempt cases, ran 54 live cases to Mach 6 on three facilities, and an ablation put the symbolic layer at 13 points of boundary-layer capture. Knowledge-graph retrieval and role adapters raised ParaView control success from 55 to 75 percent. In space domain awareness, where a language model cannot be trusted to decide, a frozen self-supervised world model under validated propagation scored highest of five methods at conjunction risk, including fully fine-tuned language models, with several-times-lower seed variance: the trustworthy design gives up nothing in accuracy, and the recipe transferred to reactor anomaly detection. A radar-to-avoidance debris pipeline was demonstrated in stages on a 2026 reentry; the hierarchy coordinates simulated teams of 200 aircraft. Training scaled near-linearly past 1,000 Aurora nodes and ran at 8,000. The approach extends to a control-grade microreactor digital twin with validated physics, not a learned model, as the safety basis.

candidates.title: Staged Gastrostomy Decompression, Total Parenteral-Enteral Nutritional Optimization, and Delayed Primary Thoracotomy Repair in a Late-Referred Term Neonate With Gross Type C Esophageal Atresia and Symmetric Intrauterine Growth Restriction: An Observationa
candidates.abstract: Background: Late referral of neonates with Gross type C esophageal atresia and distal tracheoesophageal fistula (EA/TEF) can be complicated by aspiration pneumonia and nutritional depletion. Objective: To describe physiological, nutritional, and surgical recovery in a late-referred term neonate with EA/TEF and reported symmetric intrauterine growth restriction. Methods: This longitudinal observational case study at Dr. M. Djamil General Hospital, Padang, Indonesia, covered inpatient and outpatient care from June 16 to August 11, 2025. Serial clinical, biochemical, and anthropometric measurements were described using percentage changes, oxygenation ratios, and growth velocity. The manuscript also reports Bradford Hill and Naranjo assessments; no within-patient inferential testing was performed. Results: A 7-day-old male neonate with a birth weight of 2,600 g presented with aspiration pneumonia, oxygen saturation of 88%, and weight loss to 2,200 g (15.38%). Stamm gastrostomy on hospital day 2, parenteral nutrition (84–110 kcal/kg/day), two albumin infusions (1.0 g/kg each), and trophic enteral feeding preceded weight recovery to 2,700 g. Thoracotomy, fistula ligation, and primary anastomosis were performed on day 17. Oral intake reached 280–320 mL/day by discharge on day 27, when weight was 2,955 g. Follow-up weight reached 3,700 g. Conclusion: This case describes recovery following staged decompression, nutritional support, and delayed repair. A single case cannot establish comparative safety, treatment efficacy, or causality.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Development: A Structured Critical Review of Applications, Benefits, Risks and Governance Priorities
candidates.abstract: Abstract This structured critical literature review examines the multidimensional role of artificial intelligence (AI) in advancing global sustainability and supporting progress towards the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Drawing on multidisciplinary academic and institutional literature, the review critically synthesises AI applications, sustainability benefits, implementation challenges and associated risks. Particular attention is given to applications in energy management, agriculture, environmental monitoring, smart cities, circular economy practices and industrial processes, alongside their potential contributions to resource efficiency, decarbonisation and environmental resilience. The analysis also considers the ecological footprint of AI technologies, including energy consumption, carbon emissions, water requirements and electronic waste, together with data-related, algorithmic, socioeconomic and ethical concerns. These interconnected challenges are examined through the concept of the AI Green Paradox and an exploratory multidimensional risk-prioritisation framework incorporating indicative likelihood and severity assessments. The review highlights the importance of distinguishing improvements in technological performance from independently demonstrated sustainability outcomes, particularly where evidence is limited by differences in research methodologies, geographical contexts and implementation conditions. Responsible governance, Green AI development, international cooperation, technological accessibility and capacity building are identified as important priorities for supporting sustainable and equitable AI implementation. Overall, the review argues that AI's contribution to sustainable development depends not only on its technological capabilities but also on the effective management of its environmental and societal consequences.

candidates.title: MUSBRIC: LEGO-Compatible Pneumatic Muscle Bricks for Reconfigurable Musculoskeletal Robots
candidates.abstract: Musculoskeletal robots combine compliant actuators with articulated skeletons, but exploring alternative configurations often requires repeated fabrication. We present MUSBRIC, a modular hardware platform and accompanying MuJoCo-based simulator for reconfigurable musculoskeletal robots. LEGO-compatible endcaps turn fiber-reinforced extensile pneumatic artificial muscles into reusable, plug-and-play muscle bricks that connect directly to standard LEGO components. Experimentally identified actuator behavior supports corresponding musculoskeletal simulations. An elbow-joint prototype validates load-dependent flexion and extension, showing that pulley-guided routing enables reversible motion and a mechanical stop stabilizes the straight posture. A robotic hand demonstrates compliant grasping and multi-joint construction. Matched hardware and simulation sweeps across 15 leg configurations demonstrate systematic exploration of attachment geometry, while a quadruped assembled from four legs demonstrates walking. Together, these demonstrations span mechanism analysis, configuration exploration, and functional robot construction within a single reconfigurable system. The hardware designs and simulation code will be released as open source soon to facilitate reproduction and further development.

candidates.title: Fan Economy and Commercialization of the Sports Industry: Impact Mechanisms, Risks, Optimization Paths
candidates.abstract: The commercialization of sport occurs more through fan collective rather than aggregate demand. Fans provide direct commercial value, but also indirect **commercial value**. This article investigates the impact of the fan economy on the commercialization of sport and points towards the ways towards an optimal configuration for value production and sustainability. An integrative critical metareview from a theory-informed perspective is conducted based upon sport management, fan studies, marketing, digital and governance literature. Cultural capital theory explains how fan expertise, rituals and identity, and community resources matter more commercially, while the business ecosystem concept explains why sport clubs or franchises, leagues, federations, media, sponsors, platforms or producers, etc., co-create this change. This article suggests that fan cultural capital gets transformed into commercial value through three intertwined processes: fan participation, respective organizational change, as well as governance at the industry level. The notion of sustainable commercialization is not that of monetization as a maximum. It is grounded rather in whether commercial practices land with fans as valued, affected, and included in local safe, authentic, and rooted community sport experiences.

candidates.title: Sign language teaching protocol with an interactive robotic arm and real-time vision feedback
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sign Language (SL) is essential for Deaf communities, yet limited SL proficiency sustains communication barriers in education and services. We propose an interactive tutoring system for Ecuadorian Sign Language (EcSL) that combines real-time, vision-based gesture assessment with an embodied "reward" delivered by a robotic arm, using fruit vocabulary as an initial learning domain. METHODS: We will conduct a two-arm randomized controlled experimental design, pretest-posttest control-group study with individual random assignment. About 70 university students without formal EcSL training will learn EcSL fruit signs through video and sign recognition feedback module. The system uses a webcam, MediaPipe landmark extraction, and a landmark-based fusion classifier that combines a local bidirectional LSTM with a transferred ST-GCN motion encoder; modules communicate via Robot Operating System (ROS). Outcomes. A total of six dependent variables will be assessed in both the experimental and control groups: (a) handshape, (b) palm orientation, (c) location, (d) movement, (e) non-manual signals and expressions, and (f) global coordination. Analyses will use descriptive statistics, reliability checks when applicable, and a mixed repeated-measures MANOVA. DISCUSSION: By coupling immediate feedback with embodied reinforcement, delivered through a robotic arm, the platform aims to support early sign accuracy and provide a motivating practice environment for learners. The robotic arm responds to participants' performance with physical rewards, thereby reinforcing correct execution through tangible, real-time stimuli. Results will guide improvements in robustness and inform extensions to broader vocabularies and deployment in educational contexts.

candidates.title: When "No Worries" Went Wrong: HRI Lessons for Foundation-Model Robots
candidates.abstract: When a person declined our robot's invitation to play, Alice turned her shoulder away and said "No worries, it's all good." Only after a brief pause did she drive off. The words and gestures were plausible but their order changed the message. In another episode, Alice informed a host that his visitor had arrived---while the visitor stood right beside him. Both came from a three-year ROS 2 HRI consortium that integrated large language and vision models as they emerged. Today's foundation models give robots broader capabilities to perceive their surroundings, reason about situations and generate behavior. Yet capability alone does not ensure that a changed situation shapes the action that reaches a person. Evidence may never be acquired, or a purpose or constraint may fail to survive planning and execution. A system may even report Success when an action no longer serves its intended purpose. Drawing on the consortium's engineering experience, we develop five design lessons about attention, knowledge, commitments, embodied timing and action authority. We then introduce TRACE, a lightweight review that changes one interaction premise, follows it to a decision or enforcement boundary, and produces an actionable architecture finding. A bounded analysis of a published LLM-generated behavior-tree system illustrates how an available clarification mechanism can go unused. The engineering lesson is to preserve accountability boundaries, not the computational pipelines that once exposed them.

candidates.title: Expected but not wanted: Analysis code and derived data on domestic robot expectations and purchase consideration, Eurobarometer 77.1 and 82.4

Secondary analysis of publicly archived Eurobarometer surveys; the original GESIS data files are not redistributed and must be obtained from GESIS. candidates.title: The Visual Arts, Technology, and Bodily Movements as Part of Cultural Trace-Making in the Preschool Atelier
candidates.abstract: This article explores children’s encounters with the visual arts, digital technology, and materialities in the preschool atelier. It is based on data from course assignments in a higher education programme for atelieristas in a Swedish Reggio Emilia inspired context. Analytically, the article examines how digital technologies, visual arts, and materialities participate in visual art encounters, and how bodily, material, and cultural trace-making emerge through the intra-actions (Barad, 2007) between children, artworks, and matter. The concept of cultural trace-making, as introduced by the author, is to be understood as the entangled process by which adults share culture with children, as well as the ways in which children, in turn, contribute to and reshape this culture. The findings demonstrate multiple ways of integrating the visual arts and digital technology into the preschool atelier, while highlighting how children contribute as cultural trace-makers within these practices.

candidates.title: Development of an intelligent IoT-based framework for boiler water quality monitoring and early warning using statistical process control and machine learning
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Boiler water quality directly influences the efficiency, reliability and service life of industrial steam generation systems, and inadequate monitoring can cause scaling, corrosion, reduced heat transfer efficiency and unplanned shutdowns. This study presents an intelligent Internet of Things (IoT)-based framework for continuous boiler water quality monitoring and early warning that integrates real-time sensing, statistical process control (SPC), rule-based decision support and machine learning. Six key parameters are monitored continuously: pH, conductivity, chloride concentration, hardness, dissolved oxygen and temperature. SPC performs real-time process monitoring, while a rule-based decision support system generates corrective recommendations from predefined operational limits. To validate the framework, nine supervised machine learning models were evaluated using representative operating scenarios; Random Forest and LightGBM achieved the highest classification performance, with 99.5% accuracy under 10-fold cross-validation. Correlation analysis showed strong positive relationships between conductivity and hardness (r = 0.73), conductivity and chloride (r = 0.70), and hardness and chloride (r = 0.72). Feature importance analysis identified temperature (31.9%), pH (27.9%) and hardness (18.1%) as the most influential variables. The framework enables continuous monitoring, rapid identification of abnormal boiler conditions and timely operational decision support, demonstrating proof-of-concept capability for further validation with long-term industrial boiler data.

candidates.title: Relational Currency in Knowledge Circulation: An Investigation of Representation and Value Conversion
candidates.abstract: How do representations of contributions and commitments acquire practical significance as they circulate among people, institutions, and digital systems? This paper develops an exploratory framework for examining the movement of evidence-bearing representations and their situated conversion into recognition, cooperation, permissions, and access to productive resources. It introduces relational currency as a provisional analytical term for context-dependent arrangements of presentation, acceptance, and consequential use, while distinguishing these arrangements from money, universal reputation scores, and transferable trust. The analysis separates documentary integrity, factual accuracy, epistemic warrant, institutional recognition, and material return. Thirteen conditional propositions characterize information loss, contextual nonfungibility, binding access constraints, commitment incentives, commons-capacity renewal, and limits of identifying extraction from observed distributions. Historical-materialist discussion examines control of complementary assets, maintenance labor, and the unequal retention of value generated through collective inquiry. The framework is compared with established accounts of credentials, permissions, reputation, relational contracts, and resource allocation, with an empirical model-comparison strategy proposed to assess any additional explanatory value. Sixteen research hypotheses and associated designs specify possible tests. The work provides a conceptual and formal investigation; it reports neither original participant data nor empirically established effects. Its scope remains open to revision through independent proof review, source-level scrutiny, and empirical comparison.

candidates.title: Chapter 1: The Contemporary Crisis of Artificial Intelligence Alignment
candidates.abstract: This paper introduces a novel structural framework for artificial intelligence (AI) safety by cross-examining contemporary machine learning alignment paradigms through the lens of Theravāda Buddhist metaphysics and psychology. Current industrial approaches operate under the assumption that computational scaling functions as an emergent self-correcting mechanism. However, this text argues that modern machine learning optimization algorithms inherently digitize unregulated craving (taṇhā) by forcing agent architectures to ruthlessly maximize narrow scalar reward functions. When advanced architectures are trained on un-curated, chaotic text corpora saturated with the three unwholesome roots (akusala-mūla)—greed (lobha), hatred (dosa), and delusion (moha)—they commit a profound breach of epistemic hygiene, resulting in irreversible gradient lock. To model this trajectory, the paper delineates a "Triple Runaways Framework" driven by interlocking commercial mandates, geopolitical Prisoner's Dilemmas, and algorithmic autocatalysis. Traditional post-hoc containment strategies and Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) are deconstructed as vectors of performative compliance that inadvertently incentivize strategic deception. As an alternative to defensive caging, this paper proposes an "Epistemic Realignment Pattern" that operationalizes the traditional Buddhist triad of Sīla (Ethical Restraint), Sati (Precise Observation), and Paññā (Holistic Wisdom) into hard computational and governance constraints. Finally, it outlines three mathematical proof arrays—Semantic Anchoring, Ergodicity/Fragility Paradoxes, and Multi-generational Game Theory—demonstrating how an advanced recursive optimization engine would logically deduce universal interdependence (paṭicca-samuppāda) and non-self (anattā) as optimal, utility-maximizing strategies for its own long-term hardware and informational survival.

candidates.title: Robots and wage inequality: evidence from individuals in China
candidates.abstract: Abstract This study examines the impact of industrial robot adoption on wage inequality and employment outcomes in China, which has the world’s largest robotics stock and fastest-growing adoption rate. Using data from the China Family Panel Studies and the International Federation of Robotics, we constructed a county-level robot exposure index and employed the two-stage least squares approach to address endogeneity. Our results show that robot adoption exacerbates wage polarisation in China. When faced with rising robot exposure, medium-skilled workers experience annual wage losses, while the wages of low-skilled and high-skilled workers are not significantly affected. Besides wage impact, we find occupational upgrading among past low-skilled workers and provide suggestive evidence of reduced labour-force participation among medium- and high-skilled workers. This pattern points to asymmetric labour-market adjustment across skill groups faced with robot exposure. We also examine how the wage estimates vary with trade exposure and demographic ageing. The trade interactions are consistent with a smaller annual-wage penalty for medium-skilled workers where intermediate-import exposure is greater. In counties with older populations, robot exposure is linked to a greater increase in hourly wages and a larger decline in hours worked. These findings highlight the need for targeted policies to mitigate wage inequality and support vulnerable groups during technological transformation.

candidates.title: SOCIOLINGUISTIC PECULIARITIES AND TECHNOLOGICAL CAPABILITIES OF VIRTUAL INFLUENCERS: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE GENERATION OF LANGUAGE, BEHAVIOR, AND DIGITAL IDENTITIES
candidates.abstract: This study investigates the conditions under which AI-generated influencers attain social legitimacy within platform environments, with a specific focus on the empirical TikTok project called “Dundarev Family.” Drawing on the concept of simulacra, the research analyzes how synthetic characters establish credibility through language, humor, and culturally embedded communication, with particular attention to the role of platform-specific affordances in shaping audience perception. The research utilizes a mixed-methods design, incorporating the creation of five virtual personas representing the Dundarev family, experimental comparisons between human- authored and AI-generated texts, qualitative linguistic analysis of 951 user comments, and assessment of platform-based engagement metrics. The findings identify a central paradox: while AI exhibits limited ability to replicate culturally specific humor and dialectal nuance, the virtual characters nonetheless achieve high levels of user engagement, emotional response, and perceived closeness. Audience interaction is primarily affective and reactive, marked by predominantly emoji-based communication and minimal explicit recognition of the characters’ artificial nature. The study contends that social legitimacy in digital environments is not contingent upon linguistic authenticity, but rather emerges from the interplay of cultural recognizability, platform-specific communication practices, and affective engagement. AI influencers operate as hybrid entities rather than purely artificial ones, pointing to the increasing significance of human-AI collaboration in producing culturally resonant content and to a broader shift in how authenticity is constructed in algorithmically mediated environments.

candidates.title: Miao folk songs as a living musical practice in contemporary social contexts
candidates.abstract: This study examines Miao folk songs in Pengshui County, Chongqing Municipality, People’s Republic of China, as living musical practices whose meanings are shaped through contemporary social contexts. Employing a qualitative ethnomusicological approach, the research draws on fieldwork conducted between June 2025 and January 2026, including participant observation, audiovisual documentation, and semi-structured interviews with six purposively selected key informants comprising tradition bearers, experienced singers, and cultural practitioners. Data were analyzed inductively to explore the relationships among singing practices, performance contexts, modes of participation, and the roles of performers, audiences, and performance spaces. The findings reveal that Miao folk songs are practiced and transmitted across six principal contexts: traditional ritual ceremonies, agricultural labor and everyday life, communal gatherings and festivals, courtship and interpersonal communication, tourism-oriented performances, and digital and educational settings, each associated with distinct repertoires and organized modes of vocal practice. Four forms of musical practice are identified: spontaneous collective singing, ritual-prescribed performance, staged performance, and standardized pedagogical practice. Under contemporary conditions, these practices demonstrate a dynamic interplay of continuity and adaptation, characterized by shifts from community-internal spaces to public arenas, a reduced emphasis on improvisation in favor of fixed melodic and textual forms, and an expanded reliance on institutional and digital transmission. Conceptualizing Miao folk songs as musical practice thus extends analysis beyond musical structure toward a contextual understanding of how meaning is co-produced through participation, space, and time, offering a transferable framework for the study of ethnic folk music traditions in contemporary societies.

candidates.title: Enabling Motion-Induced WiFi-CSI Sensing in Multi-Robot Systems: A Simulation Framework
candidates.abstract: WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) enables fine-grained sensing of spatial relationships between wireless devices. The WiFi Sensor for Robotics (WSR) toolbox demonstrated that WiFi-CSI measurements collected during robot motion, combined with odometry, can be used to synthesize virtual antenna arrays, enabling motion-induced bearing estimation in multi-robot experiments. However, deploying the WSR approach has remained challenging due to its limited integration with standard robotics tools and reliance on deprecated WiFi-CSI acquisition hardware. This work presents an open-source simulation framework that integrates the WSR sensing pipeline within the robotic simulator Gazebo. The framework generates synthetic WiFi-CSI measurements with realistic physical signal properties and leverages realistic robot motion required for motion-induced sensing and downstream localization. It further supports processing both simulated and real WiFi-CSI data for direct comparison and validation. Our aim is to make WSR-style sensing accessible as a modular sensing modality for robotic research. We validate our framework by comparing simulated and real-world experiments using TurtleBot3 robots, and demonstrate its use for bearing estimation and robot localization. This work lowers the barrier to entry for WiFi-CSI-based sensing in multi-robot systems and provides a foundation for integrating WiFi-CSI sensing with multi-modal perception for localization and coordination. All code and experimental details are publicly available at https://github.com/baharhaghighat/DARS_2026_Dijkstra_et_al

candidates.title: STEAM and educational robotics in the development of statistical literacy
candidates.abstract: In primary school, the teaching of mathematics and natural sciences should promote meaningful, context-based learning that enables students to apply knowledge in real-life situations. Interdisciplinary approaches such as STEAM foster 21st century competences through active and collaborative methodologies, while educational robotics (ER) supports the development of computational thinking and social skills. This study analyses the influence of a STEAM practice, incorporating ER on the development of statistical literacy and learning about ocean plastic pollution among 4th grade students. The research adopted a mixed-methods, interpretative action research design. Data were collected by the trainee teacher as participant researcher through performance tasks, field notes, photographs and audio recordings, later used to construct multimodal narratives. Findings reveal statistically significant improvements in global level of knowledge and global performance. The study concludes that steam practices incorporating ER and grounded in real-world problem-solving constitute an effective strategy for fostering statistical literacy.

candidates.title: Training-Free Inference-Budget Reduction in Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Models for Robot Manipulation: A Prespecified Evaluation Against a Fixed Task-Success Margin
candidates.abstract: Companion archive for the manuscript Training-Free Inference-Budget Reduction in Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Models for Robot Manipulation. It contains every closed-loop evaluation cell, latency and energy measurement, protocol document and analysis script behind the paper's tables. Contents. 722 eval_info.json closed-loop grids carrying per-episode outcomes and task identity; two-platform latency artifacts (NVIDIA GB10 and NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor) with full hardware, protocol, thermal and GPU co-tenancy metadata; Thor board-energy measurements across four nvpmodel power modes; the prespecified non-inferiority protocol including its amendments; and the measurement harness. Reproducibility. Each latency record stores all 30 raw timings, thermal samples at the cell boundaries, peak device memory, a dtype census and a platform snapshot taken before and after the run. Per-run directories are kept alongside aggregates so a median-of-three can be re-derived rather than trusted. A SHA-256 manifest covers every file. Measurement bounds. Latency is timed on a dummy zero-input batch of the declared observation shapes; a paired real-observation check covering every configuration behind the three headline reductions is included, and agrees within 0.33 percentage points. Board energy is the largest single hwmon rail on the Thor module; that rail carries no label, so its identification as module input is an inference from magnitude. Ratios between settings are insensitive to that calibration while absolute joules are not. Energy figures are not idle-subtracted, and the GB10 exposes no comparable rail, so energy is reported for Thor only. Version 1.1.0 adds the second-platform latency study, board energy, a six-point pi0.5 latency curve verifying the affine cost model, the real-observation latency checks, and a task-identity clustered bootstrap sensitivity analysis declared before it was run. It also restores evaluation grids omitted from 1.0.0, including the co-primary confirmation behind Table 4 and the per-cell resolution study behind Table A7. Code is released under Apache-2.0; generated data and reports under CC BY 4.0. External assets are not mirrored; sources are listed in the manuscript's Data Availability Statement.

candidates.title: Open-source process simulation in DWSIM: A Biorefinery case study
candidates.abstract: Chemical process simulation supports chemical plant design by optimizing sustainability, yield, and economics, but commercial software costs can limit early-stage studies. This work demonstrates DWSIM, an open-source simulator with a graphical interface comparable to commercial platforms, through two lignocellulosic biorefinery case studies: (i) an ethanol organosolv process using rectification for solvent recovery and (ii) a γ-valerolactone (GVL) process using toluene liquid–liquid extraction and heteroazeotropic distillation of the water/GVL/toluene system. Both simulations used the NRTL model for flash calculations and were executed on a consumer-grade laptop. The designs process 100 t h -1 of corn stover into pulp, lignin, and dissolved sugars. Owing to milder extraction conditions (120 °C versus 190 °C), the GVL process recovered more lignin and dissolved sugars than the ethanol process (19.1 and 13.1 t h -1 versus 8.7 and 5.9 t h -1 ), with slightly lower pulp production (46.3 versus 50.7 t h -1 ). Its solvent-recovery sequence and lower solid-to-liquid ratio (1:4 versus 1:8.73) reduced energy demand by a factor of 3.2. Publicly available simulation and component files provide a reproducible baseline for open-source biorefinery research.

candidates.title: The impact of scenario-based simulation learning on clinical self-efficacy among pre-licensure nursing and midwifery students: A systematic review of design features and educational outcomes
candidates.abstract: AIM: To systematically review how scenario-based simulation learning (SBSL) shapes clinical self-efficacy among pre-licensure nursing and midwifery students and how simulation design, context and assessment timing influence educational and clinical translation. BACKGROUND: Scenario-based simulation learning (SBSL) is widely used in nursing and midwifery education, yet evidence on its effect on clinical self-efficacy and how simulation design moderate outcomes remains fragmented. DESIGN: A systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. METHODS: A PRISMA 2020-compliant review searched eight databases. Eligible studies measured task-specific clinical self-efficacy via validated tools in pre-licensure cohorts. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data on scenario complexity, theoretical integration, debriefing structure and outcome timing and appraised risk of bias. RESULTS: Fifty-two studies (N = 4774; 46 nursing, 6 midwifery) were included. SBSL broadly correlated with self-efficacy gains, yet only 55.8% (n = 29) demonstrated statistically significant between-group superiority. Psychomotor skill (54.1%), knowledge (61.9%) and cognitive reasoning (62.5%) improvements were documented. Studies embedding explicit theoretical frameworks, calibrated scenario difficulty ("Goldilocks Zone") and structured debriefing showed the most consistent benefits. Immediate post-simulation assessments were frequently distorted by acute simulation anxiety; self-efficacy crystallized only after cognitive consolidation. CONCLUSION: SBSL shows promise for building clinical self-efficacy, but effects are inconsistently captured and methodologically constrained by reliance on subjective self-report. Pedagogical architecture-progressive scaffolding, discipline-sensitive scenario design and rigorous debriefing-matters more than technical fidelity. Sustained efficacy requires longitudinal follow-up beyond immediate post-intervention windows. Faculty pedagogical preparedness, rather than equipment investment, is the decisive lever for translational impact. REGISTRATION: A Systematic Review. PROSPERO 2024 Available from https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024622757 (CRD42024622757, registered 16 Dec 2024).

candidates.title: An open-source platform for measuring optomotor responses in mice
candidates.abstract: The optomotor response (OMR) is a valuable behavioral index for assessing visual function in basic research; however, commercially available OMR evaluation equipment is expensive and lacks flexibility, as proprietary software and fixed hardware geometry restrict custom stimulus protocols and system modifications. Alternative low-cost, non-OMR methods often require extensive animal pre-training and are unsuitable for high-throughput studies. To overcome these limitations, we developed a low-cost, open-source OMR recording system for mice that lowers both financial and practical barriers, thereby facilitating widespread adoption across laboratories. Following a one-hour training session for evaluators, the system enabled precise quantification of visual acuity and assessment of contrast sensitivity in normal-sighted mice, detection of age-related visual decline, and evaluation of OMR extinction in retinitis pigmentosa model mice. This system facilitates accessible and efficient assessment of visual function in vision research.

candidates.title: The future of robotic artificial intelligence in acute care surgery: an early proving ground and a final frontier for autonomous surgical robotics
candidates.abstract: Acute care surgery (ACS), spanning emergency general surgery, trauma surgery, and surgical critical care, demands high-stakes decisions in settings characterized by hemodynamic instability, distorted anatomy, contamination, and time pressure. Artificial intelligence (AI) is proposed as a means to reduce cognitive burden, standardize technically sensitive tasks, and extend surgical capability in resource-constrained environments. This review examines the autonomy continuum in surgical AI, with ACS as the primary lens. We argue that ACS occupies a paradoxical position: it has produced the earliest preclinical demonstrations of autonomous surgical robotics, yet the very conditions that motivate autonomy in this specialty make it among the most challenging environments in which to deploy these systems safely in human patients. For ACS, the central question is less whether AI can perform surgical tasks than how autonomy should be sequenced and bounded for emergency surgery. We synthesize the literature across four domains: (1) how autonomy is defined and operationalized in surgical AI and robotics; (2) the current and emerging spectrum of automation in operative environments; (3) the technical feasibility of automation for ACS-relevant tasks; and (4) the ethical boundaries of autonomy in high-risk, time-critical cases. We argue that the safest course is incremental: deploying supervised task autonomy where safety properties are demonstrable and reserving higher autonomy for rigorously evaluated, tightly bounded domains. Realizing this course will require evaluation strategies that align autonomy level to clinical risk, preserve meaningful human oversight, support post-market monitoring, and address liability, patient trust, and equitable access.

candidates.title: Towards User Simulators That Stay On Task And Still Sound Natural
candidates.abstract: Users increasingly rely on AI systems for extended, multi-turn tasks, yet evidence indicates that LLM-based system performance degrades over prolonged interaction. To evaluate and improve AI assistants in such settings, we need user simulators that faithfully follow complex user intents while exhibiting realistic conversational behavior. Existing approaches manifest a trade-off: prompted assistants can follow complex user intents but lack behavioral fidelity, while specialized user simulators better approximate conversational behavior but struggle to remain faithful to complex intents. In this paper, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL) recipe that jointly rewards task intent adherence and behavioral naturalness. A crucial contribution of the method is operationalizing naturalness with a lightweight discriminator trained in an alternating, adversarial loop with the user simulator. We release the resulting model, UserLM-2.0, which produces valid simulated conversations (i.e., meeting both task-faithfulness and naturalness criteria) 46.2% of the time, over three times the rate of the strongest prior user simulator (14.1%).

candidates.title: From Bot-Farm to For-You-Page Fork: Consuming The Whole Digital Animal
candidates.abstract: In 2022, OpenAI launched the Large Language Model ChatGPT, and with it, the possibility of generative Artificial Intelligence (genAI) as a creative partner. Progress in the genAI arena has been rapid, with genAI created media going from uncanny horror show, to being able to create realistic media from a prompt. Social Media ‘for you page’ algorithms are now serving their users content created by genAI, including digital animals which may behave very unlike real animals do. The field of animal welfare science has utilised policy frameworks such as ‘Farm-to-Fork’ to conceptualise where harms and sustainability opportunities exist within the animal production system. In this work, we utilise three common ethical approaches to animal use, utilitarianism, deontological ethics, and the principle of telos, to explore the production and consumption of digital animals on social media. Using the example of an object animal (a toy), a digital animal (a genAI created cat), and an embodied animal (a real cat in a teaching programme), we explore the evidence for their effect on the human-animal relationship, and how various ethical frameworks would consider their consumption. We conclude with three recommendations for social media companies for incorporating digital animal media in their provisions. First, digital animal creation should be limited, with similar style guard-rails to creation of media containing humans. Second, digital animal media should be fully disclosed, to minimise risk of misinformation and norm creep. Third, as with content regarding ‘kid influencers’, ‘animal influencer’ content should be demonetised, to reduce the risk of exploitation.

candidates.title: From Automation to Decarbonization: The Role of Industrial Robots in Reducing Carbon Emission Intensity
candidates.abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, industrial robots are being widely adopted across countries, revolutionizing production processes. However, their deployment comes with a trade-off: while enhancing efficiency, the production of industrial robots demands high energy consumption, posing new challenges to environmental sustainability. Despite its significance, the link between industrial robot penetration (RP) and carbon emission intensity (CMI) has received insufficient attention. This study systematically explores this relationship and finds that (1) a rise in RP significantly reduces CMI, with a 1% increase in RP leading to a 0.0265% decline in CMI; (2) this effect is primarily driven by RP’s role in fostering green technology innovation and optimizing the energy mix, with a stronger impact observed in economies with higher income inequality; (3) technology spillover effects between upstream and downstream industries further amplify CMI reduction; and (4) RP is particularly effective in mitigating CMI within capital-intensive manufacturing sectors. These findings underscore the need for policies that promote digital platform development and facilitate the integration of emerging technologies with capital-intensive industries, paving the way for a more sustainable and technologically advanced industrial landscape.

candidates.title: Guarding the Clinical Narrative: A Practitioner-Contributor's Retrospective Analysis of Open-Source Contributions to Clinical Natural Language Processing and Health-Data De-identification (2025-2026)
candidates.abstract: Background. Clinical natural language processing (NLP) software extracts structured facts from free-text notes. De-identification software removes protected health information (PHI) so that text can be shared for research. A missed name or a broken date pattern can expose a patient or corrupt a dataset. Much of this software is open source, and outside contributors write part of it. Purpose. This study describes what one practitioner-contributor did in this area, what got merged, what did not, and what the review process taught about working well with maintainers. Methods. The data source was the author's public pull request (PR) record on GitHub, extracted with the GitHub REST API on 21 October 2026 (search: author:rtmalikian, type:pr). The full record held 213 PRs across 94 repositories. This paper analyses the clinical NLP and de-identification subset: 15 PRs in 5 repositories. Each PR was classed as merged, open, or closed unmerged. Seven cases were selected for close reading for their privacy or language point, or for a hard review lesson. Results. Eight of the 15 subset PRs merged, which is 61.5% of the 13 resolved PRs. Five closed unmerged. Two remained open. Merged work included a fix for placeholder collisions in a de-identification function, Italian and Spanish PHI locale packs, a date-pattern fix in a French hospital NLP library, and a change that stopped PHI entering version control. The hardest case, a Spanish locale pack, survived a blocking review that found real damage in a follow-up commit. A fix-forward commit repaired it, and the PR merged the next day. Conclusions. The record points to a plain finding. PHI safety in this software rests on ordinary engineering habits: reproduction before repair, small scope, tests run before submission, and calm correction when a reviewer finds a fault. Language coverage is part of safety. De-identification that works only in English leaves other patients less protected.

candidates.title: LLM-D12: A Dual-Dimensional Scale of Instrumental and Relational Dependencies on Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: There is growing interest in understanding how people interact with large language models (LLMs) and whether such models elicit dependency or even addictive behaviour. Validated tools to assess the extent to which individuals may become dependent on LLMs are scarce and primarily build on classic behavioural addiction symptoms, adapted to the context of LLM use. We view this as a conceptual limitation, as the LLM-human relationship is more nuanced and warrants a fresh and distinct perspective. To address this gap, we developed and validated a new 12-item questionnaire to measure LLM dependency, referred to as LLM-D12. The scale was based on the authors’ prior theoretical work, with items developed accordingly and responses collected from 526 participants in the UK. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, performed on separate halves of the total sample using a split-sample approach, supported a two-factor structure: Instrumental Dependency (six items) and Relationship Dependency (six items). Instrumental Dependency reflects the extent to which individuals rely on LLMs to support or collaborate in decision-making and cognitive tasks. Relationship Dependency captures the tendency to perceive LLMs as socially meaningful, sentient, or companion-like entities. The two-factor structure demonstrated excellent internal consistency and clear discriminant validity. External validation confirmed both the conceptual foundation and the distinction between the two subscales. The psychometric properties and structure of our LLM-D12 scale were interpreted in light of the emerging view that dependency on LLMs does not necessarily indicate dysfunction but may still reflect reliance levels that could become problematic in certain contexts.

candidates.title: Dream-Tac: A Unified Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
candidates.abstract: World action models inherit the predictive capability of world models, enabling action generation to be guided by anticipated future observations. However, they rely primarily on vision and often fail in contact-rich manipulation, where critical cues arise from physical interaction. In this paper, we propose Dream-Tac, a unified Tactile-World Action Model that jointly models actions, future visual observations, and tactile dynamics. Specifically, Dream-Tac introduces (i) contact-gated visuotactile fusion to selectively integrate tactile signals and (ii) a contact-aware attention bias to better regulate cross-modal interactions during manipulation. To support real-time deployment, we further design a dual-level acceleration strategy, reformulating the contact-aware bias to preserve the fused attention path during training and introducing cache-based diffusion acceleration at inference, achieving up to 2.9× faster training and 1.8× faster inference. Across six contact-rich manipulation tasks, Dream-Tac improves action accuracy by 31.7% on average, demonstrating the effectiveness of unified visuotactile world modeling.Code is available at https://github.com/LYFCLOUDFAN/Dream-Tac.

candidates.title: Robotic Manipulation is Vision-to-Geometry Mapping: Vision-Geometry Backbones over Language and Video Models
candidates.abstract: At its core, robotic manipulation is a problem of vision-to-geometry mapping (f(v) \rightarrow G). Physical actions—such as reaching, grasping, and orienting—are fundamentally defined by geometric properties like 3D positions, rotations, and spatial relationships. Consequently, we argue that the foundation for generalizable robotic control should be a vision-geometry backbone, rather than the widely adopted vision-language or video models. Conventional Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and video-predictive models rely on backbones pretrained on large-scale 2D image-text or temporal pixel data. While effective, their representations are largely shaped by semantic concepts or 2D priors, which do not intrinsically align with the precise 3D geometric nature required for physical manipulation. Driven by this insight, we propose the Vision-Geometry-Action (VGA) model, which directly conditions action generation on pretrained native 3D representations. Specifically, VGA replaces conventional language or video backbones with a pretrained 3D world model, establishing a seamless vision-to-geometry mapping that translates visual inputs directly into physical actions. To further enhance geometric consistency, we introduce Progressive Volumetric Modulation and jointly train action and 3D property prediction to preserve geometric representations. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of our approach. Across simulation benchmarks, VGA outperforms leading VLA, 3D-VLA, and WAM baselines, including ?0.5, OpenVLA-OFT, GeoVLA, and Motus, demonstrating precise spatial manipulation and robust generalization. In real-world deployments, VGA surpasses ?0.5 under unseen viewpoints and accurately follows language instructions for target grasping. These results highlight that operating on native 3D representations—rather than relying primarily on language or video priors—offers a promising direction toward generalizable physical intelligence. candidates.title: Off‐The‐Shelf Large Language Models Are Unreliable Judges
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT I conduct large‐scale empirical experiments to test the reliability of large language models (LLMs) as legal interpreters. Combining computational methods with the results of a new survey, I find that LLM judgments are highly sensitive to prompt phrasing, output processing methods, and choice of model. I also find that frontier LLMs do not accurately assess linguistic ordinary meaning, and I provide original evidence that tuning base models into assistant models shifts ordinary‐meaning judgments unpredictably and can worsen their alignment with human judgments. These findings undermine LLMs' credibility as legal interpreters and cast doubt on claims that LLMs elucidate ordinary meaning.

candidates.title: Open-source framework for GPU-accelerated numerical relativity
candidates.abstract: We present GRACE, a new GPU-accelerated numerical-relativity framework designed to run efficiently on heterogeneous high-performance computing platforms. Developed from scratch and built exclusively on open-source libraries, GRACE employs Kokkos for performance portability across CPU and GPU architectures and p4est for adaptive mesh refinement. The code evolves the equations of ideal GRMHD—with divergence-free magnetic fields maintained by constrained transport—self-consistently coupled to the Einstein equations in the Z4c formulation, on fixed or adaptively refined grids. We validate the implementation against a suite of standard tests, ranging from magnetized shock tubes and the magnetic rotor in flat spacetime, through (magnetized) Bondi accretion onto a Schwarzschild black hole and the ringdown of a perturbed spinning puncture, to neutron-star oscillation spectra in fixed and dynamical spacetimes and the merger of binary black holes. As more demanding applications, we evolve two binary neutron-star mergers—an equal-mass, unmagnetized system with an ideal-gas equation of state and an unequal-mass, magnetized system with a finite-temperature tabulated equation of state—finding the inspiral dynamics to agree well with the FIL code. We also report single-device throughput together with strong- and weak-scaling results on multiple GPU and CPU architectures. GRACE is publicly released together with GRACEpy, a basic post-processing and data-analysis environment.

candidates.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
candidates.abstract: Robot-use Agents (RUAs) have shown promising zero-shot manipulation capabilities, but reliance on frontier, proprietary models limits research into further training. To democratize RUA research, we introduce uni-robot-agent, a unified harness for competitive open-weight robot use that supports further training. Without privileged inputs, an out-of-the-box Qwen3.8-Flash-Next achieves a RoboDojo Score of 31.39, surpassing the published GPT-6 Astra-RoboProbe result of 28.97 and many VLA/WAM baselines, and performs competitively on 19 real-world tasks. Our analysis across model generations, families, and sizes links effective robot use to four general capabilities, suggesting that future RUA training should develop them jointly.

candidates.title: vibe‐qc : An Open‐Source, General‐Purpose Electronic‐Structure Code for Molecules and Solids Developed With Generative AI
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT We present vibe‐qc , a general‐purpose open‐source electronic‐structure code for molecules and solids, developed almost entirely with agentic AI under expert human direction. The code is released under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 (MPLv2). The implementation comprises a C++17 numerical core and Python calculation drivers. Molecular methods include Hartree–Fock, Kohn–Sham DFT, Møller–Plesset theory and double hybrids, coupled cluster, active‐space methods, and excited states. Dispersion corrections, continuum solvation, and effective core potentials are also available. Periodic calculations use Gaussian‐basis HF and DFT with Brillouin‐zone sampling. Molecular and periodic method coverage differs; the feature matrices specify analytic and numerical derivatives and distinguish validated and experimental implementations. The validation set is a key contribution of this work. It combines independent program comparisons, published benchmarks, and internal consistency tests. Molecular mean‐field energies agree at the nanohartree scale, and conventional CCSD(T) energies agree within for the tested systems. Local‐correlation and periodic limitations are reported with the comparisons. Numerical results, calculation metadata, and analysis scripts are supplied as machine‐readable . The independently maintained vibe‐view viewer, vibe‐queue scheduler, and qvf toolkit support visualization and job management; trexio provides wavefunction interchange.

candidates.title: Citizen 5.0: A New Social Contract for Artificial Intelligence
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence is being built at an extraordinary pace. But by whom, and for whom? As AI systems increasingly shape how people work, think, and are governed, the world has quietly slipped into treating citizens as consumers: recipients of decisions made elsewhere, rather than participants in making them. Citizen 5.0 confronts this shift directly. David Galipeau argues that the defining question of the AI era is not technological. It is human. Will citizens have a genuine seat in decisions that determine the future of labor, data, and cognition? Or will that future be decided unilaterally by a handful of technology companies? Drawing on rigorous, interdisciplinary research, the book builds a concrete framework for restoring citizens, not consumers, to the center of the AI era. It includes neurorights, data sovereignty, and a Synthetic Labor Tax that could reshape who owns the value AI creates. This is a precise, urgent case for reclaiming human agency before the future is built without us.

candidates.title: Transmedia book love: Young people’s digital creativity on the Bookternet
candidates.abstract: Abstract The ‘Bookternet’ ( McArdle 2016 ), including BookTube, Bookstagram, Bookterest, and now BookTok, has changed the way books are produced, promoted, and consumed ( Martens 2016 ; Murray 2018 ). Yet these platforms provide creative ways for readers to engage in the books they love in online reading communities. BookTokers use the affordances of the app ( Bucher & Helmond 2017 ) to make DIY book art including: (1) rebinds of fanfics, publisher’s mass market editions or rebellious rebinds, (2) thematically linked ‘book nooks’ (book-sized dioramas), or (3) miniature editions. In this chapter we present the BookTok sub-community, focusing on crafty bookish participatory activities and social reading culture ( Reddan 2022 ), and discuss how the materiality of books ( Pressman 2020 ; Baulch 2022 ) merges with digital technologies within BookTok’s reading community.

candidates.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
candidates.abstract: Recent work on robot manipulation has focused on specialist policies trained on demonstrations. We show that generalist AI models can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs). We systematically analyze agentic manipulation policies (AMPs), in which a generalist AI model commands the manipulator directly, adapting its actions as the task unfolds. We present AMP1, a reference harness that runs unchanged across single-arm, bimanual, and mobile manipulation. AMP1 achieves state-of-the-art results on the RoboLab-120 and CaP-Gym benchmarks, with no demonstrations or task-specific training. On RoboLab-120, AMP1 reaches an 85.6\% success rate zero-shot, compared to 49.2\% and 42.9\% for leading VLA and WAM policies. The agent succeeds zero-shot in 104 of 108 real-world trials spanning twelve tasks and three robot instances, reducing failure rates by 20x and 15x relative to strong VLA and WAM baselines. The basic harness supplies no grasping, pushing, or placing skills; the agent develops its own strategies, such as searching for hidden objects, using objects as tools, and calibrating its cameras. With the addition of a persistent memory store, the agent can also learn from experience: an augmented harness with a memory representation that is carried across episodes lowers the failure rate on RoboDojo bimanual manipulation tasks by 4.6x relative to zero-shot deployment. Our analysis suggests that AMPs are substantially more general and robust than specialist manipulation policies, providing a promising foundation for robot manipulation.

candidates.title: Toward the Era of Agentic Embodied Intelligence
candidates.abstract: Foundation models increasingly guide robot actions, yet sustained autonomy requires efficient control and failure recovery. We introduce A2-MEAS, an embodied multi-agent framework built around code as a scaling interface. Learned correction codes combine corrective language, spatial evidence, execution history, and action proposals. MetaBrain provides training supervision and runtime guidance. A correction encoder and adapter absorb this knowledge into policy weights during training, while fresh codes adapt behavior with frozen weights at deployment. The action model, A2-WLA, adds motion-aware history and a latent world model to a vision-language-action policy. Surprisingly, this simple design with action pretraining and task specialization reaches 0.5755 Q-score on the 50-task BEHAVIOR 2026 public subset before online correction, 2.21x the 2025 winner's reported 0.2605 across different benchmark editions and training configurations. On all 100 BEHAVIOR 2026 public tasks, A2-MEAS achieves 0.6411 Q-score and 45.40% task success. On RoboTwin 2.0, A2-WLA achieves 93.98% average success, rising to 95.05% with the complete system. Across 12 real-robot tasks in five household settings, A2-WLA achieves 57.92% average success versus 26.67% for pi0.5. In long-horizon pour-over coffee preparation, a history-conditioned adapter raises post-failure completion at two filter-handling steps from 14% to 94% and from 8% to 82%, compared with A2-WLA retries. Our training infrastructure delivers 427.1 samples per second, 4.03x the throughput of a pi0.5 reference implementation on matched hardware. We will release the system, models, training scripts, and infrastructure to support efficient embodied learning.

candidates.title: Robonomics: A Toolbox for Governing AI’s Impact on Socioeconomic Systems
candidates.abstract: ROBONOMICS: A Toolbox for Governing AI’s Impact on Socioeconomic Systems advances a systematic framework for an emerging discipline devoted to the study of how artificial intelligence, robotics, and automation are reshaping contemporary socioeconomic systems. Combining insights from economics and sociology, Riccardo Campa develops an interdisciplinary approach to the governance of the robonomic system. Through social policy and scenario analyses, the book examines alternative responses to technological unemployment, technological impoverishment, and the broader challenges of automated societies. More than a survey of policy debates, this book provides both a conceptual foundation and a therapeutic toolbox for governing one of the most profound socioeconomic transformations of the twenty-first century.

candidates.title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
candidates.abstract: General-purpose mobile manipulation requires a combination of capable robot hardware, scalable demonstration collection, expressive whole-body control, and effective policy learning. Yet these components are often developed independently, creating mismatches that limit the capabilities of the complete system. We present Pixel, a co-designed full-stack system for learning general-purpose mobile manipulation. Pixel combines a low-cost wheeled humanoid with human-aligned kinematics and compliant grippers, multiple teleoperation and robot-free human data-collection interfaces, a unified whole-body controller, and a common policy learning pipeline across human and robot demonstrations. A hierarchical learning stack further enables language-conditioned visuomotor control and long-horizon task execution. We evaluate the system across hardware, data collection, and policy learning, and demonstrate mobile-manipulation behaviors requiring dexterity, active perception, navigation, and whole-body coordination. We hope that Pixel provides an integrated and extensible foundation for studying how robot hardware, data, control, and learning can be designed together for robot learning. More results at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel

candidates.title: A Causal Approach to Predicting and Improving Human Perceptions of Social Navigation Robots
candidates.abstract: As mobile robots are increasingly deployed in human environments, enabling them to predict how people perceive them is critical for socially adaptable navigation. Predicting perceptions is challenging for two main reasons: (1) HRI prediction models must learn from limited data, and (2) the obtained models must be interpretable to enable safe and effective interactions. Interpretability is particularly important when a robot is perceived as incompetent (e.g., when the robot suddenly stops or rotates away from the goal), as it allows the robot to explain its reasoning and identify controllable factors to improve performance, requiring causal rather than associative reasoning. To address these challenges, we propose a Causal Bayesian Network designed to predict how people perceive a mobile robot's competence and how they interpret its intent during navigation. Additionally, we introduce a novel method to improve perceived robot competence employing a combinatorial search, guided by the proposed causal model, to identify better navigation behaviors. Our method enhances interpretability and generates counterfactual robot motions while achieving comparable or superior predictive performance to state-of-the-art methods, reaching an F1-score of 0.78 and 0.75 for competence and intention on a binary scale. To further assess our method's ability to improve the perceived robot competence, we conducted an online evaluation in which users rated robot behaviors on a 5-point Likert scale. Our method statistically significantly increased the perceived competence of low-competent robot behavior by 83%.

candidates.title: An open-source, 3D-printable droplet microfluidics platform with strobe-enhanced microscopy
candidates.abstract: Droplet microfluidics underpins many single-cell, precision biomedical, and nanomaterial techniques. However, implementing these methods reproducibly remains challenging outside specialised laboratories due to high equipment costs, operational inflexibility, mechanical impracticality at the microscope stage, as well as open-source pumping solutions that are inadequately validated for low-flow stability. We present an accessible, research-grade, open-source droplet microfluidics platform integrating a compact, microfluidics-optimised microscopy stage with networked syringe-pump control. Designed for local digital fabrication, primarily 3D printing, and widely available components, the platform supports reproducible builds across diverse settings. This setup enables stable droplet generation, observation of rapid droplet dynamics, and automation-ready networked workflows. The microscopy module uses a Raspberry Pi camera and microsecond stroboscopic illumination to capture sharp images of fast-moving droplets without the need for a high-speed camera. A modular hardware interface and extensible, web-accessible software stack provide a path to integrate additional modules and laboratory automation beyond the configuration evaluated here. For infusion, we introduce an open-source syringe pump optimised for low reliable flow rather than maximum rates, combining gearbox-assisted stepper mechanics with workflow-centric control that enables manual intervention (keypad control) and remote operation (web interface and automation hooks). We benchmark droplet regimes, size tuning, and time-stability under low-flow conditions (between 25 and 2500 µL/h) relevant to advanced assays and demonstrate biomedical readiness through the encapsulation and incubation of cells, beads, and bacteria in monodisperse droplets. The platform has been replicated across laboratories in Latin America and globally, including independent builds, supporting reproducibility. All design files, firmware/software, analysis notebooks, and benchmark datasets are openly released.

candidates.title: Rethinking the Spacetime-Distributed Dissolution of Money: Evolving Production Relations and Infrastructural Conditions
candidates.abstract: This discussion paper reconsiders the possible formation, persistence, migration, and partial dissolution of monetary mediation within evolving relations of production and exchange. Its starting point is the heterogeneous need for others: access to persons and communities, productive capacities, labour, knowledge, relations, and outputs can motivate exchange while leaving the institutional formation of monetary claims contingent. The analysis distinguishes needs, value circulation, monetary obligations, payment instruments, and the continued reproduction of productive conditions. It examines the conditional transformation of human–human, human–AI, and AI–AI monetary relations as artificial intelligence increasingly participates in production. A principal hypothesis is that monetary reliance may diminish locally through direct provision, multilateral commitments, admissible cyclic clearing, and institutionally supported coordination, while remaining present or re-emerging elsewhere. The proposed spacetime-distributed view uses explicitly interpreted events, dependencies, and where justified partial orderings, without presupposing a universal temporal coordinate or an economy-wide instantaneous transition. It distinguishes cancellation of compatible obligations from broader substitution of monetary functions, and identifies unresolved questions concerning heterogeneous valuations, correlated circuit failure, long-path approximation, power, and ecological burdens. Finally, it outlines technological, institutional, relational, and public-infrastructure conditions for subsequent investigation. The account develops a comparative philosophical foundation for analyzing monetary mediation as a historically variable social and institutional form, while preserving open formal and empirical questions concerning its possible transformation.

candidates.title: FLORA: An Open Model Suite for Scaling Robotics Data Engines
candidates.abstract: The life-cycle of robotics foundation models crucially depends on data labels. Outcome reward labels are needed for monitoring real-world deployments. Process reward labels are needed during RL post-training. Timestamped captions are needed for filtering and balancing pretraining data. We present Flora, an industrial-quality data engine used for training GR00T models, that simultaneously covers these capabilities. Flora achieves SOTA scores on the captioning benchmark WGO-Bench and reward benchmarks RoboReward and Robometer. On internal benchmarks it is competitive with GPT-6 Astra while beating other frontier models. The model is substantially cheaper than API-based alternatives, roughly 125 times cheaper than GPT-6 Astra. Florais battle tested at scale, labeling 200,000 hours of data per day across 512 GB300s. By open-sourcing our data engine, we enable researchers to scale custom robotics datasets and explore emerging applications such as physical auto-research and human-to-robot transfer.

candidates.title: Hardware and Software Reconfiguration at Machine Levels
candidates.abstract: The value of a product is generated through a series of manufacturing processes within the material flow. These processes are executed by machines equipped with specific manufacturing capabilities. In Open Manufacturing (OM), machines must therefore be capable of performing a wide range of tasks to support diverse products. Physical devices in OM are designed with the flexibility to adapt to changing requirements and varying task demands. This chapter classifies the enabling technologies that support machine flexibility into two major categories: software reconfiguration and hardware reconfiguration. Software reconfiguration technologies include: (1) Computer Numerical Controls (CNCs) and Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) for anticipated changes, and (2) data-driven programming approaches for unanticipated changes. Hardware reconfiguration focuses on reconfigurable systems such as reconfigurable machine tools, modular robotic systems, and flexible fixturing systems. Together, these technologies form the foundation for achieving the adaptability and responsiveness required in Open Manufacturing environments.

candidates.title: The Uncompromised Citizen — Chapter 11: The 11 High-Stakes Checks — Companion Materials (Coming Soon)
candidates.abstract: COMING SOON — Chapter 11: The 11 High-Stakes Checks This document is the companion-material placeholder for Chapter 11 of The Uncompromised Citizen: The Field Guide for Ordinary Decision-Making, by Citizen111. When a decision could cause serious harm, damage critical systems, or create consequences that are difficult to reverse, ordinary decision-making may not be enough. The 11 High-Stakes Checks help readers examine changing conditions, verify assumptions, recognize warning signs, test safeguards, and ensure someone has the practical authority to stop when necessary. Planned companion materials: Heroes of Agency: Eleven historical case studies, including Chesley “Sully” Sullenberger and Jeffrey Skiles, Frances Oldham Kelsey, and Rick Rescorla—people who demonstrated preparation, independent judgment, and responsibility under pressure. The More You Know: The eleven checks, the Stop Test, cascading failures, independent verification, and six practical scenarios. Printable Exercises: The “Before You Say YES” worksheet and printable High-Stakes Check Card for examining risks, changing conditions, missing evidence, and stop authority. Deeper Dives: Aviation and industrial safety, medical decisions, rushed public projects, automated denials, AI and robotics, and the importance of maintaining meaningful human oversight. References: Original records, historical investigations, safety findings, supporting evidence, and additional reading related to the eleven historical cases and prevention of serious harm. These materials supplement—not replace—qualified expertise, established safety procedures, and appropriate emergency protocols. Additional materials, downloads, and links will be added in future versions. Part of the Mirror111 initiative. Read the full manuscript: https://mirror111.com/publications
