candidates.title: HandUMI: A Modular Hand-Worn Parallel-Jaw Interface for Robot-Free Bimanual Data Capture
candidates.abstract: HandUMI captures robot-free bimanual demonstrations with a hand-worn parallel-jaw interface. Swappable fingertips match the robot's installed gripper; Quest/PICO controllers track hands and encoders measure aperture. Robot-agnostic recordings are retargeted by inverse kinematics to seven simulated bimanual arms (median position error $\leq 1.2$ mm; $\leq 4.7$% of episodes rejected). On bimanual towel folding, 562 robot-free demonstrations train policies on real PiPER arms: ACT succeeds in 12/20 attempts and fine-tuned $π_{0.5}$ in 7/20; ACT on the first 101 and base $π_{0.5}$ each succeed in 0/20. Hardware and software are open source (Apache-2.0), and a pair costs USD 557 with Quest 3S, excluding the optional ZED Mini and host computer. Project website: https://murobotics.ai/research/handumi.

candidates.title: Early US Experience Using the Symani for Robotic‐Assisted Microvascular Surgery
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: Robotic-assisted microsurgery provides motion scaling, tremor filtration, and enhanced visualization, offering potential advantages for complex microsurgical tasks. Following Food and Drug Administration authorization, the Symani Surgical System was introduced into clinical practice in the United States in April 2024. This study presents the first multi-institutional US experience with Symani, evaluating feasibility, reconstructive outcomes, and technical challenges during its inaugural year of use in the United States. METHODS: All robotic-assisted procedures performed between April 2024 and April 2025 at two tertiary academic centers were retrospectively reviewed. Demographics, clinical indications, flap type, and anastomotic details were extracted. Primary outcomes were anastomotic patency and flap loss. Secondary outcomes included overall surgical complications and conversion to conventional microsurgery. RESULTS: Twenty-seven patients underwent robotic-assisted microsurgical procedures. Median age was 51 [IQR 39-63] years; 55.6% were female, and 74.1% identified as White. Indications included oncologic reconstruction (48.1%), trauma (18.5%), degenerative bony disease (14.8%), infection (11.1%), peripheral vascular disease (3.7%), and morphea (3.7%). A wide variety of flaps were performed, most commonly deep inferior epigastric perforator (DIEP) (44.4%), free vascularized fibular grafts (18.5%), and scapular flaps (14.8%). Robotic assistance was employed for 27 arterial anastomoses (84.4%), three venous anastomoses (9.4%), and two nerve coaptations (6.3%). Anastomotic configuration was predominantly end-to-end (71.9%). No flap loss occurred. One patient (3.7%) required re-exploration for pedicle kinking. Two conversions to conventional non-robotic microsurgery were required (7.4%). CONCLUSIONS: Early US multi-institutional experience demonstrates the Symani system is feasible and safe across diverse reconstructive procedures, enabling reliable microvascular anastomoses and nerve coaptations with minimal complications and no flap loss.

candidates.title: Translating the Language of the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Primer
candidates.abstract: Translating the Language of the COVID-19 Pandemic is an essential Primer for translators, offering a comprehensive exploration of the terminology and language that shaped the global response to an unprecedented crisis. Divided into three insightful chapters, the book delves into the linguistic and technological dimensions of the pandemic. The first chapter, The outbreak , explores key pandemic terms like shelter-in-place , the new normal , and flattening the curve , reflecting significant events during the crisis. The second chapter, Migration online, examines the pandemic's impact on education and the arts, highlighting their transition to virtual platforms. The third chapter, Fire of genius, fuel of survival— inspired by Abraham Lincoln's lecture on Discoveries and Inventions —showcases global innovations that mitigated the pandemic's effects and analyzes the vaccine rollout, covering its successes and challenges. The book includes an English–French glossary of 1,500 pandemic-related terms, covering scientific and everyday language, along with appendices listing patents and links to virtual performances. A detailed index ensures easy navigation of topics. This comprehensive resource serves as both a Primer for translators on the language that defined the COVID-19 pandemic and a reader-friendly presentation of international mitigation technologies and innovations. This book provides a research-supported retrospective analysis with enduring relevance, and features a bilingual compendium of pandemic terminology with potential for expansion into additional languages. It is an invaluable resource for translators, linguists, and researchers seeking to understand the intersection of language, technology, and human resilience during one of the most challenging periods in modern history.

candidates.title: STARFARM: A hybrid, spatially explicit agent-based framework that couples crop physiology and socio-hydrology for exploring agricultural adaptation pathways in mega-deltas
Fuzzy logic driven real time fertiliser recommendation system with internet of things-integrated soil and environmental sensor suite
candidates.abstract: Precision nutrient management is essential for improving crop productivity while minimising fertiliser misuse, production costs and environmental impacts. This paper presents a low-cost, portable and real-time fertiliser recommendation system that integrates an Internet of Things (IoT)-based soil and environmental sensor suite with a fuzzy logic inference engine. The proposed system acquires key soil parameters, including nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), pH and electrical conductivity (EC), along with environmental data and geolocation information. Sensor readings are calibrated and processed to estimate nutrient deficiencies and soil conditions. A fuzzy inference system utilises crop type, crop growth stage and nutrient deficiency percentages as inputs to generate crop-specific fertiliser recommendations for urea, diammonium phosphate (DAP), single super phosphate (SSP) and muriate of potash (MOP). An additional pH reclamation module recommends suitable amendments such as lime or gypsum. To enhance usability, a mobile application and Python-based dashboard were developed, enabling users with no prior agricultural expertise to select the crop and growth stage, deploy the sensor in the field and receive actionable recommendations, including fertiliser quantities, estimated costs and labour requirements. The system was validated using 100 soil samples collected from Southern India. The fuzzy logic output was tested across more than 40 crops and all four growth stages; however, the fuzzy-versus-conventional mathematical comparison is presented for 10 representative soil samples using sugarcane at the basal stage to provide a uniform comparison. Experimental results showed that the fuzzy recommendations followed the same recommendation trend as conventional mathematical calculations, with quantitative differences varying by fertiliser and sample. The proposed framework demonstrates a practical and scalable solution for real-time, in-field nutrient management and informed agricultural decision-making.

candidates.title: Who Benefits From Robots? Gender and Technology on the Shop Floor
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT The introduction of robots has produced uneven benefits for workers with different skills, occupations, and genders. We examine a qualitative case study of a Norwegian auto‐supply plant to ask why gender inequalities often persist on the shop floor, even in a gender‐progressive institutional context. The introduction of CNC machines in the plant made machining more like the female‐dominated assembly line in skill and strength demands, yet machining remained male‐dominated, with higher pay and greater investment in automation compared to the assembly line. The authors argue that persistent assumptions about economic value and gendered institutions and practices explain these unequal outcomes.

candidates.title: The Digital Commons and the Infrastructural Power of Generative AI
candidates.abstract: Abstract The use and construction of generative AI reshape how information flows in society and who controls it. This paper investigates these changes and assesses their potential repercussions for the future of our shared information infrastructure. The findings elucidate an emergent social dilemma in which the use and construction of generative AI tend to degrade and compete with our existing infrastructure, while also layering atop the commons new infrastructure that is, by its current design, centralised and mediated. Yet, alternative futures that preserve the collective nature of our infrastructure remain possible. As a first step toward such futures, this paper concludes by exploring interventions to promote a decentralised and unmediated generative commons.

candidates.title: Exploring the evolution of AI ethics in CS ethics courses
candidates.abstract: Background and Context Building on a previous study analyzing CS ethics course requirements across CS undergraduate programs at 250 universities, this paper explores the content of a subset of computing ethics courses from US universities.Objective We aim to examine the evolution of content related to artificial intelligence (AI) and AI ethics in these courses, and hypothesize that the growth of AI in both academic and industrial settings has precipitated an increased focus on the ethics of AI in undergraduate CS courses.Method Through an online search, we manually construct a data corpus consisting of 116 CS ethics courses from 93 universities in the United States. Subsequently, we conduct both a keyword analysis of course titles, descriptions, and syllabi for these courses, and qualitatively evaluate the subset of 54 courses for which a course syllabus or course website could be found.Findings We find that, while the introduction of content on AI in ethics courses takes many forms, the majority of content only started to be added beginning in 2020. In the years since, more courses have revised their syllabi to address the social implications of AI, while some courses that already incorporated AI content have begun to deepen their engagement with the ethical challenges posed by AI.Implications Synthesizing our findings, we propose a three-phase classification of the integration of AI ethics content into the curriculum, and advocate for increased attention to the legal, policy, and governance frameworks necessary to guide the development and use of “responsible” AI systems.

candidates.title: How robot gender shapes customer experience in phygital retail
candidates.abstract: As service robots populate unmanned retail settings, design choices shape customer experience. This study contributes to the Phygital Service Economy (PSE) literature by examining whether robot gender cues affect customer satisfaction, and whether this depends on the customer’s own gender. A moderated serial mediation model (PROCESS 83; N = 572) tested social presence and engagement as mediators and respondent gender as a moderator, as respondents evaluated male- or female-presenting robots in physical and digital forms. Robot gender had no direct effect on satisfaction; its influence operated indirectly through social presence and engagement, and only among male respondents, who perceived male-presenting robots as more socially present than female-presenting robots, interpreted through a social identity and similarity-attraction lens. These findings extend gendered HRI research into retail contexts, identify social presence as a key mechanism linking robot gender to satisfaction, and show that gendered robot design effects are conditional on customer gender.

candidates.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
candidates.abstract: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy. Despite these advances, the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, a reliable evaluation framework, or a research roadmap. We argue that Embodied System 2, realized by a foundation model together with an embodied harness, forms the decision-making core of agentic robotics. Its central challenge is to translate general-purpose reasoning into effective and verifiable actions under physical constraints such as limited reaction time, mechanical limits, unpredictable environment changes, and irreversible consequences. Motivated by this perspective, we propose an evaluation framework that measures both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance. Furthermore, we identify the principles that carry over from digital to physical agents and the challenges that must be addressed to achieve reliable physical autonomy. On top of the Embodied System 2 and the evaluation framework, we envision a research roadmap toward sustained autonomy: the ability to perform work safely and reliably with progressively broader responsibility, from executing individual primitives to fulfilling standing roles.

candidates.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
candidates.abstract: Robot-use agents (RUAs) have emerged as a promising approach to general-purpose robot control. However, strong performance has so far been achieved only by frontier proprietary models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, whereas open-weight models remain substantially less capable. We show that an open-weight 27B reasoning model can be trained to use real robots natively through reinforcement learning, entirely in simulation and without demonstrations. Like a computer-use agent (CUA), the model observes the environment, reasons in a chain of thought, and generates the next end-effector pose, without any harness. We build a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics (PEAR) and use it to train the model on simulated robot tasks at scale with robot-use reinforcement learning (RURL), mirroring how frontier models acquire computer use. We find that the skills acquired in simulation generalize well beyond the training tasks: they transfer to an unseen robot, to the real world, and to novel instructions. After training on LIBERO and RoboDojo in simulation, the model succeeds in 60% of our trials on a real dual-arm robot, whereas the base model succeeds in none. On LIBERO, training raises the success rate from 1.6% to 74.4%, approaching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol at maximum reasoning effort. Compared with $π_{0.5}$, a vision-language-action model fine-tuned on demonstrations, our model is substantially more robust to changes in the task itself. On LIBERO-Pro, $π_{0.5}$ succeeds in only 0.75% of episodes when assigned a new task in a familiar scene whereas our model succeeds in 57.4%. Finally, the model retains its general capabilities, with no measurable degradation on nine reasoning, coding and vision benchmarks. These results highlight robot-use reinforcement learning as a promising component of foundation-model post-training.

candidates.title: Designing an AI Companion: Preservice Teachers Learning to Teach STEM with Robotics
candidates.abstract: Research shows that preservice teachers’ self-efficacy to teach with technology impacts how they implement technology in teaching practice. In many countries, elementary teachers are expected to teach all STEM subjects, even though they have no undergraduate preparation in STEM. Therefore, an important goal of Teacher Education is to enhance elementary preservice teachers’ confidence to teach STEM subjects with technology such as Educational Robotics (ER). This conceptual paper reports on the theoretical foundations and structural design features of an artificial learning companion (ALC) designed to support preservice teachers learning how to teach STEM with ER. While ALCs have been reported to enhance students’ learning, motivation, and self-regulation, this paper responds to calls to explore ALCs as facilitators of learning by negotiation. The ALC design is therefore explained in terms of Vygotsky’s Sociocultural Learning Theory, specifically the Zone of Proximal Development, instructional scaffolding, and prompt engineering design. Generative AI (GenAI) will serve as an ALC to scaffold learning tasks such as coding. The ALC will function as a responsive scaffold by offering task-specific support through questions, hints, feedback, and reflection with gradual reduction in support as preservice teachers’ competence and confidence increase. This work illustrates how a GenAI ALC can simultaneously support preservice teachers as learners of STEM and as future STEM instructors. The paper provides STEM teacher educators with a concrete, adaptable model for embedding AI scaffolds into robotics-based learning to foster reflective and pedagogical thinking.

candidates.title: Organizational Structure with an Open Source Culture
candidates.abstract: Corporate open source contribution is often discussed in terms of total contribution volume or the presence of prominent maintainers. However, to understand whether an open source culture has permeated an organization, it is necessary to look not only at a small number of high-frequency contributors, but also at how many contributors exist outside that core across a wide range of activity levels, and whether the organization has created conditions in which people can participate upstream when needed. This paper reanalyzes one year of contributor-level contribution data previously obtained and preserved from CNCF DevStats. The dataset covers 3,159 contributors from 18 large IT companies that had been selected at the time from the CNCF Top 50 contribution companies based on having at least 10,000 employees. Contributor activity was divided into 13 bands increasing by roughly a factor of two, and further grouped into three categories: **Ad-hoc (1–16 contributions)**, **Active (17–512)**, and **Top (513 or more)**. This makes it possible to observe not merely “how many Top contributors exist,” but how contributors are distributed continuously from low-frequency to high-frequency activity as a **Contributor Activity Spectrum**. Across all 18 companies, 1,528 contributors (48.4%) were Ad-hoc, 1,160 (36.7%) were Active, and 471 (14.9%) were Top contributors. Among the five companies in the CNCF Contribution Top 10, the average number of contributors per company was 484, consisting of 232.6 Ad-hoc, 175.4 Active, and 76.0 Top contributors. The average declined to 86.4 contributors among companies ranked 11–25 and to 38.4 among those ranked 26–50. Furthermore, all five Top 10 companies had contributors in every one of the 13 activity bands, forming an uninterrupted continuum from low-frequency to high-frequency activity. In contrast, companies ranked 26–50 had an average of 3.1 empty bands within their activity ranges. Several showed a separation between low-frequency and high-frequency contributors, or a concentration in only a particular high-frequency band. The characteristic observed among higher-ranked companies is therefore neither “having only Heroes” nor “having everyone contribute equally.” Rather, they combine a strong core of contributors with large and continuous layers of Active and Ad-hoc contributors around that core. This suggests that these organizations may have established a state in which many engineers can make the contributions they need when they need to—in other words, a state in which they can participate upstream **ad hoc**. Such a state may be associated with company-wide rules that enable open source contribution, operational and support functions such as OSPOs, and a culture that recognizes contribution as a normal part of engineering work.

candidates.title: Recreating northeastern lifestyles in Osaka, Japan: interpersonal relationships through Bathing and Yangge dancing among Zanryu Koji
candidates.abstract: Background: The Zanryu Koji (残留孤児), Japanese children separated from their families during the 1945 Soviet invasion of Manchuria and raised in northeastern China, constitute one of East Asia's most historically complex diasporic communities. Resettled in Osaka from the late 1970s, this population negotiates a distinctive double displacement: culturally Chinese yet legally Japanese. Aim: This study examines how Zanryu Koji in Osaka recreates northeastern Chinese lifestyles through communal bathing and Yangge folk dancing, and how these practices shape their interpersonal relationships and cultural identity. Setting: A Zanryu Koji community association in Osaka, Japan, operating a weekly Yangge dance group and regular communal bathing routine. Methods: Qualitative semi-structured interviews were conducted with fifteen purposively sampled participants. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results: Four themes emerged: the bathhouse as a Third Space of unguarded belonging; Yangge as embodied cultural memory and relational infrastructure; role differentiation as the architecture of fictive kinship; and bodily practice as diasporic identity negotiation. Conclusion: Communal bathing and Yangge dancing function not as instruments of cultural preservation but as generative practices through which the community actively produces belonging, fictive kinship, and a distinctively diasporic northeastern Chinese identity in Japan. Findings advance theories of embodied belonging, the Third Space, and integration-based acculturation, with implications for policies that support older migrant communities.

candidates.title: Research on application of live insulation cleaning technology for electrical cabinets of heavy-duty track maintenance machinery
candidates.abstract: Purpose Heavy-duty track maintenance machinery, including ballast cleaners, rail grinders and tamping machines, operates under harsh working conditions mixed with dust, iron filings and oil contamination. Pollutants easily adhere to circuit boards, terminal blocks, wiring harnesses and switch components inside electrical cabinets, resulting in reduced insulation resistance, equipment overheating, electrostatic discharge and frequent short-circuit faults. The conventional method of manual air-blow cleaning with the power disconnected suffers from low cleaning efficiency, high operation and maintenance costs and heavy downtime losses. Design/methodology/approach Supported by a dedicated scientific research project jointly undertaken by the Science and Technology Research Institute of Daqin Railway Co., Ltd., Taiyuan Track Maintenance Machinery Depot, Taiyuan University of Technology and Shanxi Angtuo Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd., this paper systematically presents the development approaches, key technologies, performance parameters of the complete cleaning equipment, field test data and comprehensive benefits of the integrated live insulation cleaning system for electrical cabinets of heavy-duty track maintenance machinery. The contamination-induced insulation degradation mechanism is analyzed; comparative tests against competing mainstream cleaning technologies are conducted, and statistical hypothesis testing is adopted to assess the significance of the observed differences. Findings The project developed an integrated live cleaning system comprising a high-insulation, eco-friendly cleaning fluid, an intelligent high-pressure cleaning main unit and an extended universal cleaning spray gun. Originality/value The research findings show that electrical cabinets can be cleaned in depth while the equipment remains energized. The technology's cleaning efficiency is more than seven times that of conventional manual power-off cleaning; the insulation impedance of the equipment is increased by four times, electrostatic hazards are significantly mitigated and the equipment failure rate is reduced by 55%. A statistical t-test demonstrates that the improvements in insulation impedance, operating temperature and static voltage are statistically significant (p < 0.05). The technology substantially shortens maintenance downtime, balances safety, production efficiency and full-lifecycle maintenance requirements in railway track maintenance, and can provide a standardized technical solution for predictive maintenance of electrical systems of heavy-duty track maintenance machinery across China's railway network. It should be noted that this technology focuses on post-contamination remediation cleaning; further research is required to develop a quantitative contamination degradation model to enable full-scale predictive early warning.

candidates.title: Sex Robots, Misogyny, and Artificial Intimacy in Contemporary Speculative Fiction: A Posthuman Feminist Analysis
candidates.abstract: This article offers a posthuman feminist analysis of contemporary literary fiction featuring sex dolls and robots, including Sierra Greer's Annie Bot (2024), Jeanette Winterson's Frankissstein (2019), and Paolo Bacigalupi's “Mika Model” (2016). It examines how the design and commodification of artificial sexual companions reproduce cultural misogyny, sustain gender inequality, and reinforce feminised technological servitude. Drawing on Kathleen Richardson's critique of the sex robot and situating these texts alongside contemporary misogynistic discourse associated with figures such as Nick Fuentes and Andrew Tate, the article situates speculative fiction in direct relation to ongoing social and ideological formations. It argues that these works move beyond a feminist critique of sex robots as misogynistic commodities by tracing a progression from commodified spectacle to demands for recognition in the face of exploitation and, finally, to emergent autonomy, which recasts the sex robot as a contested figure suspended between objectification and ethical subjectivity.

candidates.title: Robotics for Persons with Intellectual Disabilities: A Review in the Indian Context
candidates.abstract: This paper explores the intersection of robotics and disability studies, focusing on its transformative potential for inclusion, rehabilitation, and education, particularly for individuals with intellectual disabilities (ID). Initial research, including Conti (2015), showcased the effectiveness of robotic models in enhancing support for persons with ID, while subsequent empirical studies (Shukla et al., 2019) confirmed their benefits for users and caregivers. The integration of humanoid robots in educational settings has demonstrated versatility I n diverse pedagogical contexts (Alemi & Bahramipour, 2019). Systematic reviews have further consolidated evidence of robotics' applications across social, cognitive, and physical domains, indicating a shift toward scalable, context-sensitive solutions. In India, recent advancements in robotics complement traditional therapeutic practices, enhancing motivation and communication for persons with intellectual disabilities (PwID). The study highlights innovative initiatives, such as robotic library services (Maddisetty, 2024) and the integration of artificial intelligence in education (Rajput et al., 2025), while addressing cultural perceptions and ethical considerations among special educators (Ashwini et al., 2024). The paper underscores the need for culturally sensitive approaches in adopting robotics, contrasting the distinct trajectories of robotics development in India and the West. While Indian initiatives focus on affordability and cultural adaptation, Western approaches prioritize socially assistive and rehabilitation technologies. This review aims to chart a path for inclusive, contextually relevant robotics in disability care, enriching the global discourse on this vital intersection.

candidates.title: Between Risk, Recognition, and Necessity: How Open-Source Project Maintainers Perceive and Navigate CVEs Through Reporting and Resolving Vulnerabilities
candidates.abstract: Researchers have investigated automated security impact and analysis techniques that leverage the content of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs). Understanding the perspectives of open-source software (OSS) project maintainers, especially those who historically lack a security background and have little to no targeted funding to secure OSS projects, is currently understudied. In this study, we investigate how OSS maintainers who have created or triaged security vulnerabilities perceive, use, and work around the CVE system. We use a mixed-methods approach through a listing survey (n 1 =77), a Likert-scale survey (n 2 =109), and interviews (n 3 =24) to identify and categorize 36 factors into OSS maintainers' perceptions of CVE value, challenges associated with CVEs, and wants for future vulnerability identification and resolution features. We find that fix prioritization and assessing project health are the most important benefits for OSS maintainers, while producing fixes and how CVEs lack project context are the most challenging to overcome. Despite this, OSS maintainers express adaptability and openness to alternative systems, provided that they offer credibility, visibility, and ecosystem compatibility, and most desire less hands-on involvement while evaluating vulnerabilities. This work has implications for the future design of inclusive, OSS developer-centered vulnerability disclosure infrastructures, and gives a comprehensive insight into how current aspects of vulnerability identifiers work or do not work for the OSS community.

candidates.title: JEV-VAD: Efficient Semantic Endpointing via Task-First Conditioning and Decoder-Prefix Pruning
candidates.abstract: Semantic endpointing must distinguish a completed turn from a temporary pause, yet its binary output does not require the full generation pathway of an audio-language model. We propose JEV-VAD, an ASR-free framework that combines task-first conditioning, a scalar endpoint readout, and decoder-prefix pruning. The question and completion criteria are placed before audio tokens, allowing causal decoder attention to construct audio states conditioned on the endpointing objective. A dedicated scalar head maps the assistant-prefix state directly to a stop probability, removing transcript generation, answer decoding, and vocabulary-sized output projection. To reduce representation cost, decoder-prefix pruning physically retains only the initial decoder blocks. Matched head refitting then identifies which retained depths provide useful endpoint information under a common adaptation budget. The framework is built on Qwen3-ASR-0.6B and adapted through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning for calibrated decisions. Together, these components address input conditioning, output complexity, and decoder depth within one endpointing framework. Experiments on EOT-bench show cross-language transfer from English endpoint supervision and useful discrimination in shallow prefixes, supporting a selectable quality-resource trade-off.

candidates.title: Autonomous Trail Racing with a Bicycle Robot
candidates.abstract: Navigating off-road trails on a mountain bike requires diverse locomotion skills, including aerial maneuvers, cornering, and slip recovery, paired with sophisticated perception for scene understanding. Translating these capabilities to autonomous, two-wheeled robots remains a formidable challenge. We show that autonomous, high-speed trail navigation can be achieved through a single idea: encoding the trail as a semantic layer of the terrain. In simulation, this layer embeds the navigation task into the training environment; during deployment, it is reconstructed onboard from camera and LiDAR data. First, we introduce a unified learning framework that treats local navigation and locomotion as a joint optimization problem, bypassing the twist or pose command interface of classical control hierarchies. With fixed reward weights, the same framework produces both trail racing and agile parkour, shaped only through terrain semantics and episode length. Second, our perception pipeline combines a frozen vision foundation model with a lightweight dual-head decoder that predicts per-pixel terrain semantics and confidence scores, which are fused with LiDAR range measurements into an egocentric semantic elevation map at 30 Hz onboard an NVIDIA AGX Orin. We validate our framework on the Ultra Mobility Vehicle (UMV), a bicycle robot that autonomously raced across all sections of a kilometer-long, unstructured mountain bike trail at speeds exceeding 5 m/s and averaging 3.26 m/s. In simulation, our policy fails up to an order of magnitude less often than hierarchical baselines while driving faster.

candidates.title: sK/n: towards a seamful grammar of distributed sentience
candidates.abstract: This paper argues that technical sensing does not extend the human sensory system but instead establishes a distinct, non-experiential sensory regime. Rather than amplifying human faculties, sensor-based systems register, process and compute signals according to operational logics that are irreducible to embodied experience. To conceptualize this shift, the paper introduces sK/n as a media-theoretical figure that articulates the relationship between technical skin (sK) and human, embodied skin (n). sK/n marks a split sensorium in which heterogeneous sensing regimes become operationally entangled yet remain non-convergent, and is structured by translation, asynchrony and temporal disjunction. Drawing on examples from e-skin technologies, interface design, (soft-)robotic systems, and artistic practice, the paper shows how touch and tactile input are increasingly translated into data-driven processes. This transformation is framed as a shift from multisensual to multisentient configurations of sensing, in which sensing is distributed across bodies, technical infrastructures, and computational systems. Rather than describing the machine sensorium as a system in opposition to a unified human sensorium, the paper proposes sK/n as a media-theoretical grammar for analysing distributed, asynchronous sensing regimes.

candidates.title: ARTS: An Open-Source, Reproducible Three-Arm Platform for Autonomy Research in Minimally Invasive Surgery
candidates.abstract: Research on surgical autonomy needs open platforms that any laboratory can build, yet the most widely shared platform depends on donated clinical hardware, and open alternatives on industrial arms each lack part of the surgical chain. We present the Autonomous Robotic Translational System (ARTS), an open-source three-arm platform for autonomy research in minimally invasive surgery, built entirely from purchasable parts for about USD 137,000. Two UR5e arms hold wristed da Vinci X/Xi instruments, a UR5 arm holds a stereo endoscope with two FLIR cameras, the surgeon console provides haptic handles, footswitches and a stereo viewer, and a hardware stop independent of the software lets a supervisor freeze all three arms in place. The ROS 2 software pins every dependency, installs from the same scripts on bare metal or in containers, and records stereo images with hardware-measured timing. On the real arms, ARTS commands each arm at its controller's full rate (e.g., 500 Hz on the UR5e), the two cameras expose within 12 microseconds of each other, hand motion reaches the arm in 58 ms, and the endoscope image reaches the monitor in 68 ms. The ISO 9283 pose repeatability is 0.14-0.25 mm, comparable to a da Vinci Research Kit (dVRK) Classic arm on the same protocol, and an optical tracker measured a mean remote-center-of-motion error of 0.34-0.37 mm. Three expert and three novice operators performed the Fundamentals of Laparoscopic Surgery (FLS) peg transfer through a laparoscopic trainer box, and one of the experts sutured on a suture pad. The hardware designs, firmware and software are available at https://github.com/MRE-Lab-UMD/arts.

An Empirical Study of Maintainer-Identified AI Slop Pull Requests in Free and Open Source Software Projects
candidates.abstract: The FOSS ecosystem has always relied on outside contributions, notably through issues or Pull Requests (PRs), to sustain itself. With the advance of GenAI, the barrier to contributing to FOSS projects has never been lower, leading to the emergence of AI slop PRs: low-quality, low-value generated PRs. Past studies have examined AI slop PRs through theoretical, platform-level, or practitioner-account frames, but not at the project level. To this end, this study investigates the incidence of maintainer-identified AI slop PRs in FOSS projects by focusing on PRs flagged as slop by maintainers. Using a mixed-methods approach, we trace the origins of maintainer-identified AI slop PRs, quantify their volume in FOSS projects, describe their characteristics, and highlight maintainers' reasons for flagging or closing them. Our results show that the volume of maintainer-identified AI slop PRs increased in mid-2025, peaking in May 2026. These PRs are mostly additive, rarely merged, and typically closed within 3 days. The authors of these PRs disclosed the use of AI in 14% of cases, with 1% disclosing after a maintainer's request. Most PRs are closed or marked as slop without any reason provided by the maintainer. Based on our open coding, reasons range from concrete elements, like build failures, to ideological or intuitive (i.e., "looks AI to me"). This exploratory study captures a phenomenon in its early stage and highlights GenAI's potential impact on FOSS, emphasizing the pressure it puts on maintainers and the need to shift current open-source development practices.

candidates.title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Water Security in Western Rajasthan: A Study of Selected Renewable Energy Companies
candidates.abstract: The western parts of Rajasthan experience water scarcity owing to the arid nature of the climate and low amount of rainfall in the area. As such, the CSR programs of renewable energy companies have immense importance in conserving the water resources as well as uplifting the rural population. This research analyzes the water-based CSR initiatives of Suzlon Energy Limited and Adani Green Energy Limited (AGEL) in western Rajasthan. Using the descriptive research methodology, the paper is based only on corporate annual reports and any other available corporate public reports. The analysis is conducted by classifying and examining company's interventions in pond construction, desilting, and construction of water infrastructure. It is found that both the companies have carried out many water projects; however, type of activities and places have varied in different financial years. Furthermore, it is found that there is a serious lack of information in the corporation's reports, especially about the number of beneficiaries and project viability in the long run. It is concluded that the water projects by CSR programs have great potential to increase water security of rural areas provided they are monitored constantly.

candidates.title: When does online vision-language inference help? A survey of socially aware robot navigation
candidates.abstract: Abstract Vision-language models (VLMs) and large language models are increasingly built into the navigation stacks of robots that share space with people, where the models read cues that occupancy maps omit, such as a raised hand or a conversing group. This survey organizes 41 cases reported from 2024 to 2026, 34 on socially aware navigation and 7 adjacent mechanism extensions, by where the model enters the stack: scene interpretation, cost modulation, subgoal or path proposal, hierarchical coordination, direct action output and offline transfer or generation. For each of these six patterns we describe representative systems and their reported results, and we review the datasets, simulators, benchmarks and metrics behind them. We then discuss what the reported comparisons establish about running the model online, separating system utility, component contribution and online necessity. In these comparisons, cue-aware systems improved the outcomes that hinge on their cue, although whole-system differences limit attribution to the VLM; in one offline study, a model selector helped on hard selections and hurt on routine ones; in one deployment, delayed advice stayed useful when fused with current plans; model-supervised students navigated without runtime teacher queries, but online, cached and distilled alternatives have not been compared with student computation included; and better answers have not yet been linked to better behavior. We also define an invocation ratio (model requests per control decision), propose a minimum reporting set for deployment comparisons, and outline open challenges in real-time reasoning, spatial grounding and safety.

candidates.title: The Positronic Aid: The Servitude of Robotic Altruism in Asimov’s I, Robot
candidates.abstract: Science fiction is one of the types of speculative fiction that traverses imagination based on discoveries, scientific techniques, and principles. It is an emerging field in this modern world. It encourages imagination and creativity, allowing authors to envision worlds, technologies, and societies that defy conventional norms and expectations. It challenges many critical interventions on future and the possibilities of science and technology. Today, technology has developed very well. Artificial intelligence is ruling the world of technology till date. Many robots are being developed in many countries. They resemble human beings in general. They do many works like human beings and are also capable of doing things that humans never thought of. They talk and act like humans and possess a lot of memory. One of the biggest achievements in the field of science and technology is the invention of robots. They are developed for the betterment of humans. They can’t replace humans at any cost and are in no way inferior to humans. This research paper discusses the advantages of robots in the present scenario. The book taken into study is I robot by Isaac Asimov. Robots are always beneficial to the entire human race. They are not produced to harm anyone.

candidates.title: From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self
candidates.abstract: Abstract The experience of being, or having, a self—contained by our bodies and able to act in the world—comes naturally to us as humans, along with a feeling of being the same self from day to day and of seeing others as also being selves. But what is the self, and how is it constituted? In this theme issue, we explore these questions through contemporary analytic approaches, in philosophy, psychology and neuroscience, that seek to understand the human self through conceptual and empirical investigations. Alongside this, we also explore synthetic approaches that attempt to construct a sense of self, or some part thereof, in artefacts such as robots. Our overall aim is to deepen the understanding of self as a foundational aspect of the human condition and explore both theoretical and practical implications of the emerging science of the self. In this introduction, we review the scope and content of the theme issue and argue that these complementary research strands can be seen as converging towards a ‘systems’ view that sees the self as an emergent property of an embodied, dynamical and informational system that continuously distinguishes, regulates and models itself through processes that sustain and explain its own existence. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue ‘From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self’.

candidates.title: Active Inference and Predictive Processing for Skill Learning: Implications for Skill Acquisition in Coaching Practice
candidates.abstract: This paper explores the potential of the Active Inference Framework (AIF) and Predictive Processing (PP) to advance our understanding of skill and motor learning with a key focus on introducing these concepts to coaches and highlighting their practical implications. Conceptual frameworks such as Information Processing (IP) and Ecological Dynamics (ED) have contributed significantly to the field of skill acquisition. Despite recent efforts to reconcile these perspectives, however, their fundamentally different theoretical foundations concerning perception, cognition and learning processes pose substantial challenges for integration. Although ED has made valuable contributions through its focus on perception-action coupling and direct interaction with the environment, it involves adopting a radical ontological stance that emphasises rejecting traditional cognitive constructs that can complicate practical applications in coaching. Conversely, IP's reliance on concepts such as stored motor programs and the view of the brain as a computer-like processor can limit its ability to account for the dynamic, emergent nature of skill acquisition in real-world contexts. We suggest that AIF offers a parsimonious perspective, accommodating the dynamic, embodied and enactive nature of skill acquisition without the necessity of committing to either framework's specific assumptions. This perspective provides practitioners with a coherent and flexible framework for understanding and designing skill learning interventions, offering a practically useful account of skill acquisition for coaching practice.

candidates.title: The double-edged sword of virtual influencer anthropomorphism: a paradoxical framework of social presence and identity threat
candidates.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how the perceived physical and psychological anthropomorphism of virtual influencers shape consumers’ attitude toward virtual influencers through the competing psychological pathways of social presence and identity threat. Design/methodology/approach Through a cross-sectional survey, a sample of 448 Instagram users in Egypt was collected and analyzed using CB-SEM through AMOS v.23. Findings Both perceived physical and psychological anthropomorphism of virtual influencers have a positive influence on both social presence and identity threat. Importantly, both social presence and identity threat concurrently mediate the relationships between both dimensions of anthropomorphism and attitudes toward virtual influencers. Therefore, both dimensions of anthropomorphism influence consumers’ attitudes toward virtual influencers through the positive mediating role of social presence and the negative mediating role of identity threat. Research limitations/implications The study expands anthropomorphism research to the virtual influencer context by showing that anthropomorphism is not unequivocally superior. Therefore, grounding in social presence and social identity theory, we suggest that anthropomorphism is a double-edged sword in shaping attitudes toward virtual influencers. Practical implications Both designers and marketers employing virtual influencers should consider the multi-dimensionality anthropomorphism. Moreover, they should aim to maximize social presence while reducing identity threat when utilizing virtual influencers. Originality/value This study conceptualizes anthropomorphism as a multifaceted construct composed of physical and psychological dimensions and it can work through two opposing positive and negative pathways.

candidates.title: BioMARS 2.0: a robotic biologist for formulating and adapting biological experiments
candidates.abstract: Biological experimentation is not reducible to a single optimization problem, but requires decisions at multiple levels of abstraction: translating scientific knowledge into experimental procedures, adapting culture conditions to measured phenotypes and selecting interventions that test biological hypotheses. Automating experimental execution does not, by itself, determine which experiments should be performed next or how they should change in response to biological feedback. Here we introduce BioMARS, a human-in-the-loop multi-agent robotic system that connects knowledge-guided experimental decision-making with robotic execution and biological feedback. At the procedural level, BioMARS generated literature-grounded protocols and traceable action plans, improving expert-reviewed protocol quality scores across four model backends. At the parametric level, BioMARS used image-derived phenotypes from robotic retinal organoid culture to select subsequent experimental conditions, with higher reported scores in later rounds of the three-round experiment. At the intervention level, BioMARS nominated drug-repurposing candidates from biomedical evidence and advanced six candidates to wet-lab testing by researchers. Together, these studies demonstrate feedback-driven robotic biological experimentation within a framework that supports decisions about experimental procedures, culture conditions and biological interventions.

candidates.title: Telepresence Robotics for Isolated Children: Cross-Perspectives between Education and Hospitals
candidates.abstract: Telepresence robotics allows users to access a remote location and interact socially through a mobile robot as a proxy. Despite a huge potential, its deployment is nevertheless hampered by usability issues. In order to explore possible solutions, the workshop "Innovations and challenges in Frenchspeaking telepresence robotics" was held on November 4, 2025, as part of the 36th International Francophone Conference on Human-Machine Interaction (IHM 2025 6 ) in Toulouse. Based on two French case studies (the TED-i project 7 and the Buddy Guard project 8 ), 17 participants discussed four main themes by groups of four (design, network quality, interaction methods, and robot characterization) and proposed possible areas for improvement. In this article, we first present a comparison of the two case studies which, despite having different scopes, contexts, and objectives, share many similarities and common issues. We then discuss the areas for improvement that emerged from this comparison between telepresence robotics focused on continuity of education for students who are unable to attend school (TED-i) and telepresence robotics used in hospitals to recreate social ties between children and their families (Buddy Guard). These considerations open up promising perspectives of research for telepresence robotics.

candidates.title: ExoStack: A Modular and Reconfigurable Software Framework for Wearable Robotics Using ROS 2
candidates.abstract: Wearable robots depend on a software chain that links body-worn sensing to gait interpretation, assistance generation, and actuation. Personalization further requires each measured response to remain associated with the assistance parameters that generated it. This paper presents ExoStack, a modular ROS 2 framework for implementing that chain across embedded hubs and a host computer. Its Embedded Sensing and Actuation (ESA) library configures ESP32 boards as microROS sensing and actuation hubs. ExoCore supplies multi-hub synchronization, gait-event detection, profile generation, motion planning, cost evaluation, and human-in-the-loop (HIL) optimization as configuration-instantiated nodes. The PASE desktop application edits configurations, launches the processing stages, and visualizes ROS 2 topics. Hardware drivers and algorithm plugins can be added through defined interfaces without modifying the generic processing nodes. We characterize hub and planner timing on three embedded computers and demonstrate reuse on two pneumatic exosuits.

candidates.title: Soft sensors based on artificial neural networks for advanced bioprocess monitoring
candidates.abstract: Abstract This study presents the development and validation of artificial neural network (ANN)‐based soft sensors for the online estimation of key bioprocess variables during fed‐batch cultivations of Pseudomonas putida KT2442 producing medium‐chain‐length polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA), sustainable biopolymer precursors for bioplastics production. Since variables such as cell dry weight (CDW) and PHA concentration are typically accessible only through offline laboratory analyses, soft sensors represent a promising tool for implementing advanced process analytical technology (PAT) strategies for monitoring and control. Historical experimental data from two nominal cultivations and two cultivations with non‐standard behaviour, including significant feeding perturbations, were used for model development. ANN‐based soft sensors were designed in both global and multi‐phase configurations, where dedicated models were assigned to individual cultivation phases. Model training and validation were performed using leave‐one‐batch‐out (LOBO) cross‐validation to assess robustness and generalization capability. The best‐performing soft sensors achieved normalized root‐mean‐squared errors of approximately 4% for both CDW and PHA concentration estimation. The highest prediction accuracy was obtained for models utilizing capacitance measurements as input variables, followed by models combining capacitance measurements with cumulative oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production data. CDW soft sensors demonstrated higher robustness, maintaining reliable performance even for cultivations with non‐standard trajectories, whereas PHA soft sensors showed substantially higher sensitivity to process deviations and perturbations.

candidates.title: Pax Lambayeque? Trauma, interpersonal violence, and environment over 3,000 years in the Lambayeque Valley Complex, Peru
candidates.abstract: Previous research at archaeological sites in the coastal desert of northern Peru suggests strong human behavioral responses to environmental shifts. For example, at the Huaca de la Luna, Sicán, and the Huanchaquitos-las Llamas sites, paleopathological and stratigraphic analyses suggest that sociopolitical elites organized mass human sacrifices between 550−1450 CE in response to sudden intense increases in precipitation, possibly caused by El Niño-Southern Oscillation events. However, there has not yet been quantitative research into the relationship between non-ritualized violence and precipitation over the longue durée . To investigate the role climate change may have had on driving violence in the Peruvian desert coast outside of episodic sacrifice events, as well as accidental injuries, we modeled the relationship between highland precipitation, El Niño flood frequency, and osteological trauma in the Lambayeque Valley Complex. We pull paleoclimate data from the CHELSA climate simulations, and paleopathological data from the extensive work of the Lambayeque Valley Biohistory Project, yielding a total sample size of 1,659 individuals from a period of over 3,000 years. Ultimately, we detect no strong evidence for an association between environmental factors and interpersonal violence and find that non-ritual violence in the Lambayeque Valley Complex was rare (1.6%). These findings support previous meta-analytical work in the south central Andes, which found similar results in coastal and middle elevation communities. This study not only adds to our understanding of the range of human behavioral responses to climate changes but also proposes the hypothesis that mass sacrifice in the Lambayeque Valley Complex was politico-religious in nature rather than a Malthusian consequence of resource stress.

candidates.title: Axiomatic Software Design for Industrial Automation Systems
candidates.abstract: Industrial control and automation systems (iCAS) are not only essential for automating and controlling industrial processes, but they also serve as transformative enablers of progress in modern manufacturing. Their seamless integration with operational systems enhances efficiency, productivity, and reliability while reducing human intervention and operational costs. However, this very integration—central to the transition toward smart, fully digitalized factories and initiatives such as Industry 4.0—introduces an additional layer of complexity. This complexity demands greater flexibility from iCAS, making an anti-coupled design approach increasingly critical. This thesis aims to improve the software design of industrial control and automation systems by systematically addressing the persistent problem of coupling in current design practices. From the perspective of this study, a good design is one that satisfies all functional requirements while adhering to Suh’s two fundamental design axioms: the Independence Axiom, which ensures the elimination of coupling, and the Information Axiom, which evaluates the design’s complexity. Importantly, the Information Axiom can be meaningfully applied only after the Independence Axiom is satisfied; without functional independence, any assessment of design complexity becomes invalid. For this reason, the primary focus of this thesis is on the first axiom—developing and formalizing the principles of anti-coupled design for industrial control and automation systems through a systematic design framework based on axiomatic design theory. Building on axiomatic design theory, this research introduces a systematic method ology that guides iCAS designers from the highest level—interactions among design elements—to the lowest level—the candidates.title: System Optimizations for Cost-Efficient Agent Harnesses
candidates.abstract: AI agent harnesses play the critical role of providing LLMs with an interface to a computing environment. Recent studies show that AI agents' task-execution accuracy depends mostly on the LLM used, while harness-side variances such as system prompts or tools have minimal impact. Rather, such harness-side variances show a larger impact on the cost of agent executions, achieving cost reductions up to 2.6 times on the same model and task. To further explore these harness-side cost optimization opportunities, we analyze the cost accumulation patterns across various agent traces and identify system opportunities to reduce token use and LLM calls without modifying the model or affecting task accuracy. Based on this analysis, we design Agency, a harness interposition platform that provides a unified abstraction and allows easy and portable implementation of harness-side system optimizations on existing off-the-shelf harnesses such as Claude Code or OpenAI Codex. Using Agency, we implement proof-of-concept optimization techniques based on our analysis and achieve cost reductions up to 35% across various real-world benchmarks on existing harnesses without compromising accuracy.

candidates.title: Tutorial: Vision-Based Formation Control with Differential-Drive Robots
candidates.abstract: This tutorial presents a step-by-step introduction to multi-robot formation control using differential- drive robots, an overhead camera, and Python. ArUco markers are used to estimate robot positions and orientations, while desired pairwise displacement vectors define a circular formation. By comparing measured and desired relative positions, the controller computes movement vectors that are converted into differential-drive wheel commands, with basic proximity-sensor-based obstacle avoidance. The tutorial guides readers through hardware and software setup, robot pose estimation, formation geometry, feedback control, system integration, and formation-error evaluation. Motivated by the need to bridge the gap between theoretical understanding and practical implementation in robotics education, we emphasize how mathematical concepts are translated into coordinated behaviors on physical robots. Although the implementation uses a specific robotic platform, the underlying perception and formation-control principles can be adapted to other differential-drive robots and simulation environments. The accompanying open-source GitHub repository provides the Python implementation, setup instructions, and demonstrations to support hands-on learning and further exploration of multi-robot systems.

candidates.title: BUT telepresence: a fully open-source VR framework for low-latency stereoscopic video streaming with end-to-end latency instrumentation
candidates.abstract: Abstract Advances in immersive telepresence have enabled compelling virtual reality (VR)-based teleoperation, yet existing systems remain difficult to reproduce, inflexible in their streaming configuration, and largely devoid of end-to-end latency instrumentation. Current research prototypes typically rely on fixed encoding parameters, do not expose a unified interface for real-time reconfiguration, and rarely support hardware-accelerated decoding on standalone VR headsets. As a result, the community lacks an open, validated reference framework for low-latency stereoscopic teleoperation. This paper introduces a fully open-source VR telepresence system that integrates stereoscopic capture on a two-degrees-of-freedom (2-DOF) camera module, low-latency encoding using GStreamer, head-coupled camera actuation, and a native OpenXR application capable of hardware-accelerated decoding on modern standalone VR headsets. A key contribution is a built-in end-to-end latency instrumentation mechanism that timestamps each stage of the pipeline and embeds these measurements into the media stream, enabling continuous monitoring by the VR client. This information enables the user to dynamically adjust codec, resolution, and frame rate to maintain stable operator perception under heterogeneous network conditions, including wireless links. The framework is validated in representative robotics scenarios, demonstrating reliable stereoscopic teleoperation with a measured instrumented end‑to‑end latency of approximately 79 ms on a quiet 6 GHz link and 101 ms with the operator’s link saturated by competing traffic, with the VR headset’s pose prediction helping, in informal use, to mitigate perceived delay for the operator. Because every pipeline stage is timed individually and the reported total is their sum, the instrumentation also localizes degradation to individual components: contention is shown to act almost entirely on receiver-side decoding and not on transport, and reducing frame rate under loss is shown to be counterproductive, neither of which is visible from aggregate latency alone. A pilot evaluation with operators closes the loop from instrumentation to end user: the framework imposes a latency condition, verifies per participant from its own telemetry what was delivered, and records the operator’s presence, workload and task performance on the same sessions. All software, including benchmark datasets and Grafana dashboard configuration, is released publicly at https://github.com/Robotics-BUT/BUT_Telepresence to support reproducibility and future research.

candidates.title: Seventy years of parasocial research: a bibliometric analysis and science mapping, 1956–2025
candidates.abstract: Abstract Research using the term ‘parasocial’ has appeared since 1956 in media studies and psychology and, more recently, in influencer marketing. This study maps the development, intellectual structure and recent thematic direction of the 2174 journal works published from 1956 to 2025 that use the term ‘parasocial’ in its media sense. Using records from OpenAlex, it combines performance analysis with co-citation, bibliographic coupling, keyword mapping and topic analysis and tests the robustness of the main mapping results across alternative corpora, periods and network settings. Output increased from one article in 1956 to 521 works in 2025, and, by authors’ affiliations, the USA, Indonesia and China had the most works. Horton and Wohl’s 1956 article is cited by 63.1% of the works with a reference list. Under the main network settings, the most frequently cited references form two co-citation communities, which we interpret as a media-psychology foundation and an influencer-marketing stream; they differ in topic and in the age of their references, and the share of co-citation link weight between them increased across the three periods from 2014–2019 to 2023–2025. The keyword ‘Influencer marketing’ appears in 28.7% of the works published in 2023–2025; in that period the topic ‘Digital Marketing and Social Media’ exceeded ‘Media Influence and Health’, whereas across 2020–2025 the two were nearly equal (397 and 405 works). OpenAlex topic labels identify AI-related topics in 3.0% of the works from 2023–2025. A separate language-model-assisted classification of titles and stored abstracts classified 71 of these works (6.3%) as studying a parasocial bond with an artificial partner; the author examined every such case individually. Together, the widely shared cited reference, the rising co-citation between the two communities and the application of the concept to influencers and artificial agents offer a frame for comparing which conditions of a parasocial bond studies keep and which they change; how studies define or measure the phenomenon, and whether the concept applies to artificial agents, are questions that future content analyses and experiments could examine.

candidates.title: Adaptive patriliny: care and lineage continuity in Liangtouhun families in contemporary China
candidates.abstract: Drawing on field research and interviews with six families in a peri-urban setting in Jiangsu Province, this study examines how Liangtouhun arrangements connect caregiving, family recognition, and lineage continuity. Liangtouhun is understood as a marriage arrangement involving ongoing coordination with both spouses’ natal families, rather than a uniform pattern of alternating co-residence. The analysis identifies four related patterns: participants explained the arrangement through childcare needs and obligations to aging parents; caregiving contributions were invoked to justify claims for recognition; participants attached differing degrees of flexibility and significance to residential, surname, and ritual practices; and competing expectations were expressed through fairness, reciprocity, and family responsibility. Existing surname allocations are distinguished from unimplemented spousal agreements and prospective preferences. Care-for-recognition describes how practical support was connected to claims for involvement and belonging, without assuming a fixed exchange. Adaptive patriliny captures how bilateral participation can coexist with, and reconfigure, continuing commitments to descent-based family continuity. These commitments were expressed by members of both spouses’ natal families. The study therefore complicates an interpretation of bilateral participation as necessarily displacing patrilineal practices, while recognizing that the evidence does not establish the preservation of male decision-making authority.

candidates.title: AI companions, human concerns: a pragmatic perspective
candidates.abstract: Abstract The rise of agentic AI and so-called AI companions introduces a shift in the modes of interactions between humans and machines. The exact contours of this shift remain unclear, but early signs of social, affective, and even romantic engagements demonstrate areas of potential benefit and potent harms to individuals and to the broader social fabric. A full appreciation of these benefits and harms demands a multi-perspectival account not only of technological innovation and emerging modalities of human-machine interaction, but also of the historical, socio-cultural, psychological, and ethical aspects of companionship. This essay provides such as account through a pragmatist perspective that considers the material, institutional, and psycho-social conditions behind the rise of AI. From this perspective, the essay broadens the notion of “alignment” as one between means and ends rather than the commonly accepted formulation between design goals and outputs. We argue that AI companionship blurs the boundaries between tools and social actors—a dynamic that emerges from the interplay of technical architectures, intentional design practices, user psychology, and political-economic forces. Given that interplay, a set of interrelated questions arise, which we address in three clusters (supply, demand, mediation), highlighting the emerging social and ethical dilemmas, and suggesting pragmatic interventions to inform public discourse and policymaking. In so doing, we hope to curtail the tremendous fallouts that have become evident in other domains such as social media only in retrospect, and ​to contribute to the creation of an environment conducive to social cohesion and individual wellbeing.

candidates.title: Virtual Smartphone Fan Fiction in the Age of AI: Technology Empowerment and Fan Culture Reproduction
candidates.abstract: This study examines virtual smartphone fan fiction, in which fans use large language models (LLMs) and front-end tools to create interactive smartphone interfaces. Through passwords, simulated apps, prewritten content, and AI-generated replies, readers explore a character’s digital space and participate in an unfolding narrative. Using the perspectives of technology empowerment and fan-culture reproduction, this study analyzes the shift from screenshot-based stories to operable interfaces, the redistribution of authorship, the production of virtual intimacy, and the limits imposed by AI models, community norms, and platform governance. It argues that interfaces and AI responses now help shape narrative rhythm and reader agency, while creators increasingly act as system designers. However, greater technical access does not guarantee cultural recognition. The reproduction of fan culture is therefore shaped by the interaction of creators, readers, interfaces, models, and communities.

candidates.title: Taxonomy-Agnostic Neurosymbolic Grounding of Robot Kinematics
candidates.abstract: While symbolic reasoning for task allocation requires grounding a robot’s physical capabilities, standard Unified Robot Description Format (URDF) files provide only low-level kinematics without the formal semantic context needed for reasoning. We present URDF2Ontology, an automated, taxonomy-agnostic neurosymbolic framework that transforms raw URDF files into populated, grounded OWL ontologies. It leverages a Large Language Model (LLM) for targeted semantic reasoning, coupled with an iterative sequential graph-purging mechanism to prevent context window saturation. To process complex kinematic structures, it employs a morphology-aware dual-track architecture featuring a bottom-up Tree Track for branching assemblies and a top-down Chain Track for serial limbs. Guided by neurosymbolic guardrails, the framework extracts functional sub-graphs and asserts populated ontologies aligned with arbitrary user-provided taxonomies. Empirical evaluation across a diverse fleet of heterogeneous robots demonstrates strong schema alignment, valid structural extraction, and a significant reduction in manual domain authoring overhead.

candidates.title: Advancements in Embedded Surveillance Robotics for Defense and Security Applications
candidates.abstract: In military applications, surveillance plays a critical role in ensuring security, particularly in isolated and border areas. This chapter presents a recent approach to surveillance using a robot for military applications. The planned methodology is to substitute soldiers in border areas with robots, to enhance the security and both autonomous and manual control via internet connectivity. Equipped with multiple sensors and various electronic devices, the robot is designed to detect enemy presence, capture camera footage, and live-stream data to authorized personnel. This robot enables armed forces to proficiently monitor isolated areas and respond immediately to potential threats. Human risk is reduced by using this type of robot surveillance system. Deploying robots in high-risk isolated areas minimizes personnel exposure to potential threats while maintaining effective surveillance. The use of autonomous technology increases operational efficiency by enabling continuous surveillance without requiring constant human intervention. By combining cutting-edge embedded technology, real-time monitoring, and remote operability, this robot vehicle delivers a consistent and effective solution for border or boundary security. Integrating advanced technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI), embedded systems, and very large-scale integration (VLSI), will significantly enhance the capabilities and efficiency of the robot in armed forces. This robot provides not only a human-free system but also an efficient smart system to address military challenges.

candidates.title: Innovator 5.0: Integrating Design Thinking and Responsible Innovation into AI and Robotics Research Environments for Industry 5.0 and Society 5.0
candidates.abstract: Industry 5.0 and Society 5.0 call for a shift in AI and robotics development from a primary focus on automation and technical sophistication to holistic solutions that address human needs, social contexts, stakeholder perspectives, and broader societal impacts. Preparing future engineers for this shift requires educational approaches that connect technical development with design thinking and responsible innovation. To address this need, this study introduces Innovator 5.0, an educational framework that extends the Science–Engineering–Design (SED) model by incorporating responsibility (R + SED) within a design-thinking process. The proposed framework was implemented through seven embedded workshops during a five- to six-month international research internship involving nine undergraduate students across six AI and robotics projects. An exploratory post-programme evaluation examined participants’ design-oriented practices, perceived capability development, and experiences within the research environment. Participants reported high ratings across several evaluated dimensions, particularly for challenging problem statements before solution development (M = 6.78/7), systems thinking (M = 6.67/7), creative innovation (M = 6.56/7), contextual awareness (M = 6.33/7), and iterative revision (M = 6.11/7). They also highlighted project autonomy and facilitative mentoring as valued features, while limited direct stakeholder access was identified as an important implementation constraint. Together, these findings provide practical guidance for preparing engineers to consider the purpose, societal implications, and value of AI and robotics innovations alongside their technical feasibility, supporting people-centric and responsible engineering innovation.

candidates.title: The World Model Planning Accelerator (WMPA): Hardware-Algorithm Co-Design for Embedded AI in Robotics
candidates.abstract: Embedded AI is moving from perception to prediction. Robots now use world models$\unicode{x2014}$learned simulators that predict the outcome of candidate actions in a compressed latent space before any is executed. Every predicted step must be computed on board within a tight power and thermal budget, yet the energy these steps fundamentally require, and how far real hardware sits from it, have not been characterized. We derive lower bounds on the arithmetic operations and the CMOS dynamic energy of a latent state transition from information theory and Boolean circuit complexity. Profiling a DreamerV3-style Recurrent State Space Model (RSSM) shows that every rollout operation is memory-bandwidth bound and that a GPU consumes at least $5.9\times10^{10}$ times the CMOS energy floor. Transient 3D thermal simulations show that this inefficiency is also a thermal one, since sustained back-to-back planning heats a millimeter-scale silicon tile to 556 K even behind an ideal copper heat spreader. Guided by this chain from bound to bottleneck, we propose the World Model Planning Accelerator (WMPA), a chip architecture for embedded world model planning that combines near-memory computation, real-time entropy estimation, variable-precision rollout units, and copy-on-write latent scratchpads. With a design target of 40x lower power, the same tile stays near ambient at 306 K in simulation, pointing toward practical planning on thermally constrained robots.

Adventures in Reproducing and Integrating Open-Source: Developing Guidelines for Modular Software Components in Robot Grasping and Manipulation Pipelines for Picking in Clutter
candidates.abstract: When developing a novel software component of a robot system, researchers typically integrate open-source code for other components in the pipeline, such as perception, grasp planning, and motion planning. However, there are several bottlenecks related to the accessibility and reproducibility of open-source which are stifling research, development, evaluation, and deployment of robots. To this end, we are working to develop community-driven guidelines for modular components in robot software pipelines in the context of picking in clutter. In this work, we investigate reproducing and integrating multiple perception and grasp planning components used in vision-based perception-to-action pipelines. The architecture and methodology used to conduct these exercises are reviewed, highlighting issues encountered along the way. Recommendations for guidelines to improve accessibility, reproducibility, and integration of modular open-source components are shared related to the assets included in an open-source release, methods to modularize components, and practices for development and testing.
