candidates.title: Regulatory governance and full-scale digital transformation for prediction-based food safety management: Global trends and future perspectives
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Background The global food safety paradigm is shifting from traditional, reactive hazard control toward proactive, predictive risk management to address increasingly complex supply chain vulnerabilities. However, current digital implementations remain fragmented, creating structural bottlenecks that hinder the transition to next-generation regulatory science. Scope and approach To our knowledge, this study provides one of the first comparative critical analyses of the HACCP-based data governance frameworks of six major jurisdictions. We compare jurisdictions in which private actors play a relatively larger role in certification and implementation ('market-led': the United States, the European Union, Canada, and Japan) with those in which public institutions play a dominant role ('state-led': South Korea and China), positioned along a governance continuum in which all systems combine public and private functions, focusing on their capacity for real-time risk prediction, public-private data integration, and global interoperability. Key findings and conclusions The market-led systems examined tend to foster food safety culture but are affected by 'Data Silos' that limit actions to retrospective tracebacks. The state-led systems examined may enhance data integrity but can create a 'Data Island' paradox due to an over-reliance on automating isolated physico-chemical Critical Control Points. To overcome these limitations, we propose a conceptual framework for Full-Scale Digital Transformation (Full DX). Converging prerequisite programs, structured food safety culture assessment (e.g., Shapley-FAHP), and intentional threat mitigations (TACCP/VACCP) into an interoperable predictive network powered by ensemble machine learning could support a more resilient regulatory ecosystem for mitigating multidimensional global supply chain threats; this framework requires empirical validation.

candidates.title: Designing a Small Language Model Lexicon in Natural Language for Robotic Applications
candidates.abstract: In this paper, the aim is to present a project report of a method, based on which a small natural language lexicon is designed, or otherwise a small language model, for robotic applications. In this direction, a reference is made to Controlled Natural Languages, and their characteristics are determined for application in operational robotic vehicles. In addition, criteria are established for the selection of the nationality of the language, which constitutes the basis of the lexicon. A small introspection is made in the natural language unit of a human–robot interface, and a method is presented that examines the adequacy of the selected language in relation to the purpose of use of the system and the control criteria. The use of the lexicon’s method is presented, and an example of the analysis and inclusion of selected Greek language words is given. The reproduction of words from the lexicon’s stored data is also explained, as the reverse process that functions as a confirmation of the method. Received: 22 August 2025 | Revised: 20 April 2026 | Accepted: 12 October 2026 Conflicts of Interest The authors declare that they have no conflicts of interest to this work. Data Availability Statement Data sharing is not applicable to this article as no new data were created or analyzed in this study. Michail Papoutsidakis: Validation, Formal analysis. Nikolaos Laskaris: Writing – review & editing, Supervision.

candidates.title: Interactive Visual Gym: Evaluating Visual Interaction Models with Simulated Users in Interactive Worlds
candidates.abstract: Visual interaction models that support users during ongoing physical tasks require evaluation in closed loop, where assistant responses can change subsequent user behavior and task outcomes. Existing benchmarks largely rely on offline replay and therefore cannot capture these effects. We introduce Interactive Visual Gym, a framework for closed-loop evaluation and training of visual interaction models through joint simulation of executable task environments and human users. We contribute three simulators that recreate everyday tasks and human-aligned action spaces across cooking, household manipulation, and mobile-interface domains, together with a persona-conditioned user simulation harness that collaborates with the assistant while incorporating controlled execution errors and other out-of-plan behaviors. We instantiate the framework as IVG-Bench, a benchmark with 315 interaction scenarios. Evaluating state-of-the-art VLMs as visual interaction models reveals substantial limitations: the best-performing model, Claude Opus 5.5, completes only 53.5% of tasks within the time limit, exhibits significant weaknesses in factual grounding and actionable guidance, and is often too slow to prevent errors when response latency is considered. We verify our evaluation protocol with a human study which finds 78.5% agreement between our interaction-quality metric and participant preferences. We further show that the environments provide useful learning signals: in a proof-of-concept GRPO experiment, closed-loop training improves both task success and interaction quality for Qwen3.5-4B model in our cooking environment.

candidates.title: Social Humanoid: Socially Responsive Human-Humanoid Interaction
candidates.abstract: Humanoid robots are typically trained as solitary agents, leaving them unable to coordinate physically with human partners who naturally anticipate and adjust to one another. To bridge this gap, we present Social Humanoid, a hierarchical system that generates and executes socially responsive whole-body motion on a 29-DoF Unitree G1 conditioned on a human partner's motion. Its high-level policy performs flexible sequence modeling of human and humanoid motion through a shared tokenized representation, generating reactive humanoid motion and anticipating the partner's motion when they are occluded, while a low-level whole-body tracking controller executes the generated motion on the robot. To train the system, we introduce a two-phase adaptive retargeting procedure that retargets one interaction partner to the robot while morphing the other partner to preserve contact dynamics, reachability, and relative body scale. We apply this procedure across five motion-capture datasets to produce a new Human-Humanoid Interaction (HHI) benchmark of 260 hours of human-humanoid interactions. Our results demonstrate that Social Humanoid produces coordinated, human-aligned behavior across diverse interaction types in simulation and the real world. Project page: https://von31.github.io/social-humanoid/

candidates.title: Insect-inspired hexapod robot with magnetically coupled compliant and modular drive system
candidates.abstract: Legged robots are increasingly inspired by insects’ ability to combine rigidity and compliance for agile, damage-tolerant locomotion in cluttered terrain. Herein, we introduce INSECTRON, a centimeter-scale hexapod robot that employs magnetic transmission to achieve robust mobility with minimal mechanical complexity. Each leg connects to the drivetrain via neodymium magnets, forming a self-aligning micro-clutch that transmits torque under normal load and safely slips under overload, while additional magnetic couplings between drive modules accommodate load imbalances and perturbations. Hall effect sensors provide proprioception for a phase-domain controller maintaining persistent anti-phase coordination. The magnetic transmission architecture introduces intrinsic mechanical adaptability, functionally analogous to biological preflex mechanisms, enabling rapid responses to external perturbations without additional control complexity. Experiments demonstrated stable locomotion across multiple slopes and substrates. Maneuverability was achieved through differential turning and spin-in-place. A minimum Cost of Transport (CoT) of 30 was achieved during locomotion experiments. Under vertical perturbations, INSECTRON autonomously recovered in over 90% of trials, highlighting strong passive impact tolerance. The architecture eliminates the need for precision alignment and mechanical fasteners, enabling tool-free leg replacement and rapid mechanical reconfiguration. This work establishes a scalable route toward modular, resilient, and field-deployable miniature legged robots for confined and uncertain environments.

candidates.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
candidates.abstract: Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion. However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. We introduce VFlash, a method for fast, accurate visual planning through Flash Primitive Decoding. VFlash exploits the known structure of visual primitives to predict their coordinates jointly, using a lightweight drafter that generates an entire primitive in one forward pass. The layout adapts to the primitive's type, dimensionality, and length, supporting compact boxes and long, variable-length trajectories. Crucially, spatial accuracy need not require reproducing an autoregressive model's exact token sequence. VFlash therefore trains on annotated primitives and directly accepts structurally valid predictions without target-token agreement. Across the evaluated 2D and 3D robot trajectory tasks, VFlash consistently reduces prediction errors relative to autoregressive decoding. Preliminary single-rollout measurements indicate approximately 25x faster generation for 3D point motion forecasting. A world action model conditioned on VFlash plans achieves 70.2% average success across four MolmoSpaces task suites, compared with 62.6% for the baseline.

candidates.title: Vision-Based Human–Computer Interaction System for Mexican Sign Language Recognition and Robotic Reproduction: Toward Inclusive Educational Applications
candidates.abstract: Mexican Sign Language (MSL) plays an essential role in communication within the Deaf community, yet access to sign-language learning resources remains limited in some educational settings. This study presents a vision-based Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) system for MSL recognition and robotic reproduction, developed as a proof of concept toward inclusive educational applications. The system uses an RGB camera and MediaPipe Hands for hand-landmark extraction, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) for recognition of 29 static classes, and a TimeDistributed-Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model for 10 dynamic classes. Recognized signs are mapped to predefined motion sequences executed by an ATmega2560-controlled robotic arm. Under stratified random and sequential partitioning protocols, the static model achieved accuracies of 100.00% and 99.88%, respectively, while the dynamic model achieved 100.00% under both protocols. Additional comparisons with Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Random Forest classifiers, using three random seeds, demonstrated competitive performance and low variability within the original single-participant dataset. To assess generalization beyond the training participant, a preliminary signer-independent evaluation was conducted with three previously unseen participants, without model retraining or adaptation. Across 585 recognition attempts involving 39 classes, the system achieved an overall accuracy of 89.06%, providing initial evidence of recognition performance across different signers. Furthermore, 92 accepted recognition trials successfully triggered their corresponding robotic sequences, demonstrating functional integration between recognition and actuation. These findings support the technical feasibility of the proposed contactless HCI architecture as a potential foundation for interactive MSL learning tools. Nevertheless, broader signer-independent validation and user-centered evaluations are required to establish its accessibility, usability, and educational effectiveness.

candidates.title: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling
candidates.abstract: World-action models adapt pretrained video generators, and vision-language-action models build on pretrained vision-language backbones; both tie policy architecture and inference cost to large transformers designed for generation rather than control. It remains unclear how much these generation-oriented choices affect control. In this work, we introduce Latent Action JEPA (La-JEPA), a compact world-action model whose policy transformer is trained from scratch in the feature space of a pretrained V-JEPA 2.1 encoder. Following Fast-WAM, La-JEPA learns to predict future features jointly with actions during training and generates only actions at inference. Among policies without embodied pretraining, La-JEPA achieves state-of-the-art performance in clean and randomized RoboTwin 2.0 scenes and on LIBERO-Plus with correct instructions, while using far fewer parameters than the strongest competing policies. It runs substantially faster than Fast-WAM at comparable performance and outperforms the closest JEPA-based methods, LeapBot-WA and JEPA-WAM, on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0 without their pretrained policy backbones. On four real-robot tasks, its average success is comparable to pi0.5 and above non-embodied-pretrained baselines. Through a design study of the choices behind La-JEPA, we show that JEPA features outperform video VAE latents, most clearly out of distribution, and that training-time future prediction choices significantly impact the policy even when future prediction is skipped at inference. We correct the LIBERO-Plus instructions, as the officially released evaluator corrupts them for most variants, and re-evaluate several strong open baselines. Without a generative pretrained policy backbone, La-JEPA is better and faster than far larger policies, suggesting that robot foundation models may benefit from architectures designed for control rather than inherited from generation.

candidates.title: A Search for Exoplanets around Northern Circumpolar Stars. XI. A Planetary Companion around HD 112987 and a Planetary Companion Candidate around HD 58545
candidates.abstract: Abstract We present precise radial velocity (RV) measurements of the northern circumpolar giant stars HD 58545 and HD 112987 obtained over 8 yr with the Bohyunsan Observatory Echelle Spectrograph and supplemented during the final 3 yr by the Network of Robotic Echelle Spectrographs. RV variations in giant stars may arise from orbiting companions or intrinsic phenomena, including pulsations, chromospheric activity, and rotational modulation. To distinguish these possibilities, we analyzed line-profile variations, line bisectors, chromospheric activity indicators, and photometric data, and modeled the RV time series with Keplerian orbits using Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling. For HD 58545, the best-fitting Keplerian model yields an orbital period of 450.44 − 4.63 + 3.35 days and a minimum companion mass of 3.65 − 0.58 + 0.61 M J . For HD 112987, we derive an orbital period of 554.96 − 4.67 + 4.14 days and a minimum companion mass of 8.48 − 0.73 + 0.96 M J . None of the activity diagnostics for HD 112987 exhibits significant variability at the RV period, consistent with a Keplerian interpretation. In contrast, several activity diagnostics of HD 58545 exhibit periodicities comparable to the RV period, which is also consistent within the uncertainties with the projected rotational timescale, P rot / sin i = 462 ± 33 days . Thus, rotationally modulated stellar variability may contribute to the RV signal. Although the signal can be described by a Keplerian model, the current data cannot distinguish unambiguously between a planetary companion and intrinsic stellar variability. We therefore conclude that HD 112987 hosts a planetary companion, whereas further monitoring is required to determine the origin of the RV signal in HD 58545.

candidates.title: Into the Infinite Possibilities: Omar Yaghi’s Vision for Science in the Era of AI
candidates.abstract: 2025 Nobel Laurent Omar Yaghi is establishing a new center in Tsinghua University, aiming to transform chemistry and materials science through AI and robotics.

candidates.title: Intimacy Robots and Inward Decline: From Individual Symbolism to Civilisational Consequence
candidates.abstract: Abstract Philosophical work on intimacy robots has kept to two registers: the welfare of the individual user, and the symbolic wrong done to the classes of person such artefacts represent. Danaher’s symbolic-consequences argument, the fullest statement of the critical case, concedes that the downstream effects of that symbolism are hard to establish, and recommends an experimental posture. This paper takes the concession as its problem. The debate has no macro-social level of analysis, and without one it cannot say which consequences to look for. Drawing on the sociology of solidarity, Vallor’s account of moral deskilling, and the older literature of civilisational decline, it sets out three mechanisms by which individually rational uses of intimacy technology could aggregate into collectively costly outcomes: demographic subtraction, relational deskilling, and the habituation of desire to objects that cannot reciprocate. Each is put as a conditional with its defeaters named, not as a prediction. Tested against current evidence, including a nationally representative survey of adolescent companion-AI use and experimental work finding that AI companions do reduce loneliness, the third mechanism proves best supported analytically and the first least supported empirically. The result is a framework for aggregation, not a forecast of collapse; the paper closes by saying what would disconfirm it.

candidates.title: Interrogating Large Language Model Discourse on Pornography: Implications for Sexuality Education
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models have had a massive impact on learning, knowledge production, and educational processes. Concerns regarding the reliability of the knowledge LLMs produce, the impact of their use on critical thinking, and how to promote AI literacy, have been raised by many critical researchers, especially in relation to sensitive topics. This paper explores implications of the use of LLMs for comprehensive sexuality education and pornography literacy. Discourses generated by popular LLMs when asked about pornography are analyzed through a feminist lens. The LLMs produced power-blind statements about pornography, creating silences around the gendered practices. Moreover, the LLMs produce reduced discourses around pornography, violence against women, and consent. When asked to generate lesson plans, simplistic plans were created that lack systemic analysis of pornography and limit critical thinking to individual awareness. The paper argues that if LLMs are applied in CSE, the discourses they generate must be carefully considered through feminist and critical pedagogical perspectives that address power relations, oppression, and violence within the wider social context. Furthermore, the results suggest that the proliferation of easily accessible AI-generated knowledge makes comprehensive sexuality education curricula about pornography and teachers’ training even more essential.

candidates.title: ApproxHDC: Approximation Tuning for Hyperdimensional Computing
candidates.abstract: As Moore's law reaches its physical and economic limits, domain-specific approaches are increasingly employed to accelerate machine learning workloads. Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) represents one such emerging paradigm, offering an alternative to conventional deep learning techniques. Rooted in cognitive models of computation, HDC is designed bottom-up with hardware efficiency as a first-class objective. Consequently, HDC workloads map naturally to heterogeneous hardware platforms, including CPUs, GPUs, and FPGAs, as well as emerging in-memory computing technologies such as Resistive RAM (ReRAM) and Phase-Change Memory (PCM). The intrinsic tolerance of HDC algorithms to noise and approximation enables substantial performance gains with minimal loss in inference quality. In this work, we introduce ApproxHDC, a framework for automated identification and application of domain-specific approximations in HDC workloads. ApproxHDC extends the HPVM-HDC compiler infrastructure to enable retargetable compilation across diverse hardware backends, including CPUs, GPUs, and simulated ReRAM and PCM-based accelerators. The space of possible software and hardware approximations in HDC is exponentially large, making exhaustive exploration intractable; ApproxHDC employs efficient search and analysis techniques to navigate this space and identify high-impact approximations. We further integrate hardware-level approximation mechanisms within the HDC accelerator to demonstrate ApproxHDC's ability to exploit both software and hardware approximations. Experimental evaluation shows that ApproxHDC achieves up to 17.25x speedup on CPUs, 14.97x on GPUs, and 4.69x on SpecPCM while staying within user-specified quality-of-service constraints, outperforming the state-of-the-art MicroHD framework by 3.49x. HDC-specific search space pruning reduces the design space by 71 to 491 orders of magnitude automatically and up to 89 more with developer guidance, enabling discovery of high-quality configurations within minutes.

candidates.title: Software-Defined Context-Aware Virtual Fixture for Teleoperation via Vision-Language Model
candidates.abstract: Abstract Precise teleoperation in unstructured environments remains challenging, because human errors and system-inherent limitations such as control jittering can significantly degrade task success and operational efficiency. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a software-defined Context-Aware Virtual Fixture (CAVF) system that leverages the open-world understanding of a Vision-Language Model (VLM). The proposed system automatically generates motion guidance for the robot end-effector (EEF) to assist teleoperation, preserving critical task-relevant motion while suppressing unnecessary translation and rotation components. This framework enables the autonomous generation of context-aware, haptic-free assistance without relying on handcrafted rules or physical force-feedback devices. Quantitative experiments in both simulation and real-world environments demonstrate that the proposed system significantly improves success rates, reduces completion times, and enhances trajectory efficiency compared to conventional teleoperation.

candidates.title: A human-centric large language model interface for monitoring and control of autonomous mobile robots via digital twins in industry 5.0
candidates.abstract: The diversity of industrial robot manufacturers, proprietary programming languages, and graphical interfaces complicates robotic system deployment and operation. This heterogeneity highlights the need for intuitive, accessible, and human-centric interaction methods. This paper presents a framework for natural language-based monitoring and selected control of autonomous mobile robots using a Large Language Model (LLM) interface, structured API communication, and digital twin visualization. The approach enables operators to interact with robots through natural language without requiring detailed knowledge of robot-specific interfaces or technical commands. The framework is evaluated from the operator’s perspective, focusing on its ability to simplify access to robot information, reduce interaction complexity, and support selected control tasks. Digital twin integration provides additional visual feedback on robot status and its operating environment. The proposed framework contributes to the development of more transparent, accessible, and human-oriented robotic systems aligned with Industry 5.0 principles.

candidates.title: V1: An Open-Source Shallow-Water Stereo Research ROV — Hardware Design Files and Software
candidates.abstract: V1 is an open-source remotely operated underwater robot developed initially for supervised shallow-water stereo data collection and intended for reuse in related shallow-water visual research. It combines commercial propulsion, flight-control and computing components with a single acrylic watertight enclosure, six thrusters and a common multilayer internal payload rack that can be withdrawn from the rear for equipment access. A custom stereo mount behind a shared flat front viewport provides 80, 100 and 120 mm nominal mechanical camera separations for manual selection and fixation before a task. This deposit provides an engineering-only distribution based on public source release v0.1.1 (4 November 2026). It includes 11 editable SolidWorks 2018 custom parts; DXF, STEP and STL exports; five editable R1 manufacturing-review drawings, associated custom models and PDFs; functional wiring diagrams; the bill of materials and cost basis; assembly, deployment and operating instructions; onboard acquisition/communication software; and selected offline calibration and processing tools. Temperature validation data, statistics, audit logs and thermal analysis scripts are excluded at the author's request. The original GitHub release and ZIP remain unchanged. PACKAGING_NOTE.md records the selected scope; manifest.json and SHA256SUMS are regenerated for this distribution. FILE_INDEX.md lists the actual 122 files, purposes and licences. Mixed licences apply by file: CERN-OHL-P-2.0 for hardware and functional wiring; MIT for supplied engineering software; and CC BY 4.0 for project-authored documentation, BOM and metadata. Original licence texts, directory notices and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md remain authoritative. Commercial reference CAD, private complete assemblies and separately licensed upstream drivers, kernels, SDKs and SLAM algorithms are excluded. York-Tank is a separate research output associated with https://doi.org/10.3390/s26206567. Its complete raw dataset is not included in this hardware archive. The supplied R1 drawings retain manufacturing-review/nominal status. Dependencies, calibration inputs and processing scope are documented in the package.

candidates.title: Open-HumanWAM: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
candidates.abstract: Egocentric human video offers a scalable source of manipulation priors for robot learning, yet translating raw data scale into generalizable robot policies demands rigorous data curation and training recipes. We introduce Open-HumanWAM, the first fully open recipe for scaling egocentric pretraining to 50,000 hours, anchored by Open-HumanWAM-50K---a curated egocentric video corpus densely annotated with hand motion and natural language. Leveraging this corpus, we systematically investigate pure human pretraining via closed-loop simulation evaluations and uncover an empirical log-linear scaling law linking pretraining data hours to downstream robot success rates. Grounded in these findings, we develop HumanWAM-Vanilla, a world--action model pretrained exclusively on 50k hours of egocentric human video. Upon robot post-training, HumanWAM-Vanilla reaches 92.08% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean and 68.88% on Clean2Random, alongside a 14.17% mean success rate and a 19.00 mean progress score on RoboDojo. To push the capability frontier further, we explore joint human--robot pretraining with HumanWAM-Goal, a visual-goal-conditioned world--action model. Hybrid data scaling unlocks broad zero-shot generalization across both simulation and physical benchmarks, propelling post-trained RoboTwin 2.0 performance to new state-of-the-art levels: 92.70% on Clean2Clean and a substantial leap to 84.60% on Clean2Random. On physical robots, HumanWAM-Goal further exhibits emergent embodied in-context learning, dynamically adapting its manipulation behavior to unseen visual goals without parameter updates. To support reproducible scaling research in embodied AI, we open-source the Open-HumanWAM-50K corpus, data curation and pretraining pipelines, alongside the pretrained and post-trained HumanWAM checkpoints, inference code, and simulation evaluation suites.

candidates.title: Machine Learning-Enabled Rover For Autonomous Navigation In Rough Terrain
candidates.abstract: A hybrid perception-control framework for navigating rough terrains by remote YOLOv8n-based terrain classification combined with on-board safety-based control of rover is proposed. The system uses ESP32-WROOM-32 module for controlling motors, ultrasonic sensors for detecting obstacles, infrared sensors for detecting cliff edges, and watchdog communication, whereas ESP32-CAM is responsible for sending terrain images to a laptop where the inference algorithm works. Four-class terrain data consisting of 800 images of grass, sand, gravel, and soil is employed for fine-tuning YOLOv8n using stratified dataset. Terrain predictions control movements depending on traversability coefficients, while safety controls take precedence over remote controls when an obstacle or communication link is detected. The evaluation over 60 trials of outdoor navigation has resulted in terrain classification with an accuracy of 78.3% and successful navigation with an 80.0% success rate. The perception-to-action latency was 170±23 ms, fail-safe time was 1.02±0.04 s, and emergency braking was 310±45 ms. The power consumption of the rover was 4.22±0.35 W, and the estimated operational time was around 4.5 h. Such values characterize the performance of the limited resources rover that implements the separation of complex computation-based inference from motion control in embedded systems.

candidates.title: SenTrojan: Revealing Analog Hardware Trojan Attacks on Sensors
candidates.abstract: Sensors bridge the physical and digital worlds, making their integrity critical to cyber-physical system security. Existing sensor attacks largely exploit unintended and sensor-specific physical vulnerabilities, limiting their generalizability and motivating a different threat model, i.e., whether an adversary can implant hidden attack surfaces into sensors before deployment. In this paper, we present SenTrojan, an analog hardware Trojan framework for sensors. SenTrojan embeds malicious functionality into analog signal circuitry commonly shared across diverse sensor architectures, and activates the hidden behavior through crafted external physical signals. Once activated, SenTrojan can induce sensor malfunctions ranging from permanent denial-of-service to static or dynamic spoofing. To achieve these effects under different architectural constraints, we introduce two complementary designs. The Logic-Rule-Driven (LRD) Trojan adds lightweight analog monitoring logic to detect trigger features such as frequency and amplitude, enabling reliable activation across various sensor types. The Physical-Effect-Driven (PED) Trojan targets sensors with exploitable native analog effects, e.g., nonlinearity and rectification, and realizes attacks with minimal component insertion. We evaluate SenTrojan on 14 sensors spanning 6 transduction principles and demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse real-world scenarios. Overall, SenTrojan achieves an average successful trigger rate above 95%, maintains over 97% similarity to benign behavior, incurs zero false-trigger rate for LRD designs, and introduces less than 5% average deviation in drift, noise floor, and response time. To our knowledge, this work is the first systematic study of analog sensor Trojans, broadening sensor security from unintended physical vulnerabilities to intentional supply-chain compromise.

candidates.title: Haptic Shared Control for Multi-Robot Systems
candidates.abstract: Multi-agent systems offer significant advantages in terms of flexibility and redundancy, enabling the efficient distribution of complex tasks among multiple robots. However, their deployment requires advanced control strategies to ensure optimal cooperation between autonomous agents and human operators. We propose a modification of the global connectivity maintenance algorithm to incorporate measurements taken in agent's local frame, using sensors with limited fields of view. This algorithm, responsible for the autonomous behavior of the multi-robot system, is combined with different adaptive supervision strategies, allowing the user to exert control at varying scales over the entire group. (i) Single Agent Control (S): The operator directly controls a single robot, (ii) Pinning Control (P): The operator imposes constraints on multiple robots to influence the group, (iii) Centroid Control (C): The operator acts on the system's center of mass to steer the entire fleet. In conjunction with the connectivity maintenance algorithm, these methods ensure compliance with inter-agent constraints while providing haptic feedback to the user regarding the system's connectivity state. The effectiveness of these approaches was evaluated through a user study, comparing performance with and without haptic feedback across multiple scenarios tailored to the different control modes.

candidates.title: Prosthetic Heart Valve Orifice Area Detection By Using A Combined Shock-Anisotropic Coherence Filter To Improve Level Sets Algorithm
candidates.abstract: Abstract Prosthetic valve is a synthetic or tissue substitute for the natural valve. It is designed to mimic the natural valve’s normal opening and clos-ing motions. The need for replacing heart valves increased drastically as the heart valve diseases became one of the dangerous death cause in the world. “Global demand for prosthetic heart valve market expected to reach USD 5,302.1 million in 2021 and growing of 9% from 2016 to 2021”. Unfortunately, Biological valves tend to fail over time, requir-ing replacement in 30% of patients within 10 years and 50% within 15 years. The demands for testing prosthetic valves are crucial to main-tain a robustness, durability and compatibility to improve patient health care which insure a place in the global market. This article discuss a novel method for automatic detection of a leaflet edges around ori-fice area opening for PHV (Prosthetic Heart Valve). A pre-processing algorithm using a combination of Anisotropic and Shock filter is proposed to enhance image quality before using a level set to detect PHV edges. This technique shows great capabilities to detect leaflet edges and provide additional enhancement compared to the other works.

candidates.title: Large Language Models for Industrial Robots: Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions
candidates.abstract: With the accelerating intelligent transformation of global manufacturing, industrial robots have become critical equipment in modern smart factories. However, the growing prevalence of multi-variety, small-batch production has made the high programming threshold, tedious reconfiguration, and limited environmental adaptability of traditional industrial robots increasingly prominent. Over the past few years, large language models (LLMs) have proven to have strong semantic comprehension, knowledge reasoning, and task planning abilities, a new avenue in the intelligent upgrading of industrial robots. The systematic review of the literature on the topic of the industrial robot driven by LLM is presented in this paper, including the mainstream technical directions, and the representative studies in five areas of application: industrial inspection, assembly and collaboration, maintenance and fault recovery, manufacturing operation planning, and robot navigation. Based on this, the paper examines the key challenges to be addressed at present, including model output reliability and safety, the simulation-to-reality gap and real-time constraints, and data scarcity and distribution shift. It also discusses future research opportunities, including knowledge enrichment and reliable reasoning, lightweight deployment and edge computing, and life-long learning and domain adaptation. The purpose of this paper is to serve as a reference in future studies and implementation of LLMs in industrial robots.

candidates.title: Asynchronous Robot Policies
candidates.abstract: Scaling vision-language foundation models has significantly advanced generalist robot manipulation, but the increased model scale introduces computational latency that degrades real-time physical reactivity. Existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) architectures execute high-level semantic reasoning and action ex- ecution sequentially within the primary control loop, creating a fundamental tension between semantic-reasoning capability and robot agility. To address this, we propose Asynchronous Robot Policy (ARP), an architectural framework that decouples semantic reasoning from low-level action generation using asynchronous processes operating at independent frequencies. In ARP, a high-capacity Vision-Language Model (VLM) asynchronously updates a semantic memory at low fre- quency, while a lightweight Vision-Action Expert, conditioned on this semantic memory, generates robot actions at a much higher control frequency. Such a formulation, enables having a fast perception-action loop without compromising on the semantic capability. To overcome asynchronous memory staleness, ARP trains the vision-action expert on the semantic staleness and execution delay, with temporally mismatched observation across processes. On Franka manipulation tasks, ARP achieves an 18% higher success rate and 20% less time need for execution in quasi-static setups, while 3-5 times baseline performance in dynamic simulation environments. Furthermore, ARP enables operating the VLM at 10 times lower than its nominal frequency with no significant performance loss making it much more efficient than the baseline. These results highlight the architectural advantages of modeling robot policies as asynchronous processes, enabling real-world reactive deployment without sacrificing the scale of foundation models.

candidates.title: Analysing responses to digital activism in Indonesia and Malaysia using AIDA framework
candidates.abstract: This article examines how six youth-led X accounts in Indonesia and Malaysia generated engagement and were associated with different forms of participation during the 2024 Indonesian presidential election and the 2022 Malaysian general election. Using the AIDA (Attention–Interest–Desire–Action) framework as a non-linear interpretive heuristic, it draws on platform metrics, interactional traces, and interviews with organisers. The study compares four candidate-centred volunteer accounts in Indonesia with two reform-oriented and civic education initiatives in Malaysia as an analytical contrast rather than a like-for-like national test. The findings show that spectacle and gamified formats scale Attention and affective Desire within platform attention economies, yet frequently remain associated with discursive, platform-proximate Action, revealing an action gap. In contrast, the Malaysian civic initiatives demonstrate stronger organisational and institutional linkages between online coordination, procedural participation and civic education. Situating AIDA within hybrid media ecologies and platform governance, the article argues that democratic effects depend less on visibility metrics than on organisational capacity and linkages to institutional processes. The study contributes to eParticipation research by distinguishing discursive-amplificatory, material-participatory, and institutional forms of Action and by specifying how platform logics condition their relationship to online engagement

candidates.title: Conclusion: Toward Planetary Praxis
candidates.abstract: The planet enters politics.That was our opening claim.Earth itself is already shaping conditions of life: setting constraints, creating obligations, and enabling possibilities for other futures.The constitutive forces of our "home" planet manifest through nonliving, living, and technological agencies.The question is no longer whether our planet is involved in politics, but what kinds of politics become pos si ble and desirable once we take that fact seriously.This conclusion unfolds in four steps.First, it revisits the preceding chapters to draw together the sketches of a politics with, rather than merely about, the Earth.Second, it outlines a research agenda to identify and develop the concepts, methods, and institutions needed to sustain such politics.Third, it turns to practice, arguing that planetary politics does not demand premature harmony but rather the recognition of ambivalence and the willingness to form unconventional alliances.Fi nally, it closes with a planetary leitmotif-not as a blueprint, but as an invitation for open and collective engagement. SynthesisEach chapter demonstrates that the concept of the planet and, by extension, our planetary condition serve as a lens that transforms how we understand the human condition and how we approach, analyze, and engage in politics.Collectively, the chapters open a space of possibility for a planetary politics grounded in two princi ples: first, an all-effecting princi ple, which asserts that any entity shaping a shared world should have a say in decisions that concern that world; and second, a habitability princi ple, which holds that planetary politics should work to keep the Earth livable or even 7 Conclusion: Toward Planetary Praxis

candidates.title: RESONATE: a Real Social Navigation Testbed for Autonomous Service Robots
candidates.abstract: Social navigation is essential for autonomous service robots operating in human environments, but progress remains constrained by the lack of extensive real-world benchmarks. This paper presents the Real Social Navigation Testbed (RESONATE), a reproducible benchmark for human-aware navigation based on a unified robotic platform, a shared ROS 2 software stack, precise trajectory ground truth, and structured social interaction scenarios. We evaluate eight controller configurations, combining classical and predictive local planners with different social modeling strategies, over eight representative scenarios with five repetitions each, yielding 320 physical experiments. The benchmark combines quantitative navigation and social metrics with participant-based qualitative assessments to jointly measure efficiency, safety, comfort, and perceived social behavior. Results reveal scenario-dependent trade-offs among the tested methods. The algorithms that stands out for their performance are the DWA with Gaussian social costmaps for its reliability, and the SFM-MPPI to provide the best balance between robustness, navigation efficiency, and social acceptance. Overall, RESONATE supports the robotics community with a real-world benchmark, reusable baselines, data, and testbed, and a consistent evaluation protocol for advancing socially aware navigation research.

candidates.title: Self-governed access control in open robot swarms using a blockchain-based DAO
candidates.abstract: Robot swarms harness simple, local interactions among many individually limited robots to produce complex, coordinated collective behavior, making them valuable across domains from agriculture to disaster response. We envision the next frontier for such swarms as open swarms, in which robots join or leave the swarm dynamically at runtime. The ability to dynamically adjust swarm size has been shown to be beneficial, for instance by reducing inconsistencies and network partitioning, especially under sparse connectivity or in complex environments, ultimately improving task performance. For practical deployment, however, open swarms requires governance, particularly protection against Byzantine behavior (i.e., faulty or malicious robots), since allowing robots to join freely also makes the swarm easier to infiltrate. Blockchain technology has recently been incorporated into robot swarms, offering secure, decentralized coordination and improved resilience, though largely in closed settings with a fixed, predetermined membership. In this work, we extend these benefits to open swarms by introducing robot swarms governed by a blockchain-based decentralized autonomous organization (DAO), in which the swarm regulates itself using autonomous rules encoded in smart contracts. We outline several DAO-based governance mechanisms for robot swarms, depending on the needs of the application, and present a proof-of-concept implementation of a simple DAO that regulates swarm membership and prevents Byzantine infiltration. Our simulation results and real-robot validations show that DAO-governed access control and robot removal can maintain proper swarm functioning while keeping the number of Byzantine robots within acceptable limits.

candidates.title: How Much Prosody Does Your ASR Encoder Already Know
candidates.abstract: End-of-turn (EoT) detection decides in real-time whether a speaker has finished. Traditional detectors rely on hand-built prosodic features (pitch, speaking rate, pauses), while modern detectors run on a neural ASR encoder that has processed the same audio. Because the encoder reads the signal those features are computed from, it may already hold much of the information they were meant to supply. We test this three ways, reading a streaming Zipformer encoder at four depths from raw input to the final layer. First, we measure how much prosody helps over the encoder alone. Second, we test whether prosody can be recovered from the encoder. Third, we ask whether any single feature still helps given the encoder. The three tests agree; prosody adds a large gain on raw audio, but that gain collapses once the signal passes through even the first encoder layer. The same pattern holds for two open-source encoders, wav2vec2 and Whisper, both of which are offline.

candidates.title: A meta-analysis of artificial intelligence and the customer brand relationship in tourism and hospitality
candidates.abstract: This meta-analysis pools 23 independent samples ( N = 9,875) on the association between customer-facing artificial intelligence (AI) and the customer-brand relationship in tourism and hospitality. Earlier reviews of this question are narrative or stop at technology acceptance; this one quantifies the relational link and extends it into the generative-AI period. Each effect size is a zero-order, construct-level correlation taken from the primary study’s correlation matrix, and no standardised path coefficients were pooled. A random-effects model (restricted maximum likelihood with the Knapp-Hartung adjustment) gives a pooled correlation of r = 0.62, 95% CI [0.54, 0.68], with a 95% prediction interval of [0.18, 0.85]. The analyses found no statistically reliable differences by technology (service robots, chatbots, generative AI, general AI tools; Q-between = 4.1, p = 0.25), by anthropomorphism (Q-between = 1.6, p = 0.21), by type of AI predictor (Q-between = 1.8, p = 0.42), by outcome family (Q-between = 6.4, p = 0.17), by sub-sector, or by region, although several subgroups hold only a few samples and the tests have limited power. Heterogeneity is considerable (I-squared = 96.4%) and is not accounted for by the coded moderators, the correlation source, or publication year. There is no sign of a small-study effect (Egger p = 0.99; trim-and-fill adjusted r = 0.59). The certainty of evidence is low (GRADE), and because every correlation comes from a single-source survey, the pooled estimate is best read as an upper bound. Interpreted within a stimulus-organism-response framework, the evidence shows a positive association that the coded artefact-level categories do not differentiate, but the large between-study variation and the cross-sectional, self-report designs mean the average should not be treated as a universal value.

candidates.title: A Study on the Effects of Finger Movements on a Humanoid Hugging Robot
candidates.abstract: This study aimed to examine the impact of finger movements in hugging robots on users by experimentally investigating how the presence and patterns of such movements affect users psychologically. The results suggest that the presence and patterns of finger movements influence the sensations users seek from the robot; specifically, repetitive movements and asynchronous movements across multiple fingers tended to enhance these sensations. Additionally, simultaneous movement of all fingers and gentle hugging tended to evoke a greater sense of care. Conversely, no differences were observed regarding resistance to physical contact initiated by the robot.

candidates.title: A Modular Open-Source Python Framework for Small Satellite Attitude Determination and Control
candidates.abstract: Advanced attitude determination and control (ADCS) techniques can be difficult for small satellite teams to adopt: tightly coupled implementations require substantial code changes to evaluate different actuators, sensors, orbits, mission goals, and control laws. Existing tools often emphasize orbit mechanics or flight software rather than closed-loop ADCS. This paper presents an open-source, modular ADCS framework in pure Python for rapid development, repeatable testing, and flight-oriented integration across heterogeneous spacecraft. The package supports torque- and command-level control, bound-respecting allocation, and full- and reduced-attitude objectives. Interchangeable estimation, control, planning, and actuator/sensor modules are reconfigured through configuration changes. Integrated simulation includes attitude and orbit propagation, sensor and actuator bias and noise, and environmental disturbances. An actuator-aware planner supports underactuated architectures, while hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) capability enables testing on mission-representative computers. Case studies include a 3U CubeSat with three magnetorquers and one reaction wheel, a magnetorquer-only 1U, and a 6U with three reaction wheels and thrusters. These demonstrate actuator and sensor failures, full- and reduced-attitude goals, and momentum management. HIL testing on a Raspberry Pi uses the same package. Adapting a published control law to a new actuator configuration requires fewer than five lines of configuration changes. The framework underpins flight software for an Earth-observing CubeSat with visible and long-wave infrared imagers, three magnetorquers, and one reaction wheel, without star trackers or propulsion.

candidates.title: Artificially influential: examining the impact of virtual influencers on non-followers’ behavior
candidates.abstract: Purpose This study aims to address the limited understanding of how unfamiliar non-followers respond to virtual versus human influencers encountered through algorithmically curated feeds. This study tests whether disclosure that a seemingly human influencer is AI-generated lowers perceived authenticity, producing negative expectation disconfirmation that reduces engagement and purchase intentions. Design/methodology/approach Two between-subjects online experiments with US non-followers (n = 303 and n = 316) were conducted through CloudResearch Connect. Measurement validity was assessed using confirmatory factor analysis in SmartPLS 4, and hypotheses were tested using PROCESS serial mediation analyses with bootstrapping. Findings Across both studies, virtual influencer disclosure significantly lowered perceived authenticity, which generated more negative expectation disconfirmation and reduced engagement intentions. In Study 2, this serial process extended to lower purchase intentions. The hypothesized serial indirect effects were significant. Practical implications Brands using human-presenting virtual influencers with unfamiliar audiences should treat disclosure as expectation management by clearly identifying the influencer as AI-generated or virtual from initial exposure. Managers should also recognize that disclosure may lower perceived authenticity, engagement and purchase intentions. Originality/value This study examines an underexplored stage of virtual influencer exposure involving unfamiliar non-followers. This study broadens the expectation–performance comparison process of expectation disconfirmation theory by showing that, during initial encounters, the comparison standard can derive from category-based expectations formed without prior experience with the focal influencer. Perceived authenticity serves as the evaluative mechanism linking newly revealed information to disconfirmation.

candidates.title: Cognitive Multi-Agent Search and Rescue: Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Robotics
candidates.abstract: Effective search and rescue (SAR) operations require autonomous systems capable of coordinating multiple heterogeneous agents, adapting to dynamic hazards, and aligning with human mission intent. Existing language-guided reinforcement learning (RL) methods primarily focus on single-agent instruction following and lack mechanisms for team-level coordination in complex, partially observable environments. This paper presents a Cognitive Multi-Agent Framework based on Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (LG-HRL) that integrates natural-language understanding, hierarchical policy decomposition, and a shared cognitive workspace to achieve cohesive multi-agent behavior in SAR scenarios. Human instructions are interpreted by a large language model (LLM) and transformed into structured semantic cues that guide high-level strategy selection and role assignment across UAV and UGV agents. A formal Language-Grounded Multi-Agent Hierarchical Decision Process (LG-MAHDP) is introduced to model the interplay between semantic grounding, hierarchical control, and distributed coordination. Comprehensive experiments in a simulated disaster environment show that LG-HRL improves learning speed by 2.3×, increases coordination coherence by 37%, and enhances subgoal accuracy and hazard avoidance by 46% and 31%, respectively. The system achieves 20–30% higher victim rescue rates, demonstrates emergent role specialization, and adapts immediately to human verbal updates. Ablation studies confirm that both the shared cognitive workspace and language grounding are critical to overall system performance. Overall, this work establishes a new paradigm for language-guided multi-agent SAR robotics, demonstrating that semantic grounding combined with hierarchical reasoning enables safer, more efficient, and more interpretable autonomous rescue operations.

candidates.title: The PLA’s Push for Military Robotics
candidates.abstract: Drawing on over 2,000 open-source procurement documents published between October 2022 and December 2025, this report examines how the People’s Liberation Army is pursuing robotics across the ground, maritime, and space domains. These include quadruped renaissance robots and ordnance disposal systems, as well as undersea platforms and satellite manipulation devices. The data reveals a military experimenting with still maturing, mostly human-controlled systems. Sensors, navigation, and software will likely matter as much as hardware for Beijing’s military robotics ambitions.

candidates.title: ClickSight: An LLM Framework for Interpreting Student Clickstreams Through Learning Strategies
candidates.abstract: Digital learning environments produce rich clickstream data that can reveal how students approach learning tasks, yet interpreting these fine-grained traces often requires substantial expert effort. We introduce ClickSight, a framework for interpreting student clickstreams through learning strategies defined in the literature. Given a student clickstream and a predefined set of learning strategies, ClickSight uses a staged LLM-based pipeline to identify strategy-relevant evidence, assess adherence to each strategy, and generate an evidence-grounded interpretation of the student's behavior. We evaluate ClickSight across two learning environments, 365 students, and 12 model backbones using an expert-grounded quality rubric and an LLM judge calibrated with human-expert ratings. Our results show that ClickSight can generate high-quality strategy-based interpretations across different models and environments, with reasoning models performing more consistently than instruction-tuned counterparts. We further find that providing external clickstream-extracted guidance can improve interpretation quality for strategies that require precise quantitative information from the trace. By connecting fine-grained clickstreams with theoretically defined learning strategies and preserving the evidence underlying each judgment, ClickSight provides a flexible approach for studying student behavior in digital learning environments.

candidates.title: E6R-1: 3D-printed 6-DOF robotic arm
candidates.abstract: Open-source 6-degree-of-freedom robotic arm for teaching kinematics, trajectory planning and control. Includes 3D-printable STL parts, ESP32 + PCA9685 firmware, MATLAB/Simulink models (forward and inverse kinematics with the product-of-exponentials formulation, a digital twin and hardware-in-the-loop control), a MATLAB App Designer GUI and a URDF description.

candidates.title: OptimalDrive: Modular drive-by-wire retrofit kit
candidates.abstract: We developed a modular drive-by-wire retrofit kit in order to enable remote control, semi-autonomous or fully autonomous operation in virtually any vehicle with an automatic gearbox. The retrofit kit is designed to enhance development of autonomous driving and advanced driver assistance systems capabilities by providing an adaptable drive-by-wire solution suitable for both educational and professional applications. The kit is released as open source with the aim to bridge the gap between simulation and real-world autonomous driving validation. A Python backend and web frontend complement the hardware, allowing convenient calibration, control, and monitoring via a standard web browser or WebSocket-capable software. This hardware does not have a direct commercial analog, promoting accessibility and customization in research settings. By utilizing Docker containers, the software ensures compatibility across various computer systems, and the backend is structured into functional subsystems for efficient handling of control requests and actuator management. The kit is beneficial for both autonomous driving studies as well as other innovative robotic mobility applications and is supported by a comprehensive repository of design files to facilitate reproduction and adaptation.

candidates.title: A Compute Center Anyone Can Join: A Peer-to-Peer System for AI Inference
candidates.abstract: Today, most people obtain AI inference by buying it from a small number of organizations that run large data centers, while many GPUs owned by individuals and small institutions sit idle for much of the day. Bitcoin showed that strangers can contribute resources under shared rules and receive checkable rewards, but it relies on an asymmetry: proof-of-work is expensive to produce and cheap to verify. Useful inference has no such asymmetry. We propose the Open Inference Market (OIM), which replaces the missing asymmetry with an economic mechanism. A worker delivers a result without knowing whether it will be audited; its unsettled earnings serve as collateral during a challenge window; and confirmed cheating forfeits all of it. We call this principle earnings as collateral. In a simplified model we show three things. The number of audits needed for deterrence is a constant per worker per day, independent of the worker's throughput, so the audited share falls as the network gets busier. A new worker can join with a short period of intensive auditing and a very small bond. And whether the mechanism works at all depends only on the ratio of the audit judge's false-flag rate to its detection rate. Under example parameters, about 0.3 replays per worker per day are enough to make cheating unprofitable for a rational worker. On this basis we lay out a path that hands four powers back to participants one at a time: owning compute, writing history, judging work, and releasing value. A compute center need not be a building; it can be a protocol that anyone can join.

candidates.title: Executive Digital Background and Its Impact on Corporate Carbon Performance: A Multi‐Channel Study Based on Internal and External Perspectives
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT In the context of “dual‐carbon” goals, improving corporate carbon performance contributes to carbon reduction. Based on resource theory and upper echelons theory, this paper uses A‐share listed companies in Shanghai and Shenzhen from 2011 to 2023. It constructs an “internal‐external” dual‐channel mechanism framework, and employs OLS regression and fixed effects regression to examine the impact and mechanisms of executives’ digital background on corporate carbon performance. The study finds that executives with a digital background can improve corporate carbon performance. This promotion effect is realized through the improvement of internal operations and external environments, namely through multi‐channel internal and external pathways. The internal channels include enhancing profitability, green innovation, and internal management, while external channels involve improving capital infusion and market supervision. This internal‐external mechanism interaction forms a powerful self‐enhancing system. To expand the applicability of conclusions, cross‐sectional analysis is conducted from the firm, industry, and executive perspectives. From the enterprise level, the study finds that the promotion effect is significant in firms with high value, a low proportion of fixed assets, and good financial conditions. From the industry level, the positive effect is significant in high‐tech industries, non‐heavy pollution industries, and technology‐intensive industries. At the executive level, the promoting effect is significant when the firm has executives with academic backgrounds and political affiliations, lacks executives with overseas backgrounds. Furthermore, economic consequence analysis reveals that executives’ digital background also promotes corporate green transformation, reduces managerial myopia, and strengthens external positive influence. This paper not only contributes to internal optimization within enterprises but also reshapes communication between enterprises and external capital markets, transforming carbon management into an important strategic asset, offering crucial insights for promoting sustainable development.

candidates.title: Programmable Robotic Process Automation Modelling of Software Process
candidates.abstract: In Software engineering certain functions in the back-end can be performed by software robotic process.These activities are often triggered by humans from a user interface or via an API such as placing a trade in exchange trading, extracting data, filling out forms, moving files and so on.Robotic Process Automation, use automation technology to replicate these human functions integrating and performing repetitive operations between enterprise and productivity applications.In this paper an extensive review of how a software or programmable model can be built to handle these operations and looking at existing models and challenges in them that can be improved upon.It explores how a software bot combines a combination of automation, computer vision, and machine learning to automate rule-based and trigger-driven repetitive, high-volume tasks.How programmable software systems can deploy scripts that mimic human processes are also evaluated.It will examine how these automation process employs rulebased software to carry out high-volume business process activities, freeing up human resources to focus on more complicated work.It also reviews how software engineering special tools can be used for planning, engineering, designing and reuse of the Robotic Process Automation applications or software systems.

candidates.title: InstructMesh: Selective Refinement of Generative 3D Models for Fabrication
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in generative AI allow users to create 3D models from text or images. However, these models prioritize visual plausibility over geometric accuracy, often generating results with flaws that compromise their intended use post-fabrication. We present InstructMesh, an interactive post-generation refinement tool that enables selective repair of generative 3D models through region selection and targeted operations, such as opening or sealing voids, or adjusting local thickness. Users can invoke edit operations via natural language prompts or slider controls. By operating directly on the intermediate latent representation, InstructMesh allows users to apply robust geometric corrections without requiring expert modeling skills. To inform our design, we first analyze common fabrication-related failure modes in outputs from state-of-the-art generative tools. We then conduct two user studies, demonstrating that novices can identify and perform fabrication-relevant repairs on generative outputs using InstructMesh, and revealing user preference for hybrid interfaces that combine slider controls with natural language input.

candidates.title: Affordable open-source system for measuring sprint-test times
candidates.abstract: Introduction: Ultrasonic sensors integrated with open-source microcontrollers may represent a promising lowcost alternative for sprint assessment. However, evidence regarding their validity and reliability remains limited. Objective: The objective of this methodological study was to develop and valuate the validity and test-retest reliability of a low-cost sprint-timing system based on ultrasonic sensors and an open-source electronic prototyping platform incorporating open hardware and software. Methods: Ten physically active men (22.0 ± 2.6 years) participated in the study. Each participant completed two experimental sessions, with three maximal flying 30-m sprints performed per session. To assess concurrent validity, sprint times recorded by the prototype were compared with measurements obtained through video analysis using Kinovea software. The developed system consisted of two sensors. Each sensor included an HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor to detect the runner's passage, an nRF24L01 wireless communication module to enable communication between the sensors, an Arduino Uno microcontroller responsible for executing commands programmed in C++, and, for Sensor 2, a 9-V battery to power the system. Test-retest reliability was evaluated by comparing the measurements recorded across the two experimental sessions. Results: The results demonstrated excellent agreement (ICC = 0.96), associated with low measurement errors. Bland–Altman analysis showed that most observations fell within the limits of agreement (bias ± 1.96 SD), and the bias was close to zero (0.08 s). In the test–retest analysis, reliability was high (ICC = 0.81), with low typical error. Bland–Altman analysis showed a small bias between the test and retest measurements (0.08 s). Conclusion: It is concluded that the developed system represents an accessible alternative for real-time sprint time assessment, demonstrating satisfactory validity and reliability for 30-m sprint tests.

candidates.title: Perceived Anthropomorphism and Learner Agency in Self‐Directed Use of GenAI for Informal Language Learning: A Metaphor Study
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT GenAI has the potential to empower self‐directed informal language learning. Yet, given its mixed blessings for learner agency, understanding factors that shape agency enactment in actualizing this potential is essential. Perceived anthropomorphism is central to learner agency with GenAI, as the extent to which learners anthropomorphize GenAI may frame relationships of engagement. This study explored the relationship of perceived anthropomorphism with learner agency by complementing a survey study with 397 Chinese undergraduate English language learners with an interview study with 22 participants. MANCOVA analysis revealed that anthropomorphic perception was a significant predictor of learning proxy agency and spatial agency. Interview responses further revealed that anthropomorphic perceptions are situation‐specific and varied in nuanced ways according to how learners perceived their power relations with GenAI and the symbolic resources they attributed to it, potentially contributing to divergent trajectories of learner agency with GenAI. Moreover, perceived anthropomorphism was intertwined with an array of individual, socio‐educational, and socio‐technical factors in shaping agency enactment. The findings advocate metaphor interventions to expand learner agency with GenAI for self‐directed informal language learning, underscoring a differentiated but integrative approach to cater support on different agency dimensions.

candidates.title: On Queering Sex Robots, Academic Integrity and why Queering is not a Priority Claim. A Response to “Who Queered the Sex Robot.”
candidates.abstract: Abstract In this commentary, we respond to Oliver Bendel’s commentary “Who Queered the Sex Robot? Notes on Attribution and Conceptual History” (2026) on our article “Queering Sex Robots Beyond Diversifying Design? Insights from Queer Lacanian Psychoanalysis and New Materialism” (2026a). We first offer a brief overview of the critique the commentary presents on our article. Following, we respond with two key points: (1) the originality of our argument and remarks on the genealogy of queering sex robots and (2) the (feminist/queer) ethics and politics of citational practices.

candidates.title: Development trends and experience in the application of ground robotic complexes during the Russian-Ukrainian war
candidates.abstract: The prerequisites for the emergence, development trends, and combat employment experience of domestic ground robotic systems in the context of the Russian-Ukrainian war are examined. It is established that the development of ground robotics is driven by the transformation of modern warfare, the development of the domestic defense industry, the need to provide an asymmetric response to the adversary, and the preservation of personnel lives. Approaches to the classification of ground robotic systems are summarized, the specifics of their employment in combat and special tasks are analyzed, and the problems of their integration into the military command and control system are identified. It is substantiated that further development of the ground robotic component involves increasing platform autonomy, implementing artificial intelligence, and integrating robotic systems with unmanned aerial systems, reconnaissance and command-and-control assets into a unified unmanned combat operations framework.

candidates.title: Design and Validation of a Robotic Knee Exoskeleton with Musculoskeletal Simulation-Derived Biological Torque Control
candidates.abstract: Data-driven controllers have enabled lower-limb robotic exoskeletons to adapt assistance to the user across many tasks. A leading example is biological torque control, which estimates the user's own joint moment from onboard sensors and assists in proportion to that estimate. However, its estimators are trained on data recorded with the target device, so deploying the controller on new hardware requires collecting new data. Existing open-source efforts release hardware, software, or controllers separately, so this data collection must still be repeated on the assembled device. Here, we present an open-source knee exoskeleton, built from off-the-shelf components and widely available fabrication tools, with a biological torque controller derived entirely from simulation. A muscle-driven imitation policy reproduces squatting motions from an open biomechanics dataset, and the resulting knee moments are distilled into an estimator that uses only onboard sensors, so no training data are recorded on the device. In seven able-bodied participants, assistance reduced peak biological knee extension moment by 21.5% and peak vastus medialis activation by 26.7% during squatting, relative to squatting without the exoskeleton (p<0.05). Our results demonstrate that a biological torque controller derived from simulation can transfer to physical hardware without device-specific data collection. Because the hardware and training pipeline are released together, research groups can train and compare knee exoskeleton controllers on shared hardware without additional data collection overhead.

candidates.title: Environmentally Symbiotic Plant Robot
candidates.abstract: The increasing deployment of robots in natural environments exacerbates the risk of environmental damage, while realizing eco‐friendly and sustainable autonomous systems remains challenging. Here, an unprecedented robotic framework is presented: an environmentally symbiotic robot that externalizes its drive system to plants and soil, achieving locomotion through a closed cycle of seeding, germination, growth, and reseeding. The robot employs a modular wheel architecture that sows seeds onto the soil and converts the forces generated during plant germination and growth into rotational motion that triggers subsequent seeding. To validate this concept, a kinematic model linking plant growth to robot locomotion is developed, and the feasible design space is analyzed using the growth and mechanical characteristics of radish sprouts ( Raphanus sativus ). Based on this analysis, a 70 mm‐diameter physical robot is fabricated. The measured locomotion agrees well with the model predictions, and the robot autonomously travels a cumulative distance of 240 ± 20 mm on soil over 30 days using only the sown plants and the surrounding environment. These results demonstrate the feasibility of externalizing robotic drive systems to the environment by harnessing plants and environmental resources.

candidates.title: Characterizing the extrusion bioprinting process and microalgal photosynthetic efficiency in bioprinted constructs during parabolic flights
candidates.abstract: Extrusion-based bioprinting is a promising technology for in-space biofabrication, yet peer-reviewed process data derived in real microgravity remain rare. In the presented study, we used parabolic flights as a platform to characterize extrusion-based bioprinting of an alginate-methylcellulose bioink in short-term microgravity. Layer-by-layer printing was performed successfully at different layer distances (260-610 µm), and unsupported filament bridges of up to 13 cm were successfully printed under microgravity. We performed what is, to our knowledge, the first "green" bioprinting of microalgae-laden hydrogels under microgravity, with the cell viability of the thereby created samples exceeding 99% for Scenedesmus sp. and reaching 97% for Chlorella vulgaris on day 7 post-printing. Real-time pulse-amplitude modulated (PAM) fluorometry showed that the effective quantum yield of photosystem II remained stable across all gravitational phases in both liquid cultures and bioprinted samples while maintaining species-specific differences in non-photochemical quenching between the two species. The results of the study indicate that extrusion-based green bioprinting is functionally achievable under short-term microgravity conditions and that cultivation of the thereby created photosynthetically active structures is possible without loss of photosynthetic performance.

candidates.title: Liquid-metal physical unclonable functions resistant to both physical and digital cloning
candidates.abstract: Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) leverage device-specific randomness for hardware security, yet their static, persistently accessible responses allow attackers to collect sufficient data for digital cloning. We present a liquid-metal PUF (LM-PUF) that integrates physical unclonability with material-driven resistance to digital attacks. Randomly mixed, visually indistinguishable LM particles form thermally unique microstructures, ensuring physical unclonability. Digital protection arises from two concealment mechanisms: time-limited accessibility restricts meaningful data collection, while decoy obscuration prevents reliable key identification. At equilibrium, the device remains cryptographically silent, but heating through a transient non-equilibrium window reveals thermal patterns convertible to cryptographic keys. Outside the predefined temperature range, misleading thermal patterns conceal the authentic key among decoys. LM-PUF supports scalable patterning, demonstrated in secure labels and QR codes, highlighting its potential for secure supply chains and physical unclonable authentication. Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) secure hardware identity but can be digitally cloned by machine-learning attacks. Here, authors report a liquid-metal PUF whose thermal keys appear only briefly during heating and are hidden among decoys, resisting both physical and digital cloning.
